sec02-card-f01.front: What three stages make up Montana graduated driver licensing for teens under eighteen?
sec02-card-f01.expected_back: Montana’s graduated licensing program gives new drivers under eighteen an instruction permit, then a first-year restricted license, then full driving privileges.

sec02-card-f02.front: How many total and nighttime practice hours over what minimum period must teen permit holders complete?
sec02-card-f02.memory_hook: Fifty hours ten night six months
sec02-card-f02.expected_back: Before moving beyond the supervised permit stage, teen drivers must practice for at least fifty hours, including ten at night, over at least six months.

sec02-card-f03.front: Who may supervise a learner-permit driver under Montana graduated licensing?
sec02-card-f03.expected_back: Under the graduated program, a learner-permit driver must be supervised by a licensed parent, guardian or responsible adult, or a licensed adult authorized by one of them.

sec02-card-f04.front: Who must wear a seatbelt when riding with a graduated-program instruction-permit driver?
sec02-card-f04.expected_back: Everyone riding with a graduated-program instruction-permit driver must wear a seatbelt.

sec02-card-f05.front: What six-month driving and substance record is required to advance to a restricted license?
sec02-card-f05.expected_back: To advance to the restricted-license stage, a teen must have no traffic violations or alcohol-or-drug offenses during the preceding six months.

sec02-card-f06.front: Which driver-license test must a teen pass as a learner-permit prerequisite?
sec02-card-f06.expected_back: A teen’s learner-permit prerequisites include passing the required driver-license written test.

sec02-card-f07.front: What must a teen applying for a Montana learner permit do with other driver licenses?
sec02-card-f07.expected_back: A teen seeking a learner permit must turn in any other driver licenses.

sec02-card-f08.front: What health prerequisite applies to a teen seeking a Montana learner permit?
sec02-card-f08.expected_back: A teen learner-permit applicant must meet the medical requirements for the requested license type.

sec02-card-f09.front: Which court findings bar a teen applicant from getting a Montana learner permit?
sec02-card-f09.expected_back: A teen learner-permit applicant must not have a court finding of mental incompetence, alcoholism or habitual illegal-drug use.

sec02-card-f10.front: Under what course condition can a teen get a learner permit at fourteen and a half?
sec02-card-f10.expected_back: A teen may obtain a learner permit as early as age fourteen and a half only while participating in, or after successfully completing, a state-approved traffic education program.

sec02-card-f11.front: Does online traffic education count as an approved course for Montana teen learner-permit routes?
sec02-card-f11.expected_back: Online traffic education does not satisfy the approved-course requirement for the teen learner-permit paths.

sec02-card-f12.front: At what ages can a teen obtain an exam-station learner permit with versus without approved traffic education?
sec02-card-f12.expected_back: An exam-station learner permit is available at sixteen without traffic education, or at fifteen after successful completion of a state-approved traffic education program.

sec02-card-f13.front: How long must a teen under eighteen hold a learner permit before seeking a restricted license?
sec02-card-f13.expected_back: A teenager under eighteen must hold a learner permit for at least six consecutive months before applying for the first-year restricted license.

sec02-card-f14.front: How long is a Montana teen learner license valid?
sec02-card-f14.expected_back: The teen learner license is valid for up to one year.

sec02-card-f15.front: Which signed certification form must accompany fees and stage-one completion when applying for a restricted license?
sec02-card-f15.expected_back: The exam-station application for a restricted license requires first-stage completion, fees and required paperwork, including a completed form titled Graduated Driver Licensing Parent slash Legal Guardian slash Responsible Adult Certification.

sec02-card-f16.front: Where does a Montana first-year restricted license display its restriction code?
sec02-card-f16.expected_back: The first-year restricted license displays a restriction code on its front and back.

sec02-card-f17.front: Who must wear a seatbelt whenever a teen drives on a first-year restricted license?
sec02-card-f17.expected_back: Everyone in the vehicle must wear a seatbelt when the teen drives on a first-year restricted license.

sec02-card-f18.front: Between what nighttime hours is a restricted-license teenager barred from driving without an authorized exception?
sec02-card-f18.expected_back: A restricted-license teenager must not drive from eleven p.m. to five a.m. except for the limited authorized purposes described in the graduated-licensing rules.

sec02-card-f19.front: Which trips qualify as nighttime curfew exceptions for a restricted-license teen?
sec02-card-f19.expected_back: The restricted-license night-driving exceptions include emergencies, farm activities, school, church or work travel, and specific purposes authorized by a parent, guardian or responsible adult.

sec02-card-f20.front: How may law enforcement verify a restricted-license teen reason for driving during curfew hours?
sec02-card-f20.expected_back: Officers may contact the teen’s parent, guardian or responsible adult to check the purpose of driving during restricted nighttime hours.

sec02-card-f21.front: How many unrelated passengers under eighteen may ride during the first six restricted months without adult supervision?
sec02-card-f21.expected_back: During the first six months of the restricted license, a teen may carry only one unrelated passenger under eighteen unless a licensed adult driver supervises.

sec02-card-f22.front: How many unrelated passengers under eighteen may ride during the second six restricted months without adult supervision?
sec02-card-f22.expected_back: During the second six months of the restricted license, a teen may carry three unrelated passengers under eighteen unless supervised by a licensed adult driver.

sec02-card-f23.front: What penalty applies the first time a teen breaks a first-year license restriction?
sec02-card-f23.expected_back: A first violation of a first-year license restriction carries twenty to sixty hours of community service.

sec02-card-f24.front: What happens after a second violation of a first-year license restriction?
sec02-card-f24.expected_back: A second first-year license restriction violation results in a six-month license suspension.

sec02-card-f25.front: When do Montana first-year graduated license restrictions end automatically?
sec02-card-f25.expected_back: First-year license restrictions end automatically on the date shown on the license back or at age eighteen, whichever happens sooner.

sec02-card-f26.front: How long does a driver-license receipt last, and how many exam attempts does it allow?
sec02-card-f26.expected_back: A driver-license receipt lasts one year and gives a testing applicant three examination attempts within that period.

sec02-card-f27.front: Can a Montana driver-license testing receipt be renewed?

sec02-card-f28.front: What happens if an applicant has not finished licensing after one year on a receipt?
sec02-card-f28.expected_back: If licensing is unfinished after one year, the applicant must apply again and restart the process.

sec02-card-r01.front: How far ahead of expiration may a Montana driver start license renewal?
sec02-card-r01.expected_back: A driver may begin renewal up to six months before the license expiration date.

sec02-card-r02.front: May you legally drive on an expired license during the window when renewal without retesting remains open?
sec02-card-r02.expected_back: An expired license gives no authority to drive, even during the period when renewal without retesting may still be available.

sec02-card-r03.front: Within how long after expiration can a Montana license be renewed without retesting?
sec02-card-r03.expected_back: Renewal without retesting may be completed within one year after expiration.

sec02-card-r04.front: What is required once a Montana license has been expired for more than one year?
sec02-card-r04.expected_back: A license expired for more than one year requires a new-driver application with acceptable identity, residence and authorized-presence proof and all applicable licensing tests.

sec02-card-r05.front: Which federal records must match the full legal name and birth date on a license or ID application?
sec02-card-r05.expected_back: The full legal name and birth date used on a license or identification-card application must match Social Security Administration records.

sec02-card-r06.front: Which five items make up the standard Montana exam-station license renewal procedure?
sec02-card-r06.expected_back: The handbook’s renewal procedure requires proper identification, the fee, an exam-station appearance, a vision test and a new photo.

sec02-card-r07.front: What extra exams can apply at renewal when safe-driving functional ability is in doubt?
sec02-card-r07.expected_back: Renewal applicants whose functional ability to drive safely is in doubt may also need written and road tests.

sec02-card-r08.front: How does a suspension or revocation in Montana or elsewhere affect applying for or keeping a license?
sec02-card-r08.expected_back: A suspension or revocation in Montana or another jurisdiction prevents applying for, receiving or retaining a Montana driver license.

sec02-card-r09.front: What is required at a local licensing station to replace a lost or destroyed Montana license?
sec02-card-r09.expected_back: A lost or destroyed license can be replaced at a local licensing station with proper identity evidence verifying full legal name and birth date and the required fee.

sec02-card-r10.front: Whom must a Montana driver notify after moving, and within how many days?
sec02-card-r10.expected_back: A driver must notify the Department of Justice Driver Services Bureau within ten days after an address change.

sec02-card-r11.front: What two steps are required to change the legal name on a Montana driver license?
sec02-card-r11.expected_back: To change the legal name on a license, an applicant must complete the appropriate application and submit an accepted legal name-change document.

sec02-card-r12.front: Which marriage record qualifies to change the legal name on a Montana license?
sec02-card-r12.expected_back: An issuing government jurisdiction’s certified marriage certificate is an accepted license name-change document.

sec02-card-r13.front: Which general court record qualifies to update the name on a Montana license?
sec02-card-r13.expected_back: A certified competent-court decree or judgment granting a name change is accepted for a license name change.

sec02-card-r14.front: When does a certified divorce or dissolution decree qualify as a license name-change document?
sec02-card-r14.expected_back: A certified divorce or marriage-dissolution decree qualifies for a license name change only if it specifies the requested name change.

sec02-card-r15.front: Which certified USCIS naturalization form numbers qualify as Montana license name-change documents?
sec02-card-r15.memory_hook: Certified N five fifty or seventy
sec02-card-r15.expected_back: A certified DHS USCIS naturalization certificate on form N-five hundred fifty or N-five hundred seventy issued to the applicant qualifies as a license name-change document.

sec02-card-r16.front: Which agency records must match the name and birth date used for a Montana license name change?
sec02-card-r16.expected_back: The name and birth date used for a license name change must match the Social Security Administration’s records.

sec03-card-f01.front: What personal readiness check should you make before starting any drive?
sec03-card-f01.expected_back: Before driving, decide whether you are physically and mentally able to drive safely.

sec03-card-f02.front: Who bears legal responsibility for making sure a vehicle is safe to operate?
sec03-card-f02.expected_back: A driver is responsible for making sure the vehicle is safe to operate.

sec03-card-f03.front: What guide governs routine vehicle care, and who should handle repairs beyond your skill?
sec03-card-f03.expected_back: Routine vehicle maintenance should follow the owner’s manual, with work beyond the driver’s ability handled by a qualified mechanic.

sec03-card-f04.front: What action is called for by brake noise, a strange brake odor, or a pedal sinking to the floor?
sec03-card-f04.expected_back: Brake noise, an unusual brake smell or a brake pedal reaching the floor calls for a mechanic’s inspection.

sec03-card-f05.front: From where should you verify turn signals, brake lamps, taillamps, and headlights?
sec03-card-f05.expected_back: Check turn signals, brake lamps, taillamps and headlights from outside the vehicle to confirm that they work.

sec03-card-f06.front: What message do your brake lamps send to drivers behind you?
sec03-card-f06.expected_back: Brake lamps communicate that the vehicle is stopping.

sec03-card-f07.front: What driving intention do your turn signals communicate to surrounding road users?
sec03-card-f07.expected_back: Turn signals communicate an intended turn.

sec03-card-f08.front: Why should drivers run headlights in daylight as well as darkness?
sec03-card-f08.expected_back: Using headlights during both daylight and darkness helps other drivers see the vehicle.

sec03-card-f09.front: What should a mechanic inspect if night vision feels poor or oncoming drivers keep flashing high beams at you?
sec03-card-f09.expected_back: Have a mechanic check headlight alignment if seeing at night is difficult or other drivers frequently flash their headlights at you.

sec03-card-f10.front: Which three planning habits help cut down total driving miles?
sec03-card-f10.expected_back: Trip planning can reduce driving by combining errands, sharing rides or using available public transportation.

sec03-card-f11.front: What benefit comes from routing or timing trips to avoid heavy traffic?
sec03-card-f11.expected_back: Avoiding heavy traffic reduces wear on the driver and vehicle.

sec03-card-f12.front: What quick step prevents wasted pickup trips before heading out?
sec03-card-f12.expected_back: Before a pickup trip, call to confirm the needed item is available or ready.

sec03-card-f13.front: For what two safety reasons should damaged windshield glass be replaced?
sec03-card-f13.expected_back: Replace damaged windshield glass because it can obstruct sight and break more easily in a minor collision or impact.

sec03-card-f14.front: When should windshield wiper blades be replaced?
sec03-card-f14.expected_back: Replace ineffective wiper blades so the windshield can be cleared of rain and snow.

sec03-card-f15.front: How much glass must you clear of snow and ice before driving?
sec03-card-f15.expected_back: Remove snow and ice from every window before driving.

sec03-card-f16.front: How do worn or bald tires change stopping and turning on wet pavement?
sec03-card-f16.expected_back: Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distance and make turning harder on wet roads.

sec03-card-f17.front: What four problems come from low tire pressure or unbalanced wheels?
sec03-card-f17.expected_back: Low tire pressure or unbalanced tires can increase wear and fuel use while making steering and stopping harder.

sec03-card-f18.front: What does bouncing, steering-wheel vibration, or pulling to one side call for?
sec03-card-f18.expected_back: Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side warrants a mechanic’s check.

sec03-card-f19.front: Which two major highway hazards become likelier with worn tires?
sec03-card-f19.expected_back: Worn tires can cause hydroplaning and increase the likelihood of a blowout.

sec03-card-f20.front: When should you measure tire pressure with a gauge, and where is the target pressure listed?
sec03-card-f20.expected_back: Use a gauge to check pressure while the tires are cold, using the owner’s manual to find the recommended pressure.

sec03-card-f21.front: How do you run the penny tread check, and what result means replacing the tire?
sec03-card-f21.expected_back: For the penny tread check, insert Lincoln’s head first; if the tread does not reach at least his head, replace the unsafe tire.

sec03-card-f22.front: What should you do if steering feels stiff or lags when the wheel first turns?
sec03-card-f22.expected_back: Have a mechanic inspect steering that is hard to turn or does not respond when the steering wheel first turns.

sec03-card-f23.front: Which system needs a mechanic inspection if the vehicle keeps bouncing after a bump or stop?
sec03-card-f23.expected_back: Excessive bouncing or continued bouncing after a bump or stop is a reason for a mechanic to inspect the suspension.

sec03-card-f24.front: What three jobs does a vehicle exhaust system perform?
sec03-card-f24.expected_back: The exhaust system removes engine gases, reduces engine noise and cools the hot exhaust.

sec03-card-f25.front: What two dangers make leaking exhaust fumes an urgent cabin threat?
sec03-card-f25.expected_back: Leaking exhaust fumes can quickly be fatal and can make a driver drowsy.

sec03-card-f26.front: What rule applies to running a vehicle engine inside a garage?
sec03-card-f26.expected_back: Do not run a vehicle’s engine inside a garage.

sec03-card-f27.front: What window precaution applies when sitting inside a parked car with the engine running?
sec03-card-f27.expected_back: The handbook warns against sitting in a car with its engine running without an open window.

sec03-card-f28.front: When should detected vehicle exhaust leaks be repaired?
sec03-card-f28.expected_back: Have exhaust leaks repaired when they are detected.

sec03-card-f29.front: What three operational problems can an out-of-tune engine cause?
sec03-card-f29.expected_back: A poorly tuned engine may lose needed power, fail to start or stall in traffic.

sec03-card-f30.front: Why must items on the rear shelf or back seat be secured?
sec03-card-f30.expected_back: Secure objects on the rear shelf or back seat that could strike someone during a sudden stop or crash.

sec03-card-f31.front: Why must loose objects stay off the floor near the driver pedals?
sec03-card-f31.expected_back: Keep floor objects from rolling under the brake pedal and preventing braking.

sec03-card-f32.front: For what sole purpose should a vehicle horn be sounded?
sec03-card-f32.expected_back: Use the horn only to warn others.

sec03-card-f33.front: On post-1956 vehicles, what colors and visibility distance apply to required front and rear lighting?
sec03-card-f33.memory_hook: White amber front red amber rear
sec03-card-f33.expected_back: For vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six, the listed front lighting must be white or amber and the rear lighting red or amber, visible from five hundred feet.

sec03-card-f34.front: When is colored covering or tinting forbidden on headlights and taillights?
sec03-card-f34.expected_back: Headlights and taillights must not be tinted or covered with colored material unless compliant original or optional equipment meets federal manufacturing regulations.

sec03-card-f35.front: At what minimum distance ahead should high-beam headlights reveal people or vehicles?
sec03-card-f35.expected_back: High-beam headlights should reveal people or vehicles at three hundred fifty feet.

sec03-card-f36.front: At what minimum distance ahead should low-beam headlights reveal people or vehicles?
sec03-card-f36.expected_back: Low-beam headlights should reveal people or vehicles at one hundred feet.

sec03-card-f37.front: At what distance from an approaching oncoming vehicle must you dim high-beam headlights?
sec03-card-f37.expected_back: Dim high beams when an approaching vehicle is one thousand feet away.

sec03-card-f38.front: At what distance behind a vehicle you are overtaking must you dim high beams?
sec03-card-f38.expected_back: When overtaking another vehicle, dim high beams at five hundred feet.

sec03-card-f39.front: Between what sunset and sunrise times must Montana drivers run headlights?
sec03-card-f39.expected_back: Headlights must be used from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.

sec03-card-f40.front: Below what visibility distance in weather or blowing dust are headlights required?
sec03-card-f40.expected_back: Headlights are required when weather or blowing dust reduces visibility below five hundred feet.

sec03-card-f41.front: Which vehicles may legally use flashing or pulsating lights other than turn signals?
sec03-card-f41.expected_back: Flashing or pulsating vehicle lights other than turn signals are prohibited unless the vehicle is authorized or an emergency vehicle.

sec03-card-f42.front: What motions and colors are barred for decorative undercarriage lighting?
sec03-card-f42.expected_back: Decorative undercarriage lights must not rotate, flash, oscillate or use a color reserved for police or emergency vehicles.

sec03-card-f43.front: On post-1956 vehicles, what colors and sunlight visibility distance apply to turn signals?
sec03-card-f43.expected_back: On vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six, turn signals must show white or amber ahead and red or amber behind, visible for three hundred feet in sunlight.

sec03-card-f44.front: Which two steering-post measurements make mechanical or electrical signal lamps mandatory?
sec03-card-f44.memory_hook: Over twenty four inches fourteen feet
sec03-card-f44.expected_back: Signal lamps are required if the steering-post center is more than twenty-four inches from the vehicle’s left edge or more than fourteen feet from the rear edge of the vehicle or load.

sec03-card-f45.front: Which two vehicle actions do brake lamps signal?
sec03-card-f45.expected_back: Brake lamps indicate slowing or stopping.

sec03-card-f46.front: On post-1956 vehicles, what colors and normal-sunlight distance apply to brake lights?
sec03-card-f46.expected_back: For vehicles built after January one, nineteen fifty-six, brake lights must be red or amber and visible from three hundred feet in normal sunlight.

sec03-card-f47.front: What color and rear visibility distance are required for license-plate lighting on post-1956 vehicles?
sec03-card-f47.expected_back: A vehicle made after January one, nineteen fifty-six must have white license-plate illumination visible for fifty feet behind it.

sec03-card-f48.front: How does Montana treat aftermarket rear plate lighting compared with original manufacturer equipment?
sec03-card-f48.expected_back: License-plate lighting that is not original manufacturer equipment is prohibited.

sec03-card-f49.front: What sound condition must every vehicle muffler prevent?
sec03-card-f49.expected_back: The muffler must prevent unusual or excessive noise.

sec03-card-f50.front: How far behind must a mirror show on vehicles manufactured after January 1, 1956?
sec03-card-f50.expected_back: A vehicle manufactured after January one, nineteen fifty-six must provide a rearward mirror view of two hundred feet.

sec03-card-f51.front: What three things must service and parking brakes do across operating loads and grades?
sec03-card-f51.expected_back: The service and parking brakes must control, stop and hold the vehicle for its operating loads and grades.

sec03-card-f52.front: From what minimum distance must a required vehicle horn be audible?
sec03-card-f52.expected_back: The horn must be audible from two hundred feet.

sec03-card-r01.front: What parking-light colors and visibility distance apply when stopped or parked on a roadway during headlamp hours?
sec03-card-r01.expected_back: When headlamps are required, a vehicle stopped or parked on a roadway must show parking lights that are white or amber ahead and red behind, visible for five hundred feet.

sec03-card-r02.front: What front glass is required on motor vehicles, and which ones require safety glass?
sec03-card-r02.memory_hook: Front windshield post fifty six safety
sec03-card-r02.expected_back: Motor vehicles require a front windshield, with safety glass required for those manufactured after January one, nineteen fifty-six.

sec03-card-r03.front: What condition must a motor vehicle windshield always maintain?
sec03-card-r03.expected_back: The windshield must stay in a condition that does not block the driver’s view.

sec03-card-r04.front: When is attaching stickers, posters, or other material to any vehicle window prohibited?
sec03-card-r04.expected_back: Do not attach material to any window if it restricts the driver’s view.

sec03-card-r05.front: What must required windshield wipers be capable of clearing?
sec03-card-r05.expected_back: Working windshield wipers are required to remove rain, snow and other moisture.

sec03-card-r06.front: Which seating positions require belts on vehicles built between January 1, 1965 and January 1, 1968?
sec03-card-r06.expected_back: Vehicles manufactured between January one, nineteen sixty-five and January one, nineteen sixty-eight must have belts for both outer front seats.

sec03-card-r07.front: Which positions require seatbelts on vehicles manufactured after January 1, 1968?
sec03-card-r07.expected_back: Vehicles manufactured after January one, nineteen sixty-eight require seatbelts at every designated seating position.

sec03-card-r08.front: In what mechanical state must required vehicle seatbelts be kept?
sec03-card-r08.expected_back: Seatbelts must be kept in working order.

sec03-card-r09.front: What occupant restraint condition must be met before a driver operates on Montana roads?
sec03-card-r09.expected_back: A driver may not drive in Montana unless each occupant has a properly adjusted and fastened safety belt.

sec03-card-r10.front: How many clearance lamps and where go on buses or trucks over 80 inches wide and heavy wide trailers?
sec03-card-r10.expected_back: For buses and trucks over eighty inches wide, and trailers or semitrailers over three thousand pounds gross vehicle weight and over that width, two clearance lamps are required at the front and two at the rear, one on each side.

sec03-card-r11.front: Where are clearance lamps required on a truck tractor?
sec03-card-r11.expected_back: A truck tractor needs two front clearance lamps, one on each side.

sec03-card-r12.front: Where must clearance lamps be placed on a pole trailer over three thousand pounds gross weight?
sec03-card-r12.expected_back: A pole trailer above three thousand pounds gross vehicle weight needs a clearance lamp on each side.

sec03-card-r13.front: Which four vehicle types are exempt from the post-1956 requirement for two rear taillamps?
sec03-card-r13.expected_back: Vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six need two rear taillamps, except motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, quadricycles and truck tractors.

sec03-card-r14.front: What colors and visibility distance apply to required vehicle clearance lamps?
sec03-card-r14.expected_back: Clearance lamps must be amber at the front or side and red at the rear, and visible for five hundred feet when required.

sec03-card-r15.front: During headlamp hours, what marker belongs on a load extending four feet or more past the rear body?
sec03-card-r15.expected_back: A load projecting at least four feet beyond the vehicle body needs a red lamp at its farthest rear point, visible for five hundred feet, while headlamps are required.

sec03-card-r16.front: When headlamps are not required, what marker belongs on a rear load extending four feet or more?
sec03-card-r16.expected_back: When headlamps are not required, a load extending four feet or more beyond the vehicle body needs a red flag at least twelve inches square.

sec03-card-r17.front: What front and rear lights must a farm tractor or implement show on highways during headlamp hours?
sec03-card-r17.expected_back: A farm tractor or implement of husbandry moving on a highway during required-headlamp hours must show a front white light visible for at least five hundred feet and a rear red light visible for five hundred feet.

sec03-card-r18.front: Which outer edge must required farm-vehicle lighting mark?
sec03-card-r18.expected_back: Required farm-vehicle lights must be mounted to show the vehicle’s farthest left projection.

sec03-card-r19.front: How many combined spot or auxiliary fog lamps may a vehicle carry at most?
sec03-card-r19.expected_back: A vehicle may carry no more than two spot or auxiliary fog lamps.

sec03-card-r20.front: What must you do with spot lamps when approaching another moving vehicle from either direction?
sec03-card-r20.expected_back: Turn spot lamps off when approaching another moving vehicle from either direction.

sec03-card-r21.front: Under what beam-strength limit may fog lamps run alongside low-beam headlights?
sec03-card-r21.expected_back: Fog lamps may accompany low-beam headlights only if the fog-lamp beam is no stronger than the low beam.

sec03-card-r22.front: When do trailers, semitrailers, or pole trailers require separation-activated break-away brakes?
sec03-card-r22.memory_hook: Air vacuum or over three thousand
sec03-card-r22.expected_back: Trailers, semitrailers and pole trailers need separation-activated break-away brakes if they have air or vacuum brakes or weigh more than three thousand pounds gross.

sec03-card-r23.front: How must vehicle brakes be maintained and adjusted across the wheels?
sec03-card-r23.expected_back: Maintain brakes in working order and adjust them to act equally on all wheels.

sec03-card-r24.front: Which vehicles are allowed an exception to the ban on sirens, whistles, and bells?
sec03-card-r24.expected_back: Vehicle sirens, whistles and bells are prohibited except where authorized emergency vehicles are permitted to use them.

sec03-card-r25.front: What front backup connection is required on a trailer weighing three thousand pounds gross or less?
sec03-card-r25.expected_back: A trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer weighing three thousand pounds gross vehicle weight or less needs a securely fastened front steel safety chain or cable at least one-quarter inch in diameter.

sec03-card-r26.front: Which three heavy vehicle types must carry specified roadside warning equipment?
sec03-card-r26.expected_back: A truck with at least one-ton capacity, passenger bus or truck tractor must carry the specified warning equipment.

sec03-card-r27.front: What flame-free kit meeting federal standard 125 can replace older roadside warning sets?
sec03-card-r27.expected_back: Three emergency reflective triangles meeting United States Department of Transportation Motor Vehicles Safety Standard one hundred twenty-five may replace the listed warning-device set.

sec03-card-r28.front: Which warning devices may never be carried on explosive, flammable-liquid, or compressed-gas vehicles?
sec03-card-r28.expected_back: Vehicles carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases, or using compressed gas fuel, must not carry flame-producing warning devices.

sec03-card-r29.front: Where must the very first warning device go immediately when a covered commercial vehicle breaks down during lamp hours?
sec03-card-r29.expected_back: If a truck, passenger bus, tractor, trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer is disabled on a highway or shoulder while lamps are required, place an initial warning device immediately on the traffic side toward approaching traffic.

sec03-card-r30.front: Where do the three warning devices go for a disabled commercial vehicle on an undivided highway during lamp hours?
sec03-card-r30.expected_back: For the listed disabled vehicles on an undivided highway during required-lamp hours, warning devices go one hundred feet behind and one hundred feet ahead in the occupied lane, plus a traffic-side device at least ten feet toward the nearest approaching traffic.

sec03-card-r31.front: How are lane warning devices spaced behind a disabled commercial vehicle on a divided highway during lamp hours?
sec03-card-r31.expected_back: For the listed disabled vehicles on a divided highway during required-lamp hours, use the two hundred-foot rear placement and place the other lane device one hundred feet in the same direction instead of in front.

sec03-card-r32.front: How far out must a warning marker move when a disabled commercial rig sits within 500 feet of a blind curve or crest?
sec03-card-r32.expected_back: When a listed disabled vehicle is within five hundred feet of a curve, hill or other blocked view, put the warning in that direction at least five hundred feet from the vehicle so approaching traffic has adequate warning.

sec03-card-r33.front: What warnings must a covered disabled vehicle display on a roadway outside required lamp hours?
sec03-card-r33.expected_back: When the stated lamp-time warning-device requirement does not apply to a listed disabled vehicle on a roadway, the driver must display two red flags at the specified front and rear positions.

sec03-card-r34.front: Which warning devices and distances apply when an explosive, flammable, or compressed-gas rig is disabled?
sec03-card-r34.expected_back: In the stated highway or shoulder disablement situations, a vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquid or compressed gas, or using compressed gas fuel, needs immediate red electric-lantern or portable-red-reflector warnings on its traffic side and one hundred feet ahead and behind in its occupied lane.

sec03-card-r35.front: Which roadside signals are strictly forbidden around disabled vehicles carrying explosives, flammables, or compressed gas?
sec03-card-r35.expected_back: Do not use flares, fuses or other flame signals to warn of a disabled vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases, or using compressed gas as fuel.

sec03-card-r36.front: What speed threshold requires a rear slow-moving emblem, and which protected work equipment is exempt?
sec03-card-r36.expected_back: A slow-moving vehicle or item of equipment, animal-drawn vehicle, or road-work machine normally operating at twenty-five miles per hour or less needs the rear emblem, except machinery doing actual road work while protected by a flagger or warning signs.

sec03-card-r37.front: What shape, center color, and dimensions define the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
sec03-card-r37.expected_back: The slow-moving emblem is a fluorescent yellow-orange triangle with a fourteen-inch base and fourteen-inch height.

sec03-card-r38.front: What color, material, and width make up the border of a slow-moving emblem?
sec03-card-r38.expected_back: The slow-moving emblem needs reflective red border stripes one and three-quarter inches wide.

sec03-card-r39.front: Where and how high above the road should a slow-moving vehicle emblem be mounted?
sec03-card-r39.expected_back: Mount the slow-moving emblem at the rear center, three to five feet above the road.

sec03-card-r40.front: When must a slow vehicle on a two-lane road pull over to let trailing traffic pass?
sec03-card-r40.expected_back: On a two-lane road, a slow vehicle that leaves no clear passing lane must pull over at the first safe opportunity with sufficient turnout space to let others pass.

sec03-card-r41.front: Why does keeping your windshield clean matter in bright sun or oncoming headlights?
sec03-card-r41.expected_back: Keep the windshield clean because sunlight or headlights on dirty glass can make seeing difficult.

sec03-card-r42.front: What washer-fluid habit applies where temperatures can drop below freezing?
sec03-card-r42.expected_back: Keep washer fluid filled and use antifreeze washer fluid where temperatures may drop below freezing.

sec03-card-r43.front: Why should you wipe interior window surfaces, especially if someone smokes inside?
sec03-card-r43.expected_back: Clean interior window surfaces, especially when smoking has left a film.

sec03-card-r44.front: Which window surfaces need snow, ice, and frost cleared before driving?
sec03-card-r44.expected_back: Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost from the front, side and rear windows.

sec12-card-f01.front: What sensory screening does Montana require before issuing a driver license?
sec12-card-f01.expected_back: Montana requires a vision test before issuing a driver license.

sec12-card-f02.front: What visual acuity standard must you meet in at least one eye, and are corrective lenses allowed?
sec12-card-f02.expected_back: The stated vision standard is at least twenty over forty in one eye or better, with or without corrective lenses.

sec12-card-f03.front: If your license requires corrective lenses, must you wear them on a quick neighborhood errand?
sec12-card-f03.expected_back: Wear required glasses or contact lenses whenever driving, even on a short trip.

sec12-card-f04.front: What legal consequence can hit you for driving without corrective lenses required on your license?
sec12-card-f04.expected_back: Driving without corrective lenses required by the license can result in a citation.

sec12-card-f05.front: Why should drivers who rely on prescription glasses stash an extra pair inside the vehicle?
sec12-card-f05.expected_back: Keep spare glasses in the vehicle in case the usual pair is lost or broken.

sec12-card-f06.front: Why should you never wear sunglasses or tinted contact lenses while driving after dark?
sec12-card-f06.expected_back: Avoid dark glasses or tinted contacts at night because they reduce the light available for seeing.

sec12-card-f07.front: Once peripheral vision flags motion beside you, what else may you need to see that hazard clearly?
sec12-card-f07.expected_back: Side vision helps detect hazards, but mirrors and a sideways glance may still be needed to see them clearly.

sec12-card-f08.front: Which two highway maneuvers especially test your practiced ability to judge vehicle speeds and distances?
sec12-card-f08.expected_back: Judging vehicle speeds and distances takes practice, especially for merging gaps and two-lane passing.

sec12-card-f09.front: How should you adjust your schedule and driving style if seeing clearly after dark becomes difficult?
sec12-card-f09.expected_back: If night vision is difficult, limit nighttime driving to what is necessary and drive cautiously when it is unavoidable.

sec12-card-f10.front: Which three traffic sounds serve as vital audible warnings of nearby road danger?
sec12-card-f10.expected_back: Horns, sirens and screeching tires can give an audible warning of danger.

sec12-card-f11.front: How can a driver with reduced hearing compensate safely behind the wheel?
sec12-card-f11.expected_back: A driver with hearing loss can adapt by relying more on vision and staying alert.

sec12-card-f12.front: How does driver fatigue degrade eyesight, thinking speed, and cabin safety?
sec12-card-f12.expected_back: Fatigue can reduce vision and alertness, slow decisions and make falling asleep at the wheel more likely.

sec12-card-f13.front: In what sleep condition should you start a long highway drive instead of rolling out already tired?
sec12-card-f13.expected_back: Begin a long trip rested after a normal night’s sleep rather than leaving already tired.

sec12-card-f14.front: Why should you choose light snacks over a heavy meal right before starting a trip?
sec12-card-f14.expected_back: Before leaving, eat lightly instead of a large meal that may cause sleepiness.

sec12-card-f15.front: How often should you plan rest stops on a long drive, and what if tiredness hits sooner?
sec12-card-f15.expected_back: On a long trip, stop for a break about every two hours or whenever a break is needed.

sec12-card-f16.front: How should you budget travel time when planning any trip?
sec12-card-f16.expected_back: Allow enough time to complete a trip without rushing.

sec12-card-f17.front: Why should you avoid scheduling road trips late at night during hours you normally sleep?
sec12-card-f17.expected_back: Avoid driving late at night when that is normally your sleeping time.

sec12-card-f18.front: What two safe options replace pushing forward when drowsiness hits mid-trip?
sec12-card-f18.expected_back: Do not drive while sleepy; stop to sleep or share the driving with another driver when possible.

sec12-card-f19.front: Which five core driving abilities does alcohol degrade?
sec12-card-f19.expected_back: Alcohol impairs judgment, reflexes, reaction time, clear vision and alertness needed for driving.

sec12-card-f20.front: Why does Montana advise never driving after drinking, even if you only had one alcoholic beverage?
sec12-card-f20.expected_back: If you drink alcohol, do not drive, because even a single beverage can affect driving.

sec12-card-f21.front: Beyond how much and how fast someone drinks, which three personal factors change alcohol impairment?
sec12-card-f21.expected_back: The amount and pace of drinking, body weight, food and general health can all affect impairment.

sec12-card-f22.front: Does pacing yourself at one drink per hour guarantee alcohol will not build up in your system?
sec12-card-f22.expected_back: Alcohol can accumulate even when someone consumes only one drink per hour.

sec12-card-f23.front: Which serving sizes of eighty-proof liquor, commercial beer, and wine represent standard comparable drinks?
sec12-card-f23.expected_back: The handbook’s drink comparison uses one and one-half ounces of eighty-proof liquor, twelve ounces of commercial beer or five ounces of wine.

sec12-card-f24.front: Why is counting craft beers or mixed specialty cocktails as single standard drinks risky?
sec12-card-f24.expected_back: Craft beer and specialty drinks can contain more alcohol than the standard drink examples.

sec12-card-f25.front: What three sober transportation options should you line up whenever drinking is part of your plans?
sec12-card-f25.expected_back: Arrange for a designated driver who does not drink, or use available public transportation or a cab.

sec12-card-f26.front: What blood alcohol percentage triggers arrest, and can you still be arrested below that number?
sec12-card-f26.expected_back: Driving at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or more, or while under the influence, can lead to arrest.

sec12-card-f27.front: What does BAC measure, and which three chemical sample types usually determine it?
sec12-card-f27.memory_hook: Blood alcohol via breath, blood, urine
sec12-card-f27.expected_back: Blood alcohol concentration describes the proportion of alcohol in blood and is usually assessed by breath, blood or urine testing.

sec12-card-f28.front: What happens to your driver license if you refuse a blood alcohol test requested by police?
sec12-card-f28.expected_back: Refusing a police-requested blood alcohol test can result in loss of the driver license.

sec12-card-f29.front: Where inside a vehicle on a public highway is keeping an unlawful open alcohol container banned?
sec12-card-f29.expected_back: An open alcoholic beverage container must not be unlawfully kept in a vehicle’s highway passenger area.

sec12-card-f30.front: What condition makes a glove box or interior storage compartment legal for stowing an alcohol container?
sec12-card-f30.expected_back: A locked glove compartment or storage compartment is among the listed permitted places for an alcoholic beverage container.

sec12-card-f31.front: Which four cargo or exterior areas are legal places to transport alcoholic beverage containers?
sec12-card-f31.expected_back: The handbook lists a trunk, luggage compartment, truck bed or cargo compartment as permitted container-storage locations.

sec12-card-f32.front: Where can an SUV, hatchback, or van without a trunk legally carry an alcohol container?
sec12-card-f32.expected_back: In a vehicle without a trunk, an alcoholic container may be behind the last upright seat or in a closed container in an area not normally occupied by riders.

sec12-card-f33.front: Which two conditions qualify a bottle for the sealed-container exception?
sec12-card-f33.expected_back: The container restriction has an exception for an unbroken seal with none of the original contents removed.

sec12-card-f34.front: Which section of a camper, travel trailer, or motor home has an open-container storage exception?
sec12-card-f34.expected_back: The listed open-container exceptions include storage in the living quarters of a camper, travel trailer or motor home.

sec12-card-f35.front: Which three hired-driver vehicles allow passengers an exception to the open-container ban?
sec12-card-f35.expected_back: Passengers carried by a hired driver in a bus, taxi or limousine have a listed open-container exception.

sec12-card-f36.front: Whom should you contact to report a suspected drunk driver, and what two details help officers intercept them?
sec12-card-f36.expected_back: To report suspected impaired driving, contact local law enforcement or the highway patrol with the vehicle description and direction of travel.

sec12-card-f37.front: Must you give your own name when calling law enforcement to report a suspected impaired driver?
sec12-card-f37.expected_back: A person reporting suspected drunk driving does not have to provide a name.

sec12-card-r01.front: Can nonprescription pharmacy medicines impair your driving just like prescription drugs?
sec12-card-r01.expected_back: Prescription and nonprescription medicines can impair driving.

sec12-card-r02.front: What should you inspect before taking any medication ahead of a planned drive?
sec12-card-r02.expected_back: Check a medicine’s label for driving-related warnings before taking it when you plan to drive.

sec12-card-r03.front: What does a medication warning against operating heavy machinery mean for everyday drivers?
sec12-card-r03.expected_back: A medicine warning about operating heavy machinery also means not driving a car or truck.

sec12-card-r04.front: Which two health professionals should you ask if you are unsure how a medication affects driving?
sec12-card-r04.expected_back: If unsure about a drug’s driving effects, ask a physician or pharmacist about side effects.

sec12-card-r05.front: Why must you never mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medications?
sec12-card-r05.expected_back: The handbook warns against mixing alcohol with other drugs because the combination can intensify impairment or add harmful side effects.

sec12-card-r06.front: What should you do when an illness makes driving unsafe?
sec12-card-r06.expected_back: When illness makes driving unsafe, have someone else drive.

sec12-card-r07.front: When should you evaluate whether you are physically and mentally fit to operate a vehicle?
sec12-card-r07.expected_back: Before each drive, decide whether you are physically and mentally able to drive safely.

sec12-card-r08.front: What documentation does the Montana handbook call for when an applicant or driver has epilepsy?
sec12-card-r08.expected_back: For epilepsy, the handbook calls for a physician’s written attestation that the condition is stable and unlikely to interfere with safe driving.

sec12-card-r09.front: Whom should a driver with a heart condition consult about whether driving remains safe?
sec12-card-r09.expected_back: Ask the treating doctor whether a heart condition could affect safe driving.

sec12-card-r10.front: How do heavy stress or intense emotions affect your performance in traffic?
sec12-card-r10.expected_back: Stress or strong emotions can reduce concentration and safe-driving ability.

sec12-card-r11.front: What should you do if you feel angry or worked up right before driving?
sec12-card-r11.expected_back: If angry or excited, wait off the road until calm before driving.

sec12-card-r12.front: What trip-planning habit counters impatience before it pushes you into speeding or risky moves?
sec12-card-r12.expected_back: Allow extra trip time when impatience might encourage speeding or risky driving.

sec12-card-r13.front: What should an older driver do if a physician advises avoiding night, high-speed, or heavy-traffic driving?
sec12-card-r13.expected_back: An older driver should follow a doctor’s advice to avoid heavy traffic, high-speed traffic or night driving when that advice is given.

sec12-card-r14.front: Which numbered Montana form can medical professionals file to recommend a driver re-examination?
sec12-card-r14.expected_back: Medical professionals can use form thirty-two-one thousand eight hundred for a Recommendation for Re-Exam.

sec12-card-r15.front: Which numbered Montana form is used for a formal Driver Medical Evaluation?
sec12-card-r15.expected_back: Form twenty-nineteen hundred is listed for Driver Medical Evaluation.

sec12-card-r16.front: Which numbered Montana form records a specialist's Report of Eye Examination?
sec12-card-r16.expected_back: Form twenty-two-one thousand eight hundred one is listed for a Report of Eye Examination.

sec12-card-r17.front: Under what personal condition should older drivers choose to get behind the wheel?
sec12-card-r17.expected_back: Older drivers should drive only when they feel well and able to do so.

sec12-card-r18.front: When may an older driver get behind the wheel after taking medication?
sec12-card-r18.expected_back: Older drivers should not drive after taking medication unless their doctor says it is safe.

sec12-card-r19.front: Whose unexpected, unsafe movements must defensive drivers stay constantly alert for?
sec12-card-r19.expected_back: Stay alert for sudden unsafe moves by other drivers, pedestrians and children.

sec12-card-r20.front: What traffic knowledge should experienced drivers keep refreshing over the years?
sec12-card-r20.expected_back: Keep current on traffic laws and safe-driving rules.

sec12-card-r21.front: How should older drivers plan routes to match their comfort and safety?
sec12-card-r21.expected_back: Older drivers should plan trips and avoid busy, high-speed or personally troubling routes.

sec12-card-r22.front: What three adjustments help if your slower pace backs up vehicles behind you?
sec12-card-r22.expected_back: If slow driving holds up traffic, pull off and let it pass, or choose another route or a quieter travel time.

sec12-card-r23.front: How should you keep your vehicle mechanically safe as part of personal fitness precautions?
sec12-card-r23.expected_back: Keep the vehicle in safe condition with regular equipment checks.

sec12-card-r24.front: Which three surfaces should you clean regularly to protect visibility, especially after dark?
sec12-card-r24.expected_back: Clean the windshield, headlamps and eyeglasses to preserve the driving view, especially at night.

sec12-card-r25.front: On which trips does the fitness-precautions section advise buckling your seatbelt?
sec12-card-r25.expected_back: Wear a seatbelt on every drive.

sec12-card-r26.front: How many attempts at parallel parking count as a driving-skill self-check warning?
sec12-card-r26.expected_back: Needing two or three attempts to parallel park is one of the handbook’s driving-skill self-check concerns.

sec12-card-r27.front: What does struggling to spot objects at night or lingering discomfort from headlight glare indicate?
sec12-card-r27.expected_back: Trouble distinguishing objects at night or prolonged discomfort from headlight glare is a reason to reassess driving vision.

sec12-card-r28.front: In the older-driver self-check, what do lagging behind traffic pace or slow starts at green lights suggest?
sec12-card-r28.expected_back: For the handbook’s older-driver self-check, trouble keeping pace with traffic or taking a long time to start after a green light is a reason to consider driving ability.

sec12-card-r29.front: What pattern of minor body damage warns a driver to review their driving skills?
sec12-card-r29.expected_back: Increasing minor vehicle scrapes or dents can be a warning to review driving skills.

sec12-card-r30.front: What should missing road signs or feeling disoriented in unfamiliar traffic prompt you to do?
sec12-card-r30.expected_back: Missing traffic signs or becoming confused by unfamiliar situations calls for reviewing driving ability.

sec12-card-r31.front: What self-check conclusion follows trouble judging distance, spotting near or far objects, or seeing road edges?
sec12-card-r31.expected_back: For the handbook’s older-driver self-check, trouble judging distance, seeing nearby or distant objects, or detecting the road edges is a reason to consider driving ability.

sec12-card-r32.front: Which five personal warning signs can guide a driver's decision to stop driving altogether?
sec12-card-r32.expected_back: Health or medication effects, close calls, a serious crash, discomfort at the wheel or fear of getting lost can inform the decision to stop driving.

sec12-card-r33.front: Where can a Montana driver voluntarily surrender their license once safe driving is no longer possible?
sec12-card-r33.expected_back: A driver who believes safe driving is no longer possible may surrender the license at any driver exam station.

sec12-card-r34.front: Which form lets concerned family or citizens ask the state to re-examine another driver's ability?
sec12-card-r34.expected_back: Concerns about another driver’s ability may be submitted using Recommendation for Re-Exam form thirty-two-one thousand eight hundred.

sec14-card-f01.front: Why can Montana suspend, revoke, or cancel your driver license if you break traffic laws?
sec14-card-f01.expected_back: A driver license is a privilege that can be suspended, revoked or canceled for breaking the law.

sec14-card-f02.front: Beyond fines or court dates, what licensing consequence does the handbook tie to impaired driving?
sec14-card-f02.expected_back: Impaired driving is a listed example of conduct that can lead to losing a driver license.

sec14-card-f03.front: Can distracted driving lead to losing your Montana driver license, or only minor fines?
sec14-card-f03.expected_back: Distracted driving is a listed example of conduct that can lead to losing a driver license.

sec14-card-f04.front: What happens to your licensing status if you keep driving while already suspended or revoked?
sec14-card-f04.expected_back: Driving while the license is suspended or revoked can cause further loss of licensing privileges.

sec14-card-f05.front: Which underage offense can strip a young person's driver license even outside a traffic stop?
sec14-card-f05.expected_back: A minor-in-possession offense is another listed example that can cause license loss.

sec14-card-f06.front: Which major section of a Montana driving record holds your identifying background details?
sec14-card-f06.expected_back: Personal-history information is one major category in a driving record.

sec14-card-f07.front: Which major category of a driving record tracks your credential class, status, and endorsements?
sec14-card-f07.expected_back: Licensing information is a major driving-record category.

sec14-card-f08.front: Which combined major category on a driving record pairs court violations with road collisions?
sec14-card-f08.expected_back: A driving record includes a major category covering conviction and accident history.

sec14-card-f09.front: Which major driving-record category logs formal penalties taken against your driving privilege?
sec14-card-f09.expected_back: Driver-license sanctions form a major category in the driving record.

sec14-card-f10.front: Which listed major category of a Montana driving record specifically tracks motor-vehicle collisions?
sec14-card-f10.expected_back: Motor-vehicle accident history is also listed as a major driving-record category.

sec14-card-f11.front: Does your permanent driving record retain details from your original driver-license application?
sec14-card-f11.expected_back: The driving record keeps details of the person’s driver-license application.

sec14-card-f12.front: What stage of proving your knowledge and road skills is documented in your driving record?
sec14-card-f12.expected_back: The examination process is documented in the driving record.

sec14-card-f13.front: Once you pass testing, what milestone of granting driving privileges goes onto your driving record?
sec14-card-f13.expected_back: The driving record includes the later issuance of a license.

sec14-card-f14.front: If the state declines an applicant's request for a license, is that refusal recorded?
sec14-card-f14.expected_back: A denial of a license is among the actions recorded in the driving record.

sec14-card-f15.front: How does a Montana driving record treat a formal license revocation?
sec14-card-f15.expected_back: License revocation is among the licensing actions kept in the record.

sec14-card-f16.front: Is a temporary license suspension stored among the licensing actions on your driving record?
sec14-card-f16.expected_back: License suspension is among the licensing actions kept in the record.

sec14-card-f17.front: Does your driving record's licensing history also include a license cancellation?
sec14-card-f17.expected_back: Cancellation of a license is included in the driving record’s licensing history.

sec14-card-f18.front: Beyond applications and status changes, what performance details and state interventions does your record keep?
sec14-card-f18.expected_back: The record also keeps information about driver performance and actions taken for unsafe performance or other legal requirements.

sec14-card-r01.front: Which Montana Motor Vehicle Division resource does the handbook name for deeper suspension and revocation rules?
sec14-card-r01.expected_back: The handbook refers drivers to the Montana Motor Vehicle Division’s suspensions-and-revocations resource for additional penalty information.

sec14-card-r02.front: Which Motor Vehicle Division resource explains how to request a copy of a Montana driving record?
sec14-card-r02.expected_back: The handbook points to the Motor Vehicle Division’s driving-records resource for instructions on requesting a record.

sec13-card-f01.front: What routine vehicle care cuts the odds of mechanical failure out on the road?
sec13-card-f01.expected_back: Follow the owner’s maintenance schedule to reduce the chance of a vehicle failure.

sec13-card-f02.front: If your regular brakes suddenly fail, what should you do first with the brake pedal?
sec13-card-f02.expected_back: If the brakes stop working, pump the pedal several times to try to restore pressure.

sec13-card-f03.front: If pumping fails, how should you apply a handle-operated parking brake—and why stay ready to release it?
sec13-card-f03.expected_back: If pumping fails, apply a handle-operated parking brake slowly and be ready to release it if the vehicle begins to skid.

sec13-card-f04.front: If even the parking brake cannot stop your vehicle, what gear and steering action come next?
sec13-card-f04.expected_back: If the parking brake cannot stop the vehicle, shift down and seek a safe place off the road to stop.

sec13-card-f05.front: Once you get a vehicle with failed brakes stopped safely, may you limp it further down the road?
sec13-card-f05.expected_back: Do not continue driving a vehicle without functioning brakes.

sec13-card-f06.front: What is your immediate steering priority the moment a tire blows out?
sec13-card-f06.expected_back: After a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the vehicle moving straight.

sec13-card-f07.front: How should you handle the gas and brake pedals to shed speed after a tire blows?
sec13-card-f07.expected_back: With a blown tire, release the accelerator, slow gradually and brake lightly.

sec13-card-f08.front: Where should you bring the vehicle to a complete stop after slowing from a blowout?
sec13-card-f08.expected_back: After a blowout, stop off the road in a safe place whenever possible.

sec13-card-f09.front: Why must you grip the steering wheel firmly if your engine suddenly dies in motion?
sec13-card-f09.expected_back: If the engine dies while driving, hold the wheel firmly because steering may become harder.

sec13-card-f10.front: As you steer off the roadway with a stalled engine, how will the brake pedal feel?
sec13-card-f10.expected_back: After engine failure, pull off the roadway and expect that braking may require much more pedal pressure.

sec13-card-f11.front: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, what are your very first three calm steps?
sec13-card-f11.expected_back: If headlights suddenly fail, stay calm, release the accelerator and begin braking.

sec13-card-f12.front: Which two lighting controls should you cycle right away to try reviving dead headlights?
sec13-card-f12.expected_back: For failed headlights, try the light switch several times and try the high beams.

sec13-card-f13.front: If neither the switch nor high beams restore your headlights, which backup lights help you pull off safely?
sec13-card-f13.expected_back: If the headlight switch and high beams do not restore lighting, use available flashers, turn signals or fog lamps while pulling off safely as soon as possible.

sec13-card-f14.front: If the accelerator sticks open, what should you do immediately while keeping your eyes on the road?
sec13-card-f14.expected_back: If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road and shift promptly to neutral.

sec13-card-f15.front: After shifting a stuck-throttle car to neutral, when do you brake, pull off, and shut off the ignition?
sec13-card-f15.expected_back: With a stuck accelerator, brake with steady pressure and pull off when safe before turning the engine off.

sec13-card-f16.front: What is your initial response if your right wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-f16.expected_back: If the right wheels leave the pavement, release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road.

sec13-card-f17.front: After slowing beside the pavement edge, how do your hands turn the wheel to reenter the right lane?
sec13-card-f17.expected_back: After a right-wheel departure, slow first and reenter safely into the right lane using both hands and a small left quarter-turn of the steering wheel.

sec13-card-f18.front: In Montana's right-wheel drop-off recovery, when do you apply the brakes and where do you position the car?
sec13-card-f18.expected_back: In the described right-wheel recovery, brake after returning to pavement and remain in the lane.

sec13-card-f19.front: Which three vehicle actions can help you avoid an impending collision?
sec13-card-f19.expected_back: To avoid a collision, a driver may need to stop, turn or accelerate.

sec13-card-f20.front: Where should you check the exact anti-lock braking instructions for the specific vehicle you drive?
sec13-card-f20.expected_back: Read the owner’s manual for the vehicle’s anti-lock braking procedure.

sec13-card-f21.front: How do you execute an emergency quick stop with anti-lock brakes, even if the pedal pulses back?
sec13-card-f21.expected_back: For a quick stop with anti-lock brakes, press hard and maintain pressure even if the pedal pushes back.

sec13-card-f22.front: How hard should you press the brake pedal during an emergency stop in a vehicle without ABS?
sec13-card-f22.expected_back: For a quick stop without anti-lock brakes, brake as hard as possible without locking the wheels.

sec13-card-f23.front: If non-ABS wheels lock up and skid during a hard stop, how should you work the pedal?
sec13-card-f23.expected_back: If non-ABS brakes lock and the vehicle skids, promptly ease off, then reapply as the skid ends, repeating until stopped.

sec13-card-f24.front: How should you hold and aim the steering wheel during a sudden collision-avoidance turn?
sec13-card-f24.expected_back: Keep both hands firmly on the wheel when making an emergency turn and steer toward the desired path.

sec13-card-f25.front: Why must you stay poised to straighten and control the vehicle right after an avoidance swerve?
sec13-card-f25.expected_back: After an avoidance turn or lane change, remain ready to control the vehicle so the maneuver does not create another collision.

sec13-card-f26.front: Which two safety systems allow a vehicle to handle simultaneous hard braking and emergency turning?
sec13-card-f26.expected_back: The handbook describes braking and turning together for vehicles with anti-lock brakes and electronic stability control.

sec13-card-f27.front: Without anti-lock brakes, how do you time braking before a quick turn so the car does not plow straight?
sec13-card-f27.expected_back: Without anti-lock brakes, slow with the brake and then release it before a quick turn; avoid locking the front wheels or turning so sharply that the car plows ahead.

sec13-card-f28.front: When can stepping on the gas avoid a rear or side crash, and what follows once clear?
sec13-card-f28.expected_back: Acceleration can help avoid a rear or side impact when there is clear room ahead, but slow again after the danger passes.

sec13-card-f29.front: Which belt combination lowers your vulnerability to injury when a crash cannot be avoided?
sec13-card-f29.expected_back: Use both lap and shoulder belts to reduce injury vulnerability in a collision.

sec13-card-f30.front: How should you position your body and foot right before being struck from behind?
sec13-card-f30.expected_back: For a rear impact, press against the seatback with the head at the restraint and be ready to brake against being pushed into another vehicle.

sec13-card-f31.front: Even with side airbags, why do belts stay essential in a side hit—and what must you stay ready for?
sec13-card-f31.expected_back: In a side impact, belts remain necessary even with side airbags, and the driver should be ready to steer or brake to avoid a second collision.

sec13-card-f32.front: If an oncoming frontal impact becomes unavoidable, how should you try to alter the hit?
sec13-card-f32.expected_back: If a frontal impact is imminent, try to avoid a direct head-on collision by changing the vehicle’s angle when possible.

sec13-card-f33.front: Under what two conditions only should you stop at a crash scene?
sec13-card-f33.expected_back: Do not stop at a crash unless involved or emergency help has not yet arrived.

sec13-card-f34.front: Why must drivers never drive toward or linger at a crash, fire, or disaster just to watch?
sec13-card-f34.expected_back: Never visit a crash, fire or disaster merely to look, because that can obstruct rescuers.

sec13-card-f35.front: What is every driver's immediate legal duty whenever involved in a crash?
sec13-card-f35.expected_back: If involved in a crash, stop.

sec13-card-f36.front: What must you try to do first right after striking an unattended parked vehicle?
sec13-card-f36.expected_back: After hitting a parked vehicle, try to locate its owner.

sec13-card-f37.front: Whom must you notify whenever a collision injures or kills anyone?
sec13-card-f37.expected_back: Notify police when a crash injures or kills someone.

sec13-card-f38.front: What legal classification applies to leaving an injury or fatal crash before police gather needed details?
sec13-card-f38.expected_back: Leaving an injury or fatal crash involving your vehicle before police obtain the needed information is a crime.

sec13-card-r01.front: After stopping at or near a crash, what should you do if your vehicle still moves safely?
sec13-card-r01.expected_back: Stop at or near the crash and move a movable vehicle off the road so it does not obstruct traffic.

sec13-card-r02.front: Where must crash occupants and witnesses avoid standing or walking while waiting at the scene?
sec13-card-r02.expected_back: Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes at a crash scene.

sec13-card-r03.front: Which two fire-prevention steps apply around wrecked vehicles at a crash scene?
sec13-card-r03.expected_back: Turn wrecked vehicles’ ignitions off and do not smoke near them because spilled fuel may ignite.

sec13-card-r04.front: How should everyone at a crash scene treat downed electrical wires?
sec13-card-r04.expected_back: Stay away from downed electrical wires at a crash.

sec13-card-r05.front: Why should you deploy appropriate warning devices around a crash site?
sec13-card-r05.expected_back: Use appropriate warning devices to keep other traffic from entering the crash scene.

sec13-card-r06.front: When a crash injures someone, which emergency responders must be called—and what hazard must be reported?
sec13-card-r06.expected_back: If someone is injured, ensure police and emergency medical or rescue help have been called, and report any fire.

sec13-card-r07.front: When is the only time you should move an injured crash victim yourself?
sec13-card-r07.expected_back: Do not move an injured person unless a burning vehicle or another immediate danger requires it.

sec13-card-r08.front: May you offer water or any other drink to someone injured in a collision?
sec13-card-r08.expected_back: Do not give an injured person anything to drink, including water.

sec13-card-r09.front: Which three groups of people at a crash should have their names and addresses written down?
sec13-card-r09.expected_back: Record the names and addresses of people involved, witnesses and injured people.

sec13-card-r10.front: What three categories of driver, vehicle, and coverage details must involved drivers swap?
sec13-card-r10.expected_back: Exchange driver names, addresses and license numbers, vehicle plates and descriptions, and insurance company and policy details.

sec13-card-r11.front: Which four specific vehicle facts belong in your post-crash information exchange?
sec13-card-r11.expected_back: The vehicle information exchanged after a crash includes plate number, make, model and year.

sec13-card-r12.front: Alongside noting vehicle damage, how must you respond to police or emergency officials at the scene?
sec13-card-r12.expected_back: Record vehicle damage and provide requested information to police or emergency officials.

sec13-card-r13.front: If you cannot find a struck parked car's owner, what details belong on the visible note you leave?
sec13-card-r13.expected_back: If a parked vehicle’s owner cannot be found after a crash, leave a visible note with contact information and the crash date and time.

sec13-card-r14.front: Besides any injury or death, what property-damage threshold requires immediate notice to law enforcement?
sec13-card-r14.expected_back: Immediately notify law enforcement of a crash involving injury, death or property damage of at least five hundred dollars.

sec13-card-r15.front: Within how many days—and to whom—must you file a report for injury, death, or $1,000 property damage?
sec13-card-r15.expected_back: An injury, death or at least one thousand dollars of damage to one person’s property requires a Highway Patrol report within ten days.

sec13-card-r16.front: Who may submit the required crash report if injuries prevent the driver from filing it personally?
sec13-card-r16.expected_back: If injury prevents filing the crash report, another person may file it for the injured driver.

sec13-card-r17.front: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec13-card-r17.expected_back: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction, yield and, when safe and possible, pull to the right edge and stop.

sec13-card-r18.front: How should you align your vehicle at the right curb when yielding to emergency lights and sirens?
sec13-card-r18.expected_back: With an emergency vehicle using audio and visual signals, non-emergency vehicles must move immediately parallel and as close as possible to the right curb or edge.

sec13-card-r19.front: On highways posted 50 mph or higher, how much must adjacent-lane traffic slow past a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec13-card-r19.expected_back: On a highway posted at fifty miles per hour or more, traffic in the lane directly next to a stationary signaling emergency or police vehicle must travel at least twenty miles per hour below the posted limit.

sec13-card-r20.front: Whenever traffic allows, which lane should you choose when passing a stationary emergency or police vehicle?
sec13-card-r20.expected_back: When possible, move to a lane farther from a stationary emergency or police vehicle displaying emergency signals.

sec13-card-r21.front: Alongside a siren, which three flashing or rotating light colors identify police emergency signals?
sec13-card-r21.expected_back: Police emergency signals may include a siren or flashing or rotating red, blue or amber lights.

sec13-card-r22.front: Which warning sound and two lamp colors are listed for authorized emergency vehicles?
sec13-card-r22.expected_back: The listed authorized-emergency-vehicle signals include a siren or flashing or rotating red or amber lamps.

sec13-card-r23.front: How should you immediately acknowledge a patrol officer who turns on emergency lights behind you?
sec13-card-r23.expected_back: When pulled over, acknowledge the officer by switching on the right turn signal.

sec13-card-r24.front: Where should you guide your car during a routine traffic enforcement stop?
sec13-card-r24.expected_back: For an enforcement stop, follow the patrol vehicle’s guidance and pull to the right shoulder.

sec13-card-r25.front: Which two roadside spots must you never pull into during a police enforcement stop?
sec13-card-r25.expected_back: During an enforcement stop, do not stop in the center median or on the opposite side of a two-lane road.

sec13-card-r26.front: How far off the pavement should you pull, and what lighting helps during a night stop?
sec13-card-r26.expected_back: Pull as far off the road as possible and choose a well-lit stopping place when available.

sec13-card-r27.front: What should you do with active phone calls and car audio as soon as you stop for police?
sec13-card-r27.expected_back: During a traffic stop, end phone conversations and switch the radio off.

sec13-card-r28.front: Should you step out of your vehicle to meet the officer during a traffic stop?
sec13-card-r28.expected_back: Remain in the vehicle unless the officer directs you to get out.

sec13-card-r29.front: Who inside a stopped vehicle should keep their hands in plain view of the approaching officer?
sec13-card-r29.expected_back: The driver and passengers should keep their hands clearly visible to the officer.

sec13-card-r30.front: If your vehicle has tinted windows, when should you roll them down during a traffic stop?
sec13-card-r30.expected_back: With tinted windows, the handbook recommends lowering them after stopping on the right shoulder and before the officer makes contact.

sec11-card-f01.front: How does your clear view ahead govern safe speed choice?
sec11-card-f01.expected_back: Choose a speed that always allows a safe stop within the clear view ahead.

sec11-card-f02.front: How do you run the four-second sight-distance check, and what if you pass the object early?
sec11-card-f02.expected_back: For the four-second sight-distance check, choose the farthest clearly visible stationary object and slow down if you reach it before finishing a four-second count.

sec11-card-f03.front: What common nighttime hazard does the four-second sight-distance check prevent?
sec11-card-f03.expected_back: The four-second sight-distance check also helps a driver avoid outdriving the headlights at night.

sec11-card-f04.front: Does a dry, empty-looking highway allow exceeding the posted speed limit?
sec11-card-f04.expected_back: Obey posted speed limits even when the road looks free of visible hazards.

sec11-card-f05.front: What road conditions do posted speed signs assume, and when must you drive slower?
sec11-card-f05.expected_back: Posted limits assume ideal conditions; wet or icy roads, poor visibility or heavy traffic require a slower speed.

sec11-card-f06.front: Can an officer ticket you while driving below the posted speed limit?
sec11-card-f06.expected_back: Driving below the posted limit can still lead to a citation if the speed is too fast for conditions.

sec11-card-f07.front: What crucial advantage does keeping a generous space cushion around your car provide?
sec11-card-f07.expected_back: Keeping more room around the vehicle gives more time to react to other road users.

sec11-card-f08.front: At what exact moment do you start counting during the three-second following check?
sec11-card-f08.expected_back: For the three-second following check, start counting when the rear of the vehicle ahead passes a fixed marker.

sec11-card-f09.front: What should you do if your car passes the fixed marker before reaching three seconds?
sec11-card-f09.expected_back: If you pass that marker before counting three seconds, fall back and repeat the check until the gap is at least three seconds.

sec11-card-f10.front: How many seconds of following space does Montana recommend when conditions demand extra margin?
sec11-card-f10.expected_back: Some conditions call for more following space, and the handbook suggests a four-second interval in these situations.

sec11-card-f11.front: Why must you widen your following gap on wet, snowy, or icy pavement?
sec11-card-f11.expected_back: On slippery roads, leave more space ahead because stopping requires more distance.

sec11-card-f12.front: How should you adjust speed when a driver behind starts passing you?
sec11-card-f12.expected_back: When a following driver wants to pass, slow enough to create room ahead and help the pass finish sooner.

sec11-card-f13.front: Why should you leave extra following distance behind a motorcycle?
sec11-card-f13.expected_back: Give a motorcycle extra following room so a fallen rider can be avoided.

sec11-card-f14.front: On which four surface types are motorcycles especially prone to losing traction and falling?
sec11-card-f14.expected_back: Motorcycles are especially likely to fall on wet, icy, gravel or metal surfaces such as bridge gratings and tracks.

sec11-card-f15.front: Why must you drop farther back behind a truck, bus, van, or trailer rig?
sec11-card-f15.expected_back: Fall back when following a truck, bus, van or towing vehicle whose driver may not see you directly behind it.

sec11-card-f16.front: How does carrying a heavy cargo load or towing a trailer change needed following space?
sec11-card-f16.expected_back: A heavy load or trailer increases stopping distance, so leave more following room.

sec11-card-f17.front: What following adjustment applies when darkness, fog, or storms obscure the view ahead?
sec11-card-f17.expected_back: Increase the following gap when darkness or bad weather makes the view ahead difficult.

sec11-card-f18.front: What two options help clear a driver who is following you too closely?
sec11-card-f18.expected_back: When closely followed, slow to encourage a pass or use a turnout to let the other driver by.

sec11-card-f19.front: How should you space your car when following emergency vehicles?
sec11-card-f19.expected_back: Allow emergency vehicles extra operating room when following them.

sec11-card-f20.front: Which two vehicle classes need extra following space approaching railroad tracks because they must stop?
sec11-card-f20.expected_back: Approaching a railroad crossing, leave extra room behind buses or hazardous-material vehicles that must stop there.

sec11-card-f21.front: Why must you stop farther back behind another vehicle on an uphill grade?
sec11-card-f21.expected_back: When stopped on a hill, leave room for the vehicle ahead to roll backward as it starts.

sec11-card-f22.front: Which two driving habits help motorists behind you maintain a safe gap?
sec11-card-f22.expected_back: A steady speed and early slowing signals help the driver behind maintain space.

sec11-card-f23.front: Where should you stop whenever picking up or dropping off passengers?
