sec10-card-r34.expected_back: If vehicles pile up behind your slower vehicle, pull over to let them pass when it is safe.

sec10-card-r35.front: What signal and two visual checks accompany every highway merge?
sec10-card-r35.expected_back: When merging, signal, use the rearview mirror and look over your shoulder.

sec10-card-r36.front: How should you use a highway acceleration ramp before blending into main lanes?
sec10-card-r36.expected_back: Use an acceleration ramp to approach the traffic speed before joining the main road.

sec10-card-r37.front: Why must you never drive to the end of an entrance ramp and stop?
sec10-card-r37.expected_back: Do not drive to the ramp’s end and stop; if waiting for a gap is necessary, slow earlier to retain acceleration room.

sec10-card-r38.front: How can drivers on a controlled-access highway help ramp traffic enter safely?
sec10-card-r38.expected_back: On a controlled-access highway, move left when possible to help another driver enter safely.

sec10-card-r39.front: When leaving via an exit ramp, in what order do you signal, enter the ramp, and slow down?
sec10-card-r39.expected_back: With an exit ramp, signal first and delay slowing until the vehicle is on the ramp.

sec10-card-r40.front: How do you exit a fast two-lane road safely when traffic follows behind?
sec10-card-r40.expected_back: When leaving a fast two-lane road with traffic behind, avoid slowing too early, tap the brakes and reduce speed promptly but safely.

sec10-card-r41.front: Why watch trucks and underpowered cars carefully on steep grades or highway entries?
sec10-card-r41.expected_back: Watch for trucks and underpowered cars that may lose speed on steep grades or need longer to enter traffic.

sec10-card-r42.front: At what speed do farm tractors, buggies, and road machines usually travel, and what rear marker is required?
sec10-card-r42.expected_back: Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles usually travel at twenty-five miles per hour or less and need a rear slow-moving sign.

sec10-card-r43.front: How many delayed vehicles require a slow-moving driver to pull off at a safe turnout?
sec10-card-r43.expected_back: A slow-moving vehicle must turn off when it delays four or more vehicles and sufficient room permits a safe turnout.

sec10-card-r44.front: Which lane must slow-moving traffic use on a multilane roadway?
sec10-card-r44.expected_back: Slow-moving traffic must use the extreme right lane.

sec10-card-r45.front: How should you adjust speed in crowded zones where people and cars leave little maneuvering room?
sec10-card-r45.expected_back: Reduce speed in crowded places where people and traffic leave little room to maneuver.

sec10-card-r46.front: Around which busy commercial zones and narrow structures must you stay poised to slow?
sec10-card-r46.expected_back: Be ready to slow around shopping areas, parking lots, busy downtown streets, rush traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels and toll plazas.

sec10-card-r47.front: What specific hazard demands extra vigilance near schools, playgrounds, and home streets?
sec10-card-r47.expected_back: Around schools, playgrounds and residential streets, watch for children entering without looking.

sec10-card-r48.front: Roughly how many total feet can reacting and stopping from 50 mph take even on dry pavement with good gear?
sec10-card-r48.expected_back: With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement, reacting and stopping from fifty miles per hour can take about four hundred feet.

sec10-card-r49.front: Roughly how many feet can stopping from 30 mph take on dry pavement with good tires and brakes?
sec10-card-r49.expected_back: With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement, stopping from thirty miles per hour can take about two hundred feet.

sec10-card-r50.front: What rule connects nighttime speed to the distance lit by your headlights?
sec10-card-r50.expected_back: Choose a nighttime speed that lets you stop within the distance illuminated ahead.

sec10-card-r51.front: Why must you run headlights in rain, fog, or falling snow?
sec10-card-r51.expected_back: In rain, fog or snow, use headlights so other drivers can see the vehicle.

sec10-card-r52.front: Above what speed does Montana warn driving becomes unsafe when heavy rain, fog, or snow cuts visibility to 200 feet?
sec10-card-r52.expected_back: In very heavy rain, thick fog or a snowstorm that limits the view to about two hundred feet, the handbook warns that more than thirty miles per hour is unsafe.

sec10-card-r53.front: What should you do when a heavy downpour cuts vision below what safe driving requires?
sec10-card-r53.expected_back: If a downpour prevents adequate vision for driving, pull off safely and wait for the weather to clear.

sec10-card-r54.front: How fast may you approach a hillcrest or curve that hides the lane ahead?
sec10-card-r54.expected_back: Approach a hill or curve with blocked sightlines slowly enough to stop for a hidden obstruction.

sec10-card-r55.front: Why give parked vehicles along the street as much lateral room as possible?
sec10-card-r55.expected_back: Give parked vehicles as much room as possible because they can hide pedestrians or people getting out.

sec04-card-f01.front: Why must you keep hanging items off the mirror and view-blocking decals off the windshield?
sec04-card-f01.expected_back: Do not hang items from the mirror or cover the windshield with decals that may obstruct the view.

sec04-card-f02.front: How much effectiveness can dirty headlamps, backup lights, brake lights, and taillights lose?
sec04-card-f02.expected_back: Keep headlamps, backup lights, brake lights and taillights clean because dirty lenses can cut their effectiveness by fifty percent.

sec04-card-f03.front: When should you check and adjust your seat and mirror settings?
sec04-card-f03.expected_back: Check the seat and mirror settings before starting to drive.

sec04-card-f04.front: How high should you set the driver seat, and what aid helps if needed?
sec04-card-f04.expected_back: Set the seat high enough to see the road clearly, using a cushion if needed.

sec04-card-f05.front: What problem tells you the driver seat is slid too far forward?
sec04-card-f05.expected_back: Do not place the seat so far forward that steering becomes difficult.

sec04-card-f06.front: What view should the interior rearview mirror frame?
sec04-card-f06.expected_back: Set the interior rearview mirror to show the view through the back window.

sec04-card-f07.front: How should outside mirrors be angled when checked with a slight forward lean?
sec04-card-f07.expected_back: Adjust side mirrors to show the sides, with the vehicle side visible when leaning slightly forward.

sec04-card-f08.front: How should you set a day-and-night interior mirror before driving?
sec04-card-f08.expected_back: Set a day-and-night mirror for the lighting conditions in which you will drive.

sec04-card-f09.front: What injury is a vehicle head restraint designed to reduce, and in what kind of crash?
sec04-card-f09.expected_back: A head restraint is intended to reduce whiplash in a rear impact.

sec04-card-f10.front: Where should a properly adjusted head restraint make contact?
sec04-card-f10.expected_back: Adjust the head restraint so that it contacts the back of the head.

sec04-card-f11.front: Who does Montana hold legally responsible for making sure occupants wear belts or use child seats?
sec04-card-f11.expected_back: Montana makes the driver responsible for ensuring occupants are properly belted or secured in child safety seats, subject to the listed legal exceptions.

sec04-card-f12.front: Does driving a short distance at low speed excuse skipping your safety belt?
sec04-card-f12.expected_back: Use the safety belt on every trip, including short trips at low speed.

sec04-card-f13.front: What two restraint steps belong right before pulling away?
sec04-card-f13.expected_back: Before leaving, fasten your belt and check that passengers are using belts or child restraints.

sec04-card-f14.front: What should you do with vehicle doors before driving away?
sec04-card-f14.expected_back: Lock the vehicle doors before driving away.

sec04-card-f15.front: How must a lap-and-shoulder restraint system be worn for full intended protection?
sec04-card-f15.expected_back: A two-part belt system requires both the lap portion and the shoulder portion for its intended protection.

sec04-card-f16.front: What must you still fasten manually in a car equipped with an automatic shoulder belt?
sec04-card-f16.expected_back: With an automatic shoulder belt, buckle the lap belt too.

sec04-card-f17.front: What happens to crash protection if you wear only one portion of a lap-and-shoulder belt?
sec04-card-f17.expected_back: Using only one portion of a lap-and-shoulder system substantially reduces protection.

sec04-card-f18.front: How does one unrestrained person endanger buckled occupants inside the same car?
sec04-card-f18.expected_back: An unrestrained occupant can strike and seriously injure other people in the vehicle during a crash.

sec04-card-r01.front: Vehicles manufactured before what date fall under Montana seatbelt-law exceptions?
sec04-card-r01.expected_back: The listed seatbelt-law exceptions include vehicles manufactured before January one, nineteen sixty-eight.

sec04-card-r02.front: What documentation must an occupant carry to use a medical seatbelt exemption?
sec04-card-r02.expected_back: An occupant unable to wear a belt for medical reasons needs to carry a physician’s written statement to use the stated exemption.

sec04-card-r03.front: Who is covered by the special-mobile-equipment seatbelt exemption?
sec04-card-r03.expected_back: The stated special-mobile-equipment seatbelt exemption applies to the operator of a vehicle licensed in that category.

sec04-card-r04.front: How does Montana define special mobile equipment regarding transport use and highway travel?
sec04-card-r04.expected_back: Special mobile equipment is not primarily designed or used to transport people or property and is moved on highways only incidentally.

sec04-card-r05.front: Which agency can grant a seatbelt exemption to workers making frequent job-duty stops?
sec04-card-r05.expected_back: A driver making frequent stops as part of official job duties may receive a seatbelt exemption from the Department of Justice.

sec04-card-r06.front: Which form number applies to frequent-stop workers seeking a seatbelt exemption?
sec04-card-r06.memory_hook: Apply using form MVD SE one
sec04-card-r06.expected_back: The handbook points frequent-stop workers to exemption form MVD-SE1.

sec04-card-r07.front: Until what milestone should older children continue riding in a booster seat?
sec04-card-r07.expected_back: Booster seats are recommended for older children until the lap-and-shoulder belt fits them properly.

sec04-card-r08.front: Around what height does an adult lap-and-shoulder belt usually fit a child properly?
sec04-card-r08.expected_back: A proper adult-belt fit for a child is usually reached at about four feet nine inches of height.

sec04-card-r09.front: What restraint setup must be used if a child has no choice except riding in front with an airbag?
sec04-card-r09.expected_back: If a child must sit in the front of an airbag-equipped vehicle, use a child safety seat with the vehicle belt or a booster with the lap-and-shoulder belt.

sec04-card-r10.front: How should you position the front passenger seat when a child must ride ahead of an active airbag?
sec04-card-r10.expected_back: When a child must ride in front, move the seat as far back from the active airbag as possible.

sec04-card-r11.front: What is the absolute rule on placing a rear-facing child seat in front of an active airbag?
sec04-card-r11.expected_back: Never put a rear-facing child seat in a front passenger position with an active airbag.

sec04-card-r12.front: Where should restrained children younger than thirteen ride whenever possible?
sec04-card-r12.expected_back: Whenever possible, children younger than thirteen should be restrained in the back seat.

sec04-card-r13.front: May two passengers share one seatbelt, or what does each rider require?
sec04-card-r13.expected_back: Every passenger needs an independent, properly used belt or child restraint.

sec04-card-r14.front: What deadly crash hazard comes from holding a child in your arms while riding?
sec04-card-r14.expected_back: Holding a child while riding can result in crushing the child during a collision.

sec06-card-f01.front: Which road users do traffic signals direct at intersections and mid-block crosswalks, and how?
sec06-card-f01.expected_back: Traffic signals direct vehicles and pedestrians at certain intersections and mid-block crosswalks by assigning the right of way.

sec06-card-f02.front: How must drivers treat a traffic signal that is dark or not working?
sec06-card-f02.expected_back: A signal that is not working is treated like stop signs in every direction, with the driver who stops first going first while staying cautious.

sec06-card-f03.front: When pedestrian signals are present, which display governs walkers, and what does WALK allow?
sec06-card-f03.expected_back: Where pedestrian signals are used, walkers obey them instead of the vehicle lights, and a WALK display lets them start crossing from the curb or sidewalk.

sec06-card-f04.front: How do walkers respond to steady or flashing DON'T WALK, and what do the hand and figure symbols mean?
sec06-card-f04.expected_back: A steady or flashing DON’T WALK display means wait for WALK, while walkers already in the crosswalk keep crossing; an orange hand means DON’T WALK and a white figure means WALK.

sec06-card-f05.front: Where must you stop on a steady red light, and when is a cautious right turn permitted?
sec06-card-f05.expected_back: A steady red light means stop before the stop line, the crosswalk, or the intersection, then a cautious right turn is allowed unless a sign or officer forbids it, yielding to pedestrians, bicyclists and traffic.

sec06-card-f06.front: Under what exact street layout may a driver turn left on red, and what applies to walkers facing red?
sec06-card-f06.expected_back: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street after stopping, and pedestrians facing red must stay out of the street unless a pedestrian signal directs otherwise.

sec06-card-f07.front: What does a steady red arrow require, and what narrow exception applies?
sec06-card-f07.expected_back: A steady red arrow means stop and remain stopped except for the allowed turns on red.

sec06-card-f08.front: Which sign does a flashing red light match, and what four-step check follows?
sec06-card-f08.expected_back: A flashing red light works like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, look left, right and ahead, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and continue when safe.

sec06-card-f09.front: When may a driver enter on a steady yellow light, and what rule applies to pedestrians facing yellow?
sec06-card-f09.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns that red is next, so enter cautiously and only when too close to stop safely; pedestrians facing yellow must not start across unless a pedestrian signal directs otherwise.

sec06-card-f10.front: What does a steady yellow arrow signal about your protected turn phase?
sec06-card-f10.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow ends the protected turn interval, so turning vehicles clear the intersection and prepare to obey the next display.

sec06-card-f11.front: When may you turn left on a flashing yellow arrow, and who holds the green?
sec06-card-f11.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow permits a left turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, who hold the green, and only when a safe gap exists.

sec06-card-f12.front: What does a flashing yellow traffic light tell an approaching driver to do?
sec06-card-f12.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution, which usually calls for slowing down.

sec06-card-f13.front: What hazard must drivers still watch for on a steady green light, and when may walkers cross?
sec06-card-f13.expected_back: A steady green light means go with caution while watching for traffic running the red, and pedestrians facing green may cross in a marked or unmarked crosswalk unless directed otherwise.

sec06-card-f14.front: How does turning on a steady green arrow differ from turning on a plain green ball?
sec06-card-f14.expected_back: A steady green arrow grants a protected turning movement, while turning traffic without a green arrow is unprotected and yields to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec06-card-r01.front: How do a dark traffic light and flashing red compare with a flashing yellow display?
sec06-card-r01.expected_back: A dead signal and a flashing red light both demand a stop-sign style stop, while a flashing yellow light on the same page asks only for cautious movement.

sec06-card-r02.front: May a pedestrian step off the curb on a green vehicle light while facing DON'T WALK?
sec06-card-r02.expected_back: Pedestrian WALK and DON’T WALK displays overrule the vehicle lights for walkers, so a green vehicle light never releases a pedestrian who faces DON’T WALK.

sec06-card-r03.front: How does Montana's rule for right turns on red differ from left turns on red?
sec06-card-r03.expected_back: A right turn on red is broadly allowed after stopping, while a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

sec06-card-r04.front: How does a steady red arrow's rule compare with a flashing red light's procedure?
sec06-card-r04.expected_back: A steady red arrow requires stopping and remaining stopped except for the handbook’s allowed turns on red; a flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding and proceeding only when safe.

sec06-card-r05.front: What is the exact difference between a steady yellow arrow and a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-r05.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow closes an existing protected turn, while a flashing yellow arrow opens an unprotected left turn that must yield to oncoming traffic holding the green.

sec06-card-r06.front: How does cautious movement on a flashing yellow compare with proceeding on a steady green?
sec06-card-r06.expected_back: A flashing yellow light only urges caution and slower movement, while a steady green light grants movement with continued watch for traffic running the red.

sec06-card-r07.front: Why is treating a plain green ball like a green arrow dangerous when turning?
sec06-card-r07.expected_back: A green arrow protects the indicated turning movement, while a plain green ball leaves turning traffic unprotected and yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec06-card-f15.front: What typical speed applies inside a roundabout, and what should you do on approach?
sec06-card-f15.expected_back: Roundabout driving speeds are fifteen miles per hour or less, so slow down on approach.

sec06-card-f16.front: Who holds the right-of-way at a roundabout entrance, and which direction does traffic circulate?
sec06-card-f16.expected_back: Yield to vehicles already inside the roundabout because they hold the right-of-way, and remember that circulation runs counterclockwise.

sec06-card-f17.front: Which side of the center island do you enter on, and what passing rule applies inside a single-lane roundabout?
sec06-card-f17.expected_back: Enter to the right of the center island and keep moving when the way is clear, and never pass another vehicle inside a single-lane roundabout.

sec06-card-f18.front: What signal and pedestrian check are required when exiting a roundabout onto your chosen street?
sec06-card-f18.expected_back: Circle to the desired street, give a right-turn signal, and exit, yielding to pedestrians who are in or waiting at the crosswalk.

sec06-card-f19.front: Why must smaller cars drop back behind large trucks inside a roundabout?
sec06-card-f19.expected_back: Give large vehicles extra room because their rear wheels track over the sloped truck apron, so a smaller vehicle should drop back behind them.

sec06-card-f20.front: Where must pedestrians cross at a roundabout, and which area is strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-f20.expected_back: Pedestrians cross only at the marked crosswalks and never walk to the central island, staying cautious even though vehicles must stop for them.

sec06-card-f21.front: What two options does the Montana handbook give bicyclists navigating a roundabout?
sec06-card-f21.expected_back: Bicyclists are urged to walk their bicycles on the sidewalks and crosswalks, or to ride the circulatory roadway as a vehicle with clear turn signals.

sec06-card-f22.front: How should you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle inside versus before a roundabout?
sec06-card-f22.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle approaches, never stop inside the roundabout; exit normally and then pull right, or pull over before entering only where room allows.

sec06-card-r08.front: Why must approaching drivers yield before entering a roundabout?
sec06-card-r08.expected_back: Drivers approaching a roundabout must yield to vehicles already circulating inside it because circulating traffic holds the right-of-way.

sec06-card-r09.front: Once inside a single-lane roundabout, is passing or overtaking another vehicle ever allowed?
sec06-card-r09.expected_back: Drivers must never pass or overtake another vehicle once they have entered a single-lane roundabout.

sec06-card-r10.front: If sirens approach while you are already circulating in a roundabout, what is your exact move?
sec06-card-r10.expected_back: An approaching emergency vehicle is met by exiting the roundabout first and pulling over after, never by stopping inside the circle.

sec06-card-f23.front: What four safety rules govern train races, doubt, far-side space, and shifting gears at railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f23.expected_back: Never race a train to the crossing, stop whenever safety is in doubt, keep space for the vehicle on the far side, and avoid shifting gears on the tracks.

sec06-card-f24.front: At least how far from the nearest rail must you stop when signals, gates, watchmen, or a close hazardous train require it?
sec06-card-f24.expected_back: Stop as close as practical but at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail when signals, gates, signs, watchmen, an approaching train, or a plainly hazardous visible train within fifteen hundred feet requires it.

sec06-card-f25.front: What four actions do advance railroad warning signs order before you reach the tracks?
sec06-card-f25.expected_back: Advance warning signs placed before the crossing order drivers to slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop ahead.

sec06-card-f26.front: What roadway feature do pavement markings with a stop line, a large X, and RR warn of?
sec06-card-f26.expected_back: Railroad pavement markings with a stop line, an X and the letters RR warn that a crossing lies ahead.

sec06-card-f27.front: Where do white crossbucks stand, and what extra sign appears when multiple tracks cross?
sec06-card-f27.expected_back: Crossbuck signs stand at every public crossing, with a lower sign giving the track count where more than one track exists, and drivers stay ready to stop for a train.

sec06-card-f28.front: What must you do as soon as crossing lights flash, and what extra check applies on multiple tracks?
sec06-card-f28.expected_back: Always stop when the crossing lights start to flash, and where several tracks exist confirm that every track is clear before crossing.

sec06-card-f29.front: When do you stop at a gated crossing, and when is it legal to drive forward again?
sec06-card-f29.expected_back: At gated crossings stop when the lights flash before the gates fall, and remain stopped until the gates rise and the flashing ends.

sec06-card-r11.front: How do advance railroad warning signs differ in command from flashing crossing lights or lowered gates?
sec06-card-r11.expected_back: Advance warning signs only urge readiness to stop at the crossing ahead, while flashing crossing lights and lowered gates order an actual stop.

sec06-card-r12.front: At a gated railroad crossing, why must you wait for both the gate to rise fully and the lights to stop flashing?
sec06-card-r12.expected_back: Flashing-light signals order stopping as soon as the flashing starts, while gates add a barrier that must fully rise with the flashing ended before traffic resumes.

sec06-card-f30.front: For what single maneuver may a driver cross a broken yellow centerline?
sec06-card-f30.expected_back: A broken yellow centerline may be crossed, but only to overtake or pass another vehicle.

sec06-card-f31.front: What do a solid yellow line on your side and a double yellow bar, and when may a solid centerline be crossed?
sec06-card-f31.expected_back: A solid yellow line on the driver side bars passing over the centerline, a double yellow line bars crossing from either direction, and a solid centerline may be crossed only within a left turn.

sec06-card-f32.front: How do white lane lines, yellow lane lines, and solid edge lines divide the roadway?
sec06-card-f32.expected_back: Lane lines are white between traffic moving the same way and yellow between opposing traffic, while solid edge lines mark the road edge.

sec06-card-f33.front: How does a dashed white lane line differ from a solid white lane line?
sec06-card-f33.expected_back: A dashed white lane line allows a careful lane change, while a solid white lane line means stay in lane except in a special situation.

sec06-card-f34.front: Where must you halt for a required stop, and which crosswalks get pedestrian priority?
sec06-card-f34.expected_back: When a sign or signal requires a stop, halt before the stop line or crosswalk and yield to pedestrians in or entering the crosswalk, whether marked or not.

sec06-card-f35.front: Compare passing rules for a dashed yellow, a solid-plus-dashed yellow pair, and double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-f35.expected_back: A dashed yellow line between opposing lanes allows passing when safe, a solid-plus-dashed pair allows passing only when the dashed line is on the driver side, and two solid lines bar passing for both sides.

sec06-card-f36.front: Into which three destinations may you safely turn across a solid yellow line?
sec06-card-f36.expected_back: A solid yellow line may be crossed to turn into a parking lot, driveway or roadway when it is safe to do so.

sec06-card-f37.front: How are reversible lanes marked on the pavement, and what must you check before entering one?
sec06-card-f37.expected_back: Reversible lanes change direction by time of day, are usually marked with double-dashed yellow lines, and require checking the signs or overhead lights before use.

sec06-card-f38.front: What do a green arrow, red X, flashing yellow X, and steady yellow X mean over a reversible lane?
sec06-card-f38.expected_back: Over a reversible lane a green arrow allows use, a red X forbids it, a flashing yellow X allows turning only, and a steady yellow X orders leaving the lane as soon as safely possible.

sec06-card-f39.front: How are reserved lanes marked, and who may use transit or bicycle lanes?
sec06-card-f39.expected_back: Reserved lanes carry signed special uses and often a white diamond, with transit or bus lanes limited to buses and bicycle lanes limited to bicycles.

sec06-card-f40.front: What controls eligibility for an HOV lane, and how many riders does an HOV 3 sign require?
sec06-card-f40.expected_back: High-occupancy lanes require the signed minimum number of people aboard during the posted days and hours, so an HOV three marking demands at least three occupants.

sec06-card-f41.front: Which maneuvers may use a shared center lane, and how are its edges painted?
sec06-card-f41.expected_back: A shared center lane serves left turns from both directions, plus U-turns where allowed, and is marked on each side by a solid-plus-dashed yellow pair.

sec06-card-f42.front: When a road has no lane signs or painted markings, what determines which lane you use?
sec06-card-f42.expected_back: Where no signs or lane markings control lane use, the default rules for driving, passing and turning decide the lane.

sec06-card-r13.front: How does line color alone tell you whether adjacent lanes move with you or toward you?
sec06-card-r13.expected_back: White lines divide lanes of traffic moving the same way, while yellow lines divide opposing traffic, so the color alone reveals the traffic pattern.

sec06-card-r14.front: How does a solid-plus-dashed yellow pair differ from two solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-r14.expected_back: A solid-plus-dashed yellow pair permits passing only from the dashed side, while two solid yellow lines forbid passing from both directions.

sec06-card-r15.front: What is the functional difference between a painted stop line and a crosswalk?
sec06-card-r15.expected_back: A stop line marks where vehicles halt for a sign or signal, while a crosswalk marks where pedestrians cross and hold priority over vehicles.

sec06-card-r16.front: How does a reserved lane differ in purpose from a reversible lane?
sec06-card-r16.expected_back: Reserved lanes restrict use to the signed vehicle types during posted times, while reversible lanes change their allowed direction of travel by time of day.

sec06-card-r17.front: How does a shared center lane's job differ from a reversible lane's job?
sec06-card-r17.expected_back: A shared center lane permits left turns from either direction, while a reversible lane carries through traffic in its currently authorized direction.

sec06-card-r18.front: Over a reversible lane, how does a flashing yellow X differ from a steady yellow X?
sec06-card-r18.expected_back: A flashing yellow X over a reversible lane allows turning movements only, while a steady yellow X orders drivers to vacate the lane as soon as safely possible.

sec07-card-f01.front: What three core habits open the Montana handbook's general driving advice before pulling into traffic?
sec07-card-f01.expected_back: Match speed to conditions, share the road courteously, and move only when safe and clear of traffic.

sec07-card-f02.front: What check precedes backing a parked car, and what must you never do in a live travel lane?
sec07-card-f02.expected_back: Walk around a parked car before reversing, and never reverse or halt in a travel lane; keep going to a safe pull-off.

sec07-card-f03.front: Which four sources of traffic authority form the Montana handbook's first rule of the road?
sec07-card-f03.expected_back: Obey officers, flaggers, traffic devices and traffic laws as the first rule of the road.

sec07-card-f04.front: How many feet ahead must you signal a turn in town compared with on a rural Montana road?
sec07-card-f04.expected_back: Signal one hundred feet before turning in town and three hundred feet before turning on rural roads.

sec07-card-f05.front: On a road with three or more lanes moving your way, where do you cruise, and when helps the center lane?
sec07-card-f05.expected_back: Keep right except to pass on roads with three or more same-direction lanes, favoring the center lane amid entering traffic.

sec07-card-f06.front: What is the safe recovery sequence if you forget to signal or miss your intended turn?
sec07-card-f06.expected_back: After a missed turn or forgotten signal, continue to the next intersection, get in position, signal, then turn.

sec07-card-f07.front: When is driving on the shoulder permitted in Montana?
sec07-card-f07.expected_back: Never drive on the shoulder unless directed to do so.

sec07-card-f08.front: How do bad road surfaces or stormy weather affect driving at the posted speed limit?
sec07-card-f08.expected_back: Obey posted limits and drop below them for bad road or weather conditions.

sec07-card-f09.front: What day-and-night interstate speed limits apply to cars and light trucks versus heavy trucks in Montana?
sec07-card-f09.expected_back: Interstates post seventy-five or eighty for cars and light trucks by day and night, with heavy trucks held to sixty-five.

sec07-card-f10.front: What speed limit applies day and night across vehicle classes on urban highways near Billings, Great Falls, and Missoula?
sec07-card-f10.expected_back: Urban-area highways post sixty-five for all listed vehicles day and night near Billings, Great Falls and Missoula.

sec07-card-f11.front: What day and night limits apply on Montana two-lane highways for cars and light trucks versus heavy trucks?
sec07-card-f11.expected_back: Two-lane highways post seventy by day and sixty-five at night for cars and light trucks, with heavy trucks at sixty days and fifty-five nights.

sec07-card-f12.front: By how much may a driver on a two-lane road briefly exceed the limit while overtaking and returning right?
sec07-card-f12.expected_back: A two-lane driver may exceed the limit by ten miles per hour while overtaking and returning safely right.

sec07-card-f13.front: Which lane or side do you use for normal safe passing on two-lane versus multi-lane roads?
sec07-card-f13.expected_back: Pass only when safe, using the left of the centerline on two-lane roads and the leftmost lane on multi-lane roads.

sec07-card-f14.front: In which two situations is passing on the right legal, and where is it strictly forbidden?
sec07-card-f14.expected_back: Passing on the right is legal only past a left-turning vehicle or on wide multi-lane pavement, never off the roadway or on the shoulder.

sec07-card-f15.front: When no turn signs or arrows control an intersection, which entry and exit lanes must you use?
sec07-card-f15.expected_back: Without turn controls, turn from the lane nearest the destination side into the nearest lane of the new road.

sec07-card-f16.front: Which two wide-arc mistakes must you avoid when making a right turn?
sec07-card-f16.expected_back: Keep right turns tight without swinging wide left first or finishing wide in the far lane.

sec07-card-f17.front: What path error must a left-turning driver avoid while leaving space for oncoming left-turners?
sec07-card-f17.expected_back: Avoid cutting left turns into approaching traffic while leaving room for oncoming left-turning vehicles.

sec07-card-f18.front: What sight distance and traffic condition are required before turning around, and where is it banned?
sec07-card-f18.expected_back: Turn around only with five hundred feet of clear view both ways and no approaching vehicles, never on busy streets, curves or hills.

sec07-card-f19.front: Which two basic conditions must be met before executing any turn?
sec07-card-f19.expected_back: No turn is made unless the vehicle is in the proper lane and the move is safe.

sec07-card-f20.front: Does Montana law grant anyone absolute right-of-way, or what duty applies to every driver?
sec07-card-f20.expected_back: The law assigns yielding duty and grants no absolute right-of-way, so every driver must act to avoid striking anyone.

sec07-card-f21.front: What special priority do blind pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog hold, and what horn rule applies?
sec07-card-f21.expected_back: Blind pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane hold absolute right-of-way; never sound the horn at them.

sec07-card-f22.front: How does driver crosswalk yielding balance with a pedestrian's duty at the curb?
sec07-card-f22.expected_back: Drivers yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, yet no pedestrian may step off the curb into a vehicle path.

sec07-card-f23.front: What visibility gear helps night walkers, and when is walking on the roadway unlawful?
sec07-card-f23.expected_back: Night walkers should wear light clothing or carry a light, and walking on the roadway is unlawful where sidewalks exist.

sec07-card-f24.front: Where sidewalks are absent, which side of the road do walkers use, and how should they cross?
sec07-card-f24.expected_back: Roadway walkers keep left facing traffic, cross at intersections using provided crosswalks, and obey applicable traffic laws.

sec07-card-r10.front: How does normal two-lane passing compare with the narrow situations allowing a right-side pass?
sec07-card-r10.expected_back: Passing left of the centerline is the two-lane norm, while passing on the right is limited to left-turning vehicles and wide multi-lane pavement.

sec07-card-r11.front: If another road user fails to yield as required, what crash-avoidance duty remains on you?
sec07-card-r11.expected_back: Right-of-way is yielded under the rules, never seized, and every driver must still act to avoid a crash.

sec07-card-r16.front: Pair Montana's town and rural turn-signal distances with the rule on shoulder driving?
sec07-card-r16.expected_back: Town turns need a one-hundred-foot signal and rural turns a three-hundred-foot signal, with the shoulder never a driving lane.

sec07-card-f25.front: Who yields when a car crosses a sidewalk at an alley, lot, or driveway, and when may cars use sidewalks?
sec07-card-f25.expected_back: Drivers crossing sidewalks or entering and leaving driveways, alleys and lots yield to pedestrians; sidewalk driving is illegal except to cross.

sec07-card-f26.front: To whom must a left-turning driver yield, and to whom must a roundabout entrant yield?
sec07-card-f26.expected_back: Left-turning drivers yield to oncoming through traffic, and circle entrants yield to traffic already circulating.

sec07-card-f27.front: Who gets priority at an uncontrolled intersection, and how should your foot and eyes prepare?
sec07-card-f27.expected_back: At uncontrolled intersections yield to the vehicle on the right, staying ready to yield by covering the brake and scanning both ways.

sec07-card-f28.front: Who proceeds first at a four-way stop, and what rule governs pulling onto a main road from a driveway?
sec07-card-f28.expected_back: At a four-way stop the first arrival goes first after a full stop; driveway and roadside entrants stop and yield to main-road traffic.

sec07-card-f29.front: When must you hold back from entering an intersection, and what does a yield sign order?
sec07-card-f29.expected_back: Never enter an intersection without room to clear it, and treat a yield sign as an order to slow and yield to all vehicles.

sec07-card-f30.front: Summarize the lane, stop, and street requirements for right on red and left on red?
sec07-card-f30.expected_back: Right on red is allowed after stopping in the proper lane when safe unless signed otherwise, as is left on red between one-way streets.

sec07-card-f31.front: When a pedestrian is in the crosswalk, when may a stopped driver complete a right turn?
sec07-card-f31.expected_back: Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks; a stopped driver turns right only when the pedestrian is in the opposite half and safe.

sec07-card-f32.front: What is strictly forbidden when a vehicle ahead of you stops at a crosswalk for a pedestrian?
sec07-card-f32.expected_back: Drivers behind a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian must not pass the stopped vehicle.

sec07-card-f33.front: What duty falls on an overtaking driver if the vehicle being passed slows down or stops?
sec07-card-f33.expected_back: An overtaking driver yields to the vehicle being passed even as it slows or stops.

sec07-card-f34.front: What three steps are required when an emergency vehicle approaches running lights and siren?
sec07-card-f34.memory_hook: Pull far right, obey PA, hold
sec07-card-f34.expected_back: Yield to siren-and-light emergency vehicles by pulling as far right as possible, obeying loudspeaker orders, and staying stopped until they pass.

sec07-card-f35.front: How far must traffic in both directions stop from a red-flashing school bus, and how do you treat yellow flashes?
sec07-card-f35.expected_back: Stop at least thirty feet from a red-flashing school bus from either direction until the lights end, slowing with care for slowing or yellow-flashing buses.

sec07-card-r12.front: How does priority at an uncontrolled crossroad differ from priority at a four-way stop?
sec07-card-r12.expected_back: An uncontrolled intersection yields to the vehicle on the right, while a four-way stop releases the first arrival after a full stop.

sec07-card-r13.front: Combine the right-turn rule for a stopped lead car with the passing ban on trailing drivers at a crosswalk?
sec07-card-r13.expected_back: A stopped driver turns right only with the pedestrian in the opposite half and safe, while following drivers must never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian.

sec07-card-f36.front: What speed habit and visual scan apply near schools during both daytime and nighttime hours?
sec07-card-f36.expected_back: Slow down and watch for children near schools day and night, checking speed on every approach.

sec07-card-f37.front: How does the Montana handbook define a legal funeral procession?
sec07-card-f37.expected_back: A funeral procession means two or more vehicles with lead and escort units, one carrying remains, traveling in daylight hours.

sec07-card-f38.front: Which four actions are prohibited for outside motorists encountering a funeral procession?
sec07-card-f38.expected_back: Drivers outside a funeral procession must yield to it and may not cut between moving procession vehicles unless police-authorized or driving an emergency vehicle, join to gain its right-of-way, pass it on the right on a multi-lane highway unless it occupies the farthest left lane, or enter an intersection on red unless doing so without crossing its path.

sec07-card-f39.front: How do intersection traffic controls apply differently to a funeral lead car versus following cars?
sec07-card-f39.expected_back: The lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, after which followers may proceed through with reasonable care for others.

sec07-card-f40.front: What spacing, highway speed cap, and lighting rules govern drivers inside a funeral procession?
sec07-card-f40.expected_back: Procession drivers follow closely, cap speed at fifty-five on fast highways and near the limit elsewhere, burn all lights, and flash signals together on first and last cars.

sec07-card-f41.front: Must drivers inside a funeral procession still yield to signaled emergency vehicles?
sec07-card-f41.expected_back: Procession drivers still yield to signaled emergency vehicles and keep due regard for every road user.

sec07-card-f42.front: How does Montana traffic law classify bicycles, and how should drivers adjust around them?
sec07-card-f42.expected_back: Bicycles count as vehicles under the traffic laws that reasonably fit, so motorists adjust for their slower travel when passing and sharing.

sec07-card-r01.front: How much clearance does Montana recommend when passing a cyclist, and what if oncoming traffic blocks you?
sec07-card-r01.expected_back: Pass a cyclist as a slow vehicle by crossing the centerline with no oncoming traffic to leave a recommended five feet, or by slowing to the cyclist pace until passing is safe.

sec07-card-r02.front: Where should you expect touring cyclists to ride, and what do single-file groups require when passing?
sec07-card-r02.expected_back: Expect cyclists off the shoulder and often in single-file groups that need extra passing time.

sec07-card-r03.front: Why do cyclists often ride eighteen to twenty-four inches inside the lane edge?
sec07-card-r03.expected_back: Cyclists ride as far right as practical, often eighteen to twenty-four inches into the lane to deter unsafe in-lane passes.

sec07-card-r04.front: What do shared-lane arrow markings guide and warn, and how do they differ from bike-lane symbols?
sec07-card-r04.expected_back: Shared-lane arrow markings guide cyclist position and warn motorists to leave room, differing from bike-lane bicycle symbols.

sec07-card-r05.front: What four duties do motorists owe cyclists regarding rights, blocking, passing, and designated bike lanes?
sec07-card-r05.expected_back: Motorists grant cyclists full vehicle rights, never deliberately block them, pass only without endangering anyone, and yield inside designated bike lanes.

sec07-card-r06.front: When do cyclists ride single file, and in which four settings is riding two abreast allowed?
sec07-card-r06.expected_back: Cyclists ride single file except on exclusive paths, when passing another bike, two abreast on shoulders or parking lanes, or two abreast on multi-lane roads without extra impedance.

sec07-card-r07.front: List the four situations when a slower cyclist may leave the right edge of the lane?
sec07-card-r07.expected_back: Slower-than-traffic cyclists keep near the right edge except when passing, preparing a left turn, dodging hazards or narrow lanes, or avoiding parked-car doors.

sec07-card-r08.front: Because most bicycles lack rearview mirrors, what should a driver assume when approaching from behind?
sec07-card-r08.expected_back: Bicycles often lack mirrors, so drivers treat an approached cyclist as unaware and proceed with extra care.

sec07-card-r09.front: Where are school bus stopping duties at railroad crossings established according to the Montana handbook?
sec07-card-r09.expected_back: School bus stopping duties at railroad crossings are set by the cited state statute.

sec07-card-r14.front: Contrast how intersection signals bind the funeral lead vehicle versus the following vehicles?
sec07-card-r14.expected_back: The funeral lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, while followers behind it may proceed through with reasonable care.

sec07-card-r15.front: Contrast how procession cars space themselves with what outside drivers are barred from doing?
sec07-card-r15.expected_back: Outsider drivers must not split or join a procession for advantage, while procession drivers follow closely without the usual spacing.

sec08-card-f01.front: Before turning right across a cyclist's lane, what must you confirm first, and why?
sec08-card-f01.expected_back: Before turning right across a cyclist in the lane, confirm the rider has yielded or passed, since bikes should pass left but often do not.

sec08-card-f02.front: How do daytime lighting rules for bicycles differ from motorcycles, and why does that matter?
sec08-card-f02.expected_back: Bicycles are hard to see and need no daytime lights, unlike motorcycles.

sec08-card-f03.front: Why must motorists use extra caution whenever children ride bicycles nearby?
sec08-card-f03.expected_back: Many young cyclists never trained or tested, so give children on bikes extra caution.

sec08-card-f04.front: Which three aggressive behaviors around cyclists must drivers avoid because they can trigger a crash?
sec08-card-f04.expected_back: Share the road respectfully without honking, shouting or swerving at cyclists, which can startle them into a crash.

sec08-card-f05.front: What front headlight color and visibility distance must a bicycle carry at night?
sec08-card-f05.expected_back: Night bicycles need a front white light visible at least five hundred feet ahead.

sec08-card-f06.front: At night, is a five-hundred-foot rear red bicycle light mandatory or optional alongside rear reflectors?
sec08-card-f06.expected_back: Rear red lights visible five hundred feet back are optional extras beside the mandatory rear reflectors.

sec08-card-f07.front: What side-visibility equipment must both bicycle wheels carry for night riding?
sec08-card-f07.expected_back: Night bicycles need reflective sidewalls or spoke reflectors on both wheels, with spoke units near the rim and visible both sides in the stated colors.

sec08-card-f08.front: How strong must a bicycle's brakes be on dry, flat, clean pavement?
sec08-card-f08.expected_back: Bicycle brakes must be strong enough to skid the wheels on dry, level, clean pavement.

sec08-card-f09.front: What tall high-visibility accessory does the Montana handbook encourage cyclists to mount for rear visibility?
sec08-card-f09.expected_back: A fluorescent orange flag six feet above the road is encouraged for visibility from behind.

sec08-card-f10.front: While treating bicycles as vehicles, which five trouble spots demand special driver scanning?
sec08-card-f10.expected_back: Treat bicycles as vehicles, watching entries, bikeways, sidewalks, turns and children darting between parked cars.

sec08-card-f11.front: What two basic placement and visibility standards must every parked vehicle meet?
sec08-card-f11.expected_back: Park clear of travel lanes and visible to approaching traffic from both directions.

sec08-card-f12.front: Where should you park when markings exist, and how do you secure the brake and transmission?
sec08-card-f12.expected_back: Use marked areas, set the brake, and leave a manual in gear or an automatic in park.

sec08-card-f13.front: What three door habits protect you and passing traffic after parking along a street?
sec08-card-f13.expected_back: Check traffic before opening doors, exit curbside when possible, and close doors promptly.

sec08-card-f14.front: What two anti-theft steps apply every time you walk away from a parked vehicle?
sec08-card-f14.expected_back: Never leave keys inside; lock up whenever leaving the vehicle.

sec08-card-f15.front: Where relative to moving traffic and the curb or shoulder edge should you position a roadway park?
sec08-card-f15.expected_back: On roadways park as far from traffic as possible, hugging the curb or the shoulder edge.

sec08-card-f16.front: Within how many inches of the curb or outer shoulder edge must a parked vehicle sit?
sec08-card-f16.expected_back: The vehicle must sit within eighteen inches of the curb or shoulder edge.

sec08-card-r01.front: Compare Montana's nighttime requirement for a front white bicycle light against a rear red light?
sec08-card-r01.expected_back: Night front bicycle lights are mandatory white, while rear red lights are optional extras beside the mandatory rear reflectors.

sec08-card-r02.front: Where do bicycle spoke reflectors mount, and which colors belong on the front versus rear wheel?
sec08-card-r02.expected_back: Spoke reflectors sit near the rim in white or amber at the front wheel and amber or red at the rear, while sidewall reflection covers the tire sides.

sec08-card-r03.front: Pair a driver's right-turn duty across a cyclist with which side cyclists should use to pass motorists?
sec08-card-r03.expected_back: A right turn across a cyclist waits for the rider to yield or pass, while a cyclist should pass motorists on the left.

sec08-card-r04.front: Why do bicyclists younger than fifteen require extra driver margin on Montana streets?
sec08-card-r04.expected_back: Many bicyclists younger than fifteen have neither taken a bicycle safety course nor passed the motor vehicle test, leaving them unaware of many road rules and requiring extra caution around young riders.

sec08-card-r05.front: Combine Montana's lane-clearance and visibility parking rule with proper roadway edge placement?
sec08-card-r05.expected_back: A parked car must clear travel lanes and stay visible both ways, while a roadway park hugs the curb or shoulder edge.

sec08-card-f17.front: What lights and headlight setting are required when parking on a roadway or shoulder at night?
sec08-card-f17.expected_back: Roadway or shoulder parking at night needs front and rear lights visible five hundred feet, with headlights dimmed.

sec08-card-f18.front: What signal and visual checks are required when leaving a parking space, especially in reverse?
sec08-card-f18.expected_back: Signal when leaving a space, scanning both ways and double-checking for vehicles, bikes and pedestrians when backing out.

sec08-card-f19.front: How do you signal and line up beside the forward car to start parallel parking?
sec08-card-f19.expected_back: Parallel parking starts with a signal, aligning beside the lead car at least two feet out with rear bumpers even.

sec08-card-f20.front: Describe the steering sequence once you reverse to the lead car's front door while parallel parking?
sec08-card-f20.expected_back: Reverse to the lead car front door, cut sharply right to a forty-five-degree angle, then swing left while backing in and straighten forward.

sec08-card-f21.front: Which way do you turn front wheels when parking downhill, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec08-card-f21.expected_back: Hill parking turns the wheels sharply roadside so a rollaway leaves traffic; downhill aims at the curb, uphill away, and curb-free uphill aims away from the street.

sec08-card-r06.front: During hours of darkness, what visibility distance and beam rule govern cars parked on shoulders?
sec08-card-r06.expected_back: Vehicles parked on a roadway or shoulder during darkness must display front and rear lights visible from five hundred feet, and any headlights left on must be dimmed.

sec08-card-r07.front: Why must backing out of a parking stall add a double-check beyond signaling and scanning traffic?
sec08-card-r07.expected_back: Leaving a space signals and scans both ways, while backing out adds a double-check for bikes and walkers.

sec08-card-r08.front: Compare wheel direction for downhill parking, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec08-card-r08.expected_back: Downhill parking aims wheels at the curb, while uphill parking aims them away, or away from the street without a curb.

sec08-card-r09.front: Put the parallel-parking alignment, right cut, and left swing into one connected sequence?
sec08-card-r09.expected_back: Parallel parking aligns two feet out with bumpers even, then cuts right to forty-five degrees before swinging left into the space.

sec08-card-f22.front: What stopping rules apply at white, yellow, and red painted curbs in Montana?
sec08-card-f22.expected_back: Curb colors limit stopping: white for passenger pickup and drop-off, yellow for attended loading, red for no stopping, standing or parking.

sec08-card-f23.front: Where around an intersection and its crosswalk or sidewalk is parking prohibited?
sec08-card-f23.expected_back: Never park inside an intersection or within twenty feet of its crosswalk or sidewalk.

sec08-card-f24.front: How does construction blockage affect parking, and how far must you park from traffic controls?
sec08-card-f24.expected_back: Never park where construction blockage results, or within thirty feet of a signal, stop sign or yield sign.

sec08-card-f25.front: How many feet must a parked car stay clear of a fire hydrant versus a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-f25.expected_back: Keep fifteen feet from fire hydrants and fifty feet from railroad crossings.

sec08-card-f26.front: Pair the eighteen-inch curb limit with fire-station driveway clearances on both sides of the street?
sec08-card-f26.expected_back: Stay within eighteen inches of the curb and clear of fire-station driveways by twenty feet same-side or seventy-five across.

sec08-card-f27.front: Which four property or sidewalk access features must a parked car never block?
sec08-card-f27.expected_back: Never block driveways, alleys, private roads or curb cuts for sidewalk access.

sec08-card-f28.front: On or inside which four elevated or enclosed roadway structures is parking banned?
sec08-card-f28.expected_back: Never park on a bridge, elevated structure, tunnel or underpass.

sec08-card-f29.front: Which three dangerous roadway positions are outlawed alongside curb parking?
sec08-card-f29.expected_back: Never park on the wrong side, alongside another parked vehicle, or on railroad tracks.

sec08-card-f30.front: What rule governs no-parking signs and marked accessible spaces without a valid permit?
sec08-card-f30.expected_back: Never park where a sign forbids it or in a marked accessible space without a permit; violations draw fines.

sec08-card-r10.front: Contrast what white, yellow, and red curbs allow or forbid in one quick summary?
sec08-card-r10.expected_back: White curbs serve passenger stops and yellow curbs attended loading, while red curbs ban every stop.

sec08-card-r11.front: Rank the required parking clearances for hydrants, crosswalks, signals or signs, and rail crossings?
sec08-card-r11.expected_back: Hydrants need fifteen feet and crossings fifty, while signals and signs need thirty and intersection crosswalks twenty.

sec08-card-r12.front: How does same-side fire-station driveway clearance compare with opposite-side clearance?
sec08-card-r12.expected_back: Same-side fire driveways need twenty feet clear, while opposite-side driveways need seventy-five.

sec08-card-f31.front: Which vehicle class is exempt from mandatory liability insurance, and what are Montana's three dollar minimums?
sec08-card-f31.expected_back: Liability insurance is mandatory except for motorcycles, at twenty-five thousand per person, fifty thousand per accident, and ten thousand for the property of others.

sec08-card-f32.front: Where must insurance evidence stay at all times, and when must you show it to officers?
sec08-card-f32.expected_back: Stopped or crashed motorists show insurance evidence to officers with license and registration, and evidence rides in the vehicle always.

sec08-card-f33.front: What fine range, jail cap, and point penalty hit a first misdemeanor uninsured-driving offense?
sec08-card-f33.expected_back: Uninsured driving is a misdemeanor: a first offense draws at least two hundred fifty up to five hundred dollars, up to ten days in jail, or both, plus five record points.

sec08-card-f34.front: What minimum fine, jail cap, and plate-registration suspension lengths hit second and third uninsured offenses?
sec08-card-f34.expected_back: Repeat uninsured driving draws at least three hundred fifty dollars or up to ten days in jail, with plate and registration suspension for ninety days, or one hundred eighty for a third or later offense.

sec08-card-f35.front: What happens if you are responsible for a crash and fail to pay damages within sixty days?
sec08-card-f35.expected_back: Crash responsibility without payment within sixty days suspends license and registration automatically until payment or six years pass, plus fresh insurance evidence.

sec08-card-f36.front: How many Montana-registered vehicles must an owner hold to qualify as a self-insurer?
sec08-card-f36.expected_back: Owners of more than twenty-five Montana-registered vehicles may qualify as self-insurers.

sec08-card-f37.front: How does Montana's financial-responsibility law treat non-resident drivers who lack adequate coverage?
sec08-card-f37.expected_back: Non-residents face the same responsibility law on adequate in-state policies, losing Montana driving privileges for noncompliance with notice to their home state.

sec08-card-f38.front: What two records does Montana's insurance verification system match, and who can check it live?
sec08-card-f38.expected_back: The insurance verification system matches registration and insurer data so officers, courts, licensing offices and the public can confirm coverage in real time.

sec08-card-r13.front: Pair how minimum liability coverage divides with where proof of insurance must stay?
sec08-card-r13.expected_back: Minimum coverage splits per person, per accident and for property, while evidence must ride along in the vehicle always.

sec08-card-r14.front: What extra penalty hits repeat uninsured drivers beyond the fines, jail, and points of a first offense?
sec08-card-r14.expected_back: A first uninsured offense draws fine or jail plus points, while repeat offenses add plate and registration suspension.

sec08-card-r15.front: Contrast who qualifies for Montana self-insurance with how non-residents meet responsibility rules?
sec08-card-r15.expected_back: Self-insurer status fits large fleets, while non-residents rely on adequate in-state policies or lose privileges.

sec08-card-r16.front: Contrast the purpose of sixty-day crash-nonpayment suspension with the insurance verification system?
sec08-card-r16.expected_back: Crash nonpayment suspends automatically for up to six years, while the verification system confirms coverage in real time.

sec09-card-f01.front: What three elements beyond reading a manual build safe driving skill?
sec09-card-f01.expected_back: No manual alone teaches driving skill; safe operation comes only through instruction, practice and applied choices.

sec09-card-f02.front: What three losses define driver distraction, and what share of driving decisions relies on vision?
sec09-card-f02.expected_back: Distraction means eyes off the road, hands off the wheel or mind off driving, while ninety percent of decisions rest on vision.

sec09-card-f03.front: How do quick glances at phones, food, passengers, controls, or drowsiness affect crash risk?
sec09-card-f03.expected_back: Crash risk rises with any side task or glance away, spanning texting, phones, food, passengers, grooming, reading, navigation, video, audio controls and fatigue.

sec09-card-f04.front: Why does Montana single out texting as the worst driving distraction?
sec09-card-f04.expected_back: Texting is the worst distraction because it combines manual, visual and cognitive load at once.

sec09-card-f05.front: How many seconds do eyes leave the road per text, and what 55 mph distance does it match?
sec09-card-f05.expected_back: A text costs five seconds of eyes-off-road, which the handbook likens to crossing a football field blindfolded at fifty-five miles per hour.

sec09-card-f06.front: What is human multitasking behind the wheel in reality, and who faces the added danger?
sec09-card-f06.expected_back: So-called multitasking is rapid single-task switching, and every distraction raises crash risk for all road users.

sec09-card-f07.front: What three phone-free habits apply to you as both a driver and a passenger?
sec09-card-f07.expected_back: Never text or call while driving, speak up as a passenger, and urge phone-free driving on others.

sec09-card-f08.front: How do most Montana cities treat phone use behind the wheel, and how should calls or texts be handled?
sec09-card-f08.expected_back: Most Montana cities ban texting and phoning while driving; handle needs only after pulling over and stopping.

sec09-card-f09.front: What four baseline safety commitments keep focus and protection intact on every drive?
sec09-card-f09.expected_back: Keep eyes on the road, hands on the wheel, everyone buckled, and alcohol out of driving.

sec09-card-r09.front: Why is texting singled out above other distractions as the most alarming?
sec09-card-r09.expected_back: Texting is singled out as the most alarming distraction because it combines visual, manual, and cognitive distraction at the same time.

sec09-card-f10.front: How should your brake, gear selector, and clutch be set when starting a manual or automatic car?
sec09-card-f10.expected_back: Start per the owner manual with the brake set, manuals out of gear with clutch as needed, and automatics in park.

sec09-card-f11.front: Why should you accelerate gently from a stop, and how should manual transmissions be shifted?
sec09-card-f11.expected_back: Accelerate gently since hard starts spin wheels and slide the car, and shift manuals without over-revving or stalling.

sec09-card-f12.front: Where on the steering wheel should your hands grip when driving a car with a wheel airbag?
sec09-card-f12.expected_back: Grip opposite sides of the wheel, such as nine-and-three or eight-and-four with wheel-mounted airbags, for comfort and control.

sec09-card-f13.front: Why should your eyes aim far down the roadway while steering?
sec09-card-f13.expected_back: Look far down the road to anticipate steering needs in time for smooth, safe moves.

sec09-card-f14.front: What steering technique applies through corners and when straightening out afterward?
sec09-card-f14.expected_back: Corner with hand-over-hand grip and straighten by hand, never palming one-handed or letting the wheel slip.

sec09-card-r10.front: Which pedal setting is shared when starting both automatic and manual vehicles?
sec09-card-r10.expected_back: Automatic starts need park and manuals need neutral with clutch as required, with the brake set in both cases.

sec09-card-f15.front: Why must you check the speedometer often, especially right after leaving a fast highway?
sec09-card-f15.expected_back: Watch the speedometer since drivers misjudge speed, especially leaving fast roads for slow local streets.

sec09-card-f16.front: How should you adjust speed relative to posted limits when pavement or weather deteriorates?
sec09-card-f16.expected_back: Follow posted limits for safety and drive below them on bad roads or weather; standard limits sit in the driving-rules chapter.

sec09-card-f17.front: Which three hazards come from slamming the brakes late instead of anticipating stops?
sec09-card-f17.expected_back: Anticipate stops early because sudden braking risks skids, lost control and rear-end hits from behind.

sec09-card-f18.front: How can easing off the gas or changing lanes early improve stopping situations?
sec09-card-f18.expected_back: Ease off or change lanes early to avoid stopping at all, or at least to stop gradually and safely.

sec09-card-f19.front: Because missed sights top crash causes, where should you scan and when should headlights assist?
sec09-card-f19.expected_back: Most driving depends on vision, and missed sights top crash causes, so scan ahead, sides and behind with headlights in poor light.

sec09-card-f20.front: What should you do whenever reading a map or task demands more than a brief glance?
sec09-card-f20.expected_back: Never look away more than a few seconds; pull over to read maps or handle anything demanding eyes.

sec09-card-f21.front: Why should you skip even hands-free calls in motion and never wear headphones or earbuds while driving?
sec09-card-f21.expected_back: Avoid phone and radio use in motion even hands-free, and never drive wearing headphones or earbuds that block horns and sirens.

sec09-card-f22.front: How should you drive past a roadside crash or patrol stop?
sec09-card-f22.expected_back: Pass roadside incidents without staring or slowing to gawk, keeping eyes ahead and clearing the scene promptly and safely.

sec09-card-f23.front: What four things does active scanning ahead, beside, and behind help you catch early?
sec09-card-f23.expected_back: Scan ahead, to the sides and behind to spot problems, road users, warning signs and direction signs early.

sec09-card-f24.front: How many seconds ahead should you scan, and what three driving benefits follow?
sec09-card-f24.expected_back: Look at least ten seconds ahead to brake and steer early, saving fuel, smoothing traffic and holding a straighter line.

sec09-card-f25.front: How far in distance does a ten-second look-ahead reach in town compared with open highways?
sec09-card-f25.expected_back: Ten seconds spans about one city block in town and about four blocks or a quarter mile on highways.

sec09-card-f26.front: Why must your eyes keep sweeping to both sides, especially near intersections and rail tracks?
sec09-card-f26.expected_back: Search the sides constantly since crossings can appear anywhere, especially at intersections and railroad tracks.

sec09-card-f27.front: What counts as an intersection, and where must you look before entering or pulling out?
sec09-card-f27.expected_back: Intersections include any merging or crossing point; look left, right and across before entering or starting.

sec09-card-f28.front: What three checks belong before turning left across oncoming traffic, and when is one-way left on red legal?
sec09-card-f28.expected_back: Left across oncoming traffic needs a safe gap, a clear destination street, and one last oncoming check; one-way to one-way lefts are allowed unless barred.

sec09-card-f29.front: What conflicts and walkers must you check before turning right, and when is right on red allowed?
sec09-card-f29.expected_back: Right turns need clear left and no conflicting oncoming lefts, plus a pedestrian check; right on red is allowed unless barred.

sec09-card-f30.front: Why is scanning cross traffic vital right after your traffic light turns green?
sec09-card-f30.expected_back: Never trust signals to stop cross traffic; watch for red-light runners, especially just after green.

sec09-card-f31.front: How should you proceed from a stop when parked cars, hedges, or buildings hide cross-street traffic?
sec09-card-f31.expected_back: If stopped at an intersection with a blocked cross-street view, edge forward slowly until crossing traffic can be seen, allowing crossing drivers to see the vehicle front and warn if needed.

sec09-card-f32.front: Why must you scan road edges closely near storefronts, parking lots, work zones, playgrounds, and schools?
sec09-card-f32.expected_back: Scan sides near shops, lots, work zones, sidewalks, playgrounds and school yards where entries are likely.

sec09-card-f33.front: Why must you wait after a train passes on multi-track railroad crossings?
sec09-card-f33.expected_back: Look up and down every rail crossing without assuming no train; at multi-track crossings wait until the passed train clears in case another hides behind it.

sec09-card-f34.front: During which five driving situations is checking mirrors behind you especially critical?
sec09-card-f34.expected_back: Check behind often, especially in heavy traffic and before lane changes, slowdowns, backing or long downhill runs.

sec09-card-f35.front: What space must you confirm is clear before changing lanes, merging, or pulling out from a curb?
sec09-card-f35.expected_back: Lane changes, merges and curb entries all require confirming the target lane is empty beside and behind.

sec09-card-f36.front: In what order do you signal, use mirrors, and check blind spots for a lane change?
sec09-card-f36.expected_back: Signal the lane change, clear mirrors for occupants and passers, then check the blind spot over the shoulder.

sec09-card-f37.front: How long should blind-spot glances take, and what should you recheck right before steering over?
sec09-card-f37.expected_back: Glance quickly without leaving the road ahead, rechecking mirrors and the blind spot just before moving.

sec09-card-f38.front: Why scan the far lane and curb edges for bikes, motorcycles, and walkers during a lane change?
sec09-card-f38.expected_back: Check the far lane for converging drivers and watch for hard-to-see bikes, motorcycles and pedestrians, especially entering from curbs or driveways.

sec09-card-f39.front: When is checking your rearview mirror during a slowdown most urgent?
sec09-card-f39.expected_back: Check behind on every slowdown, particularly sudden ones or where followers least expect braking.

sec09-card-f40.front: What three steps belong before pulling out from a curb into traffic?
sec09-card-f40.expected_back: Leave the curb with a signal, a left-shoulder look, and a safe gap.

sec09-card-r01.front: How do you measure your look-ahead interval in seconds using a roadside object?
sec09-card-r01.expected_back: Time the gap by counting thousand-seconds to a fixed object; the count equals seconds of looking ahead.

sec09-card-r02.front: How do early speed or lane adjustments benefit drivers behind you?
sec09-card-r02.expected_back: Early moves give followers more reaction time, keeping traffic steady and safer for everyone behind.

sec09-card-r11.front: What distinct roles do your speedometer and posted speed signs play?
sec09-card-r11.expected_back: Speedometers correct misjudged speed, while posted limits set the ceiling that bad conditions lower.

sec09-card-r12.front: Why does a plain green light never excuse skipping your left-and-right intersection scan?
sec09-card-r12.expected_back: A plain green never excuses skipping the left-right check, since cross traffic may run its red.

sec09-card-r13.front: What do mirrors clear versus what only an over-the-shoulder glance clears?
sec09-card-r13.expected_back: Mirrors clear the lanes beside and behind, while only an over-shoulder look clears the blind spot.

sec09-card-r14.front: Why does ten seconds equal one city block in town yet four blocks or a quarter mile on highways?
sec09-card-r14.expected_back: A city ten-seconds means watching one block ahead, while a highway ten-seconds means four blocks or a quarter mile.

sec09-card-r15.front: Aside from allowed one-way-to-one-way lefts, what two conditions govern turning left across oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-r15.expected_back: One-way to one-way lefts are allowed unless barred, while lefts across oncoming traffic need a safe gap and clear exit.

sec09-card-r16.front: How do headphones worsen risk beyond the mental distraction already caused by hands-free calling?
sec09-card-r16.expected_back: Hands-free calling still steals attention like hand-held use, while headphones additionally block emergency sound.

sec09-card-f41.front: Because vision drops at night while still guiding ninety percent of decisions, what must you do with speed?
sec09-card-f41.expected_back: Night vision falls while ninety percent of decisions still need sight, so slow down for road, car and weather conditions.

sec09-card-f42.front: During what night hours and what visibility distance must headlights be turned on?
sec09-card-f42.expected_back: Burn headlights from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles vanish inside five hundred feet.

sec09-card-f43.front: What reach distances apply to upper and lower beams, and at what oncoming and following distances must you dim?
sec09-card-f43.memory_hook: Three fifty hundred thousand five hundred
sec09-card-f43.expected_back: Upper beams must reveal people and vehicles three hundred fifty feet out and lower beams one hundred feet; dim within one thousand feet of oncoming traffic and five hundred behind followed vehicles.

sec09-card-f44.front: Where should you look when meeting bright oncoming lights at night, and what if another driver flashes you?
sec09-card-f44.expected_back: Meet night traffic by watching the right road edge instead of the beams, and check the dimmer when flashed.

sec09-card-r03.front: How can parking choice cut down reversing, and what should you check before climbing inside?
sec09-card-r03.expected_back: Back up as little as possible, favoring drive-through spaces; check behind before entering since children and small objects hide from the seat.

sec09-card-r04.front: How should you position your body and eyes while backing up, and what outside help helps?
sec09-card-r04.expected_back: Reverse slowly while looking through the rear window with an arm over the seatback, never trusting mirrors alone, and use a guide outside when possible.

sec09-card-r05.front: What rules govern driving on parking lights, using spotlights near traffic, and driving at dusk or overcast?
sec09-card-r05.expected_back: Never drive on parking lights alone, and douse spotlights for approaching vehicles; at dusk or overcast, switch headlights on.

sec09-card-r06.front: How much night vision can tinted or photo-gray lenses steal after sunset?
sec09-card-r06.expected_back: Tinted and photo-gray lenses can steal up to thirty percent of night vision, so treat them with caution after dark.

sec09-card-r07.front: In what order should you slow, steer, park, and set lights during a nighttime tire failure or breakdown?
sec09-card-r07.expected_back: With breakdowns or tire failure, slow gently, regain control before leaving the lane, then pull as far right as safely possible with parking lights on and headlights dimmed at night.

sec09-card-r08.front: How often should you take breaks on long night drives, and what must you do if drowsy?
sec09-card-r08.expected_back: Limit long night drives, breaking at least every two hours for air and alertness, and nap or lodge when drowsy rather than pressing on.

sec02-card-f01.question_text: What three stages make up Montana graduated driver licensing for teens under eighteen?
sec02-card-f01.teaching_text: Graduated licensing builds skill step by step before granting solo unrestricted highway privileges.

sec02-card-f02.question_text: How many total and nighttime practice hours over what minimum period must teen permit holders complete?
sec02-card-f02.teaching_text: Cramming fifty practice hours into one summer month still leaves five months left on the calendar clock.
sec02-card-f02.must_match_memory_hook: Fifty hours ten night six months

visual_sync.text_span: Fifty hours ten night six months

sec02-card-f03.question_text: Who may supervise a learner-permit driver under Montana graduated licensing?
sec02-card-f03.teaching_text: Riding with an unlicensed relative or peer without parental authorization breaks graduated supervision law.

sec02-card-f04.question_text: Who must wear a seatbelt when riding with a graduated-program instruction-permit driver?
sec02-card-f04.teaching_text: Even one unbuckled back-seat passenger violates graduated-permit rules and puts the teen driver on the hook.

sec02-card-f05.question_text: What six-month driving and substance record is required to advance to a restricted license?
sec02-card-f05.teaching_text: Catching a traffic ticket or alcohol-or-drug offense resets your six-month clean-record countdown toward stage two.

sec02-card-f06.question_text: Which driver-license test must a teen pass as a learner-permit prerequisite?
sec02-card-f06.teaching_text: Mastering road signs and right-of-way rules comes first before taking a vehicle onto public streets.

sec02-card-f07.question_text: What must a teen applying for a Montana learner permit do with other driver licenses?
sec02-card-f07.teaching_text: Holding onto an out-of-state credential violates Montana single-license rules even at the teen permit stage.

sec02-card-f08.question_text: What health prerequisite applies to a teen seeking a Montana learner permit?
sec02-card-f08.teaching_text: Vision or medical conditions affecting safe control are screened right at permit entry rather than waiting.

sec02-card-f09.question_text: Which court findings bar a teen applicant from getting a Montana learner permit?
sec02-card-f09.teaching_text: Adjudicated mental incompetence, chronic alcohol dependence, or habitual illegal narcotics findings block teen permits just like adult licenses.

sec02-card-f10.question_text: Under what course condition can a teen get a learner permit at fourteen and a half?
sec02-card-f10.teaching_text: Only active participation in or completion of state-approved traffic education opens the fourteen-and-a-half pathway.

sec02-card-f11.question_text: Does online traffic education count as an approved course for Montana teen learner-permit routes?
sec02-card-f11.teaching_text: Finishing a web-only driver course leaves fifteen-year-olds ineligible until completing in-person state-approved education or turning sixteen.

sec02-card-f12.question_text: At what ages can a teen obtain an exam-station learner permit with versus without approved traffic education?
sec02-card-f12.teaching_text: Completing state-approved traffic education shaves a full year off the exam-station learner-permit age minimum.

sec02-card-f13.question_text: How long must a teen under eighteen hold a learner permit before seeking a restricted license?
sec02-card-f13.teaching_text: A gap or suspension breaks continuity because all six learner-permit months must run back to back.

sec02-card-f14.question_text: How long is a Montana teen learner license valid?
sec02-card-f14.teaching_text: Letting your learner license expire past twelve months forces reapplication before completing your road test.

sec02-card-f15.question_text: Which signed certification form must accompany fees and stage-one completion when applying for a restricted license?
sec02-card-f15.teaching_text: Examiners cannot issue a restricted credential unless an authorized adult certifies your supervised practice hours in writing.

sec02-card-f16.question_text: Where does a Montana first-year restricted license display its restriction code?
