sec02-card-f16.teaching_text: Both sides carry the restriction marker so officers immediately spot first-year graduated rules during stops.

sec02-card-f17.question_text: Who must wear a seatbelt whenever a teen drives on a first-year restricted license?
sec02-card-f17.teaching_text: Mandatory full-cabin buckling carries straight over from your learner permit through the entire restricted year.

sec02-card-f18.question_text: Between what nighttime hours is a restricted-license teenager barred from driving without an authorized exception?
sec02-card-f18.teaching_text: Late-night crash rates spike sharply for new solo drivers, making eleven at night until five in the morning off-limits.

sec02-card-f19.question_text: Which trips qualify as nighttime curfew exceptions for a restricted-license teen?
sec02-card-f19.teaching_text: Specific parent-authorized errands plus work, school, church, farm, or emergency needs are the only legal late-night exceptions.

sec02-card-f20.question_text: How may law enforcement verify a restricted-license teen reason for driving during curfew hours?
sec02-card-f20.teaching_text: Claiming parental permission at two in the morning invites a roadside phone call directly to your parent or guardian.

sec02-card-f21.question_text: How many unrelated passengers under eighteen may ride during the first six restricted months without adult supervision?
sec02-card-f21.teaching_text: Every extra teen peer multiplies distraction risk during your very first six months of solo driving.

sec02-card-f22.question_text: How many unrelated passengers under eighteen may ride during the second six restricted months without adult supervision?
sec02-card-f22.teaching_text: Months seven through twelve expand your solo peer limit from one to three unrelated passengers under eighteen.

sec02-card-f23.question_text: What penalty applies the first time a teen breaks a first-year license restriction?
sec02-card-f23.teaching_text: Breaking curfew or passenger limits even once assigns mandatory community service up to sixty hours.

sec02-card-f24.question_text: What happens after a second violation of a first-year license restriction?
sec02-card-f24.teaching_text: A second curfew or passenger slip parks your solo driving privileges completely for half a year.

sec02-card-f25.question_text: When do Montana first-year graduated license restrictions end automatically?
sec02-card-f25.teaching_text: No extra station visit is required because restrictions lift automatically at whichever milestone arrives first.

sec02-card-f26.question_text: How long does a driver-license receipt last, and how many exam attempts does it allow?
sec02-card-f26.teaching_text: Burning through three failed tries or twelve calendar months consumes the entire value of your application receipt.

sec02-card-f27.question_text: Can a Montana driver-license testing receipt be renewed?
sec02-card-f27.teaching_text: Waiting until month twelve leaves zero extension options since testing receipts cannot be renewed.

sec02-card-f28.question_text: What happens if an applicant has not finished licensing after one year on a receipt?
sec02-card-f28.teaching_text: Missing the one-year finish line resets fees, paperwork, and testing right back to square one.

sec02-card-r01.question_text: How far ahead of expiration may a Montana driver start license renewal?
sec02-card-r01.teaching_text: Renewing inside the six-month pre-expiration window avoids last-minute appointment crunches or accidental lapse.

sec02-card-r02.question_text: May you legally drive on an expired license during the window when renewal without retesting remains open?
sec02-card-r02.teaching_text: Drivers often mistake the post-expiration retest waiver year for a grace period to keep driving legally.

sec02-card-r03.question_text: Within how long after expiration can a Montana license be renewed without retesting?
sec02-card-r03.teaching_text: While you cannot drive until renewed, completing renewal within twelve months avoids repeating written and road exams.

sec02-card-r04.question_text: What is required once a Montana license has been expired for more than one year?
sec02-card-r04.teaching_text: Letting expiration pass one full year turns renewal into a brand-new driver application with full testing.

sec02-card-r05.question_text: Which federal records must match the full legal name and birth date on a license or ID application?
sec02-card-r05.teaching_text: Updating your name after marriage or court action with Social Security first prevents station verification rejections.

sec02-card-r06.question_text: Which five items make up the standard Montana exam-station license renewal procedure?
sec02-card-r06.teaching_text: In-station renewals check your eyesight and capture an updated portrait alongside identification and fee payment.

sec02-card-r07.question_text: What extra exams can apply at renewal when safe-driving functional ability is in doubt?
sec02-card-r07.teaching_text: Examiners can add knowledge and road evaluations at renewal whenever health changes raise safety questions.

sec02-card-r08.question_text: How does a suspension or revocation in Montana or elsewhere affect applying for or keeping a license?
sec02-card-r08.teaching_text: Unresolved sanctions anywhere in the country block issuance, renewal, and retention of Montana driving privileges.

sec02-card-r09.question_text: What is required at a local licensing station to replace a lost or destroyed Montana license?
sec02-card-r09.teaching_text: Station staff must re-verify your full legal name and birth date before printing a replacement credential.

sec02-card-r10.question_text: Whom must a Montana driver notify after moving, and within how many days?
sec02-card-r10.teaching_text: Missing the ten-day reporting window keeps renewal and legal notices going to an outdated address.

sec02-card-r11.question_text: What two steps are required to change the legal name on a Montana driver license?
sec02-card-r11.teaching_text: Verbal updates never change a state credential without both an application and legal name-change paperwork.

sec02-card-r12.question_text: Which marriage record qualifies to change the legal name on a Montana license?
sec02-card-r12.teaching_text: Uncertified keepsake certificates fail counter review because only government-certified marriage records authorize name updates.

sec02-card-r13.question_text: Which general court record qualifies to update the name on a Montana license?
sec02-card-r13.teaching_text: A competent court certified judgment explicitly granting the new legal name satisfies state licensing requirements.

sec02-card-r14.question_text: When does a certified divorce or dissolution decree qualify as a license name-change document?
sec02-card-r14.teaching_text: A dissolution decree that never mentions restoring or changing your surname cannot alter your driver license.

sec02-card-r15.question_text: Which certified USCIS naturalization form numbers qualify as Montana license name-change documents?
sec02-card-r15.teaching_text: Applicants who legally changed names during naturalization prove it using certified form N-550 or N-570.
sec02-card-r15.must_match_memory_hook: Certified N five fifty or seventy

visual_sync.text_span: Certified N five fifty or seventy

sec02-card-r16.question_text: Which agency records must match the name and birth date used for a Montana license name change?
sec02-card-r16.teaching_text: Visiting Driver Services before Social Security updates its file stalls your license name change immediately.

sec03-card-f01.question_text: What personal readiness check should you make before starting any drive?
sec03-card-f01.teaching_text: Fatigue, illness, or emotional distraction degrades reaction time before your tires ever touch public pavement.

sec03-card-f02.question_text: Who bears legal responsibility for making sure a vehicle is safe to operate?
sec03-card-f02.teaching_text: Blaming the vehicle owner will not excuse a driver who takes a mechanically unsafe car onto traffic lanes.

sec03-card-f03.question_text: What guide governs routine vehicle care, and who should handle repairs beyond your skill?
sec03-card-f03.teaching_text: Guessing on complex brake or steering repairs creates roadside hazards when a trained technician is needed.

sec03-card-f04.question_text: What action is called for by brake noise, a strange brake odor, or a pedal sinking to the floor?
sec03-card-f04.teaching_text: Grinding noises, burning smells, or a sinking pedal warn of impending stopping failure before a highway emergency.

sec03-card-f05.question_text: From where should you verify turn signals, brake lamps, taillamps, and headlights?
sec03-card-f05.teaching_text: Dashboard indicator blinks can miss a burned-out rear bulb unless someone checks outside the car.

sec03-card-f06.question_text: What message do your brake lamps send to drivers behind you?
sec03-card-f06.teaching_text: Working rear brake lights give trailing traffic instant visual warning before closing distance disappears.

sec03-card-f07.question_text: What driving intention do your turn signals communicate to surrounding road users?
sec03-card-f07.teaching_text: Flashing your directional lamps early lets nearby drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your path change.

sec03-card-f08.question_text: Why should drivers run headlights in daylight as well as darkness?
sec03-card-f08.teaching_text: Lit headlamps help oncoming drivers spot your approaching car against bright glare, shade, or rural pavement.

sec03-card-f09.question_text: What should a mechanic inspect if night vision feels poor or oncoming drivers keep flashing high beams at you?
sec03-card-f09.teaching_text: Misaligned headlamps simultaneously starve your lane of light and blind oncoming traffic even on low beam.

sec03-card-f10.question_text: Which three planning habits help cut down total driving miles?
sec03-card-f10.teaching_text: Bundling stops or sharing rides trims fuel costs, congestion exposure, and unnecessary roadway miles.

sec03-card-f11.question_text: What benefit comes from routing or timing trips to avoid heavy traffic?
sec03-card-f11.teaching_text: Stop-and-go gridlock drains driver concentration quickly while putting extra heat and wear on brakes, tires, and drivetrains.

sec03-card-f12.question_text: What quick step prevents wasted pickup trips before heading out?
sec03-card-f12.teaching_text: One thirty-second phone call saves an entire round trip when an order or part is delayed.

sec03-card-f13.question_text: For what two safety reasons should damaged windshield glass be replaced?
sec03-card-f13.teaching_text: Chips and cracks scatter glare across your sightline while weakening structural glass strength in minor impacts.

sec03-card-f14.question_text: When should windshield wiper blades be replaced?
sec03-card-f14.teaching_text: Hardened rubber smears rain and snow into an opaque blur right when storm visibility matters most.

sec03-card-f15.question_text: How much glass must you clear of snow and ice before driving?
sec03-card-f15.teaching_text: Scraping a tiny peephole leaves huge blind spots around intersections, lane changes, and crosswalks.

sec03-card-f16.question_text: How do worn or bald tires change stopping and turning on wet pavement?
sec03-card-f16.teaching_text: Without deep grooves to channel water away, slick rubber slides forward when braking or cornering in rain.

sec03-card-f17.question_text: What four problems come from low tire pressure or unbalanced wheels?
sec03-card-f17.teaching_text: Underinflated or unbalanced tires burn extra gas, chew tread uneven, and degrade steering and braking response.

sec03-card-f18.question_text: What does bouncing, steering-wheel vibration, or pulling to one side call for?
sec03-card-f18.teaching_text: Wheel shimmy or sideways drift warns of alignment, tire, or suspension faults needing professional inspection.

sec03-card-f19.question_text: Which two major highway hazards become likelier with worn tires?
sec03-card-f19.teaching_text: Thinning rubber both rides up on standing water films and ruptures easily under highway heat.

sec03-card-f20.question_text: When should you measure tire pressure with a gauge, and where is the target pressure listed?
sec03-card-f20.teaching_text: Driving heats air inside tires and skews readings upward compared to cold owner-manual specifications.

sec03-card-f21.question_text: How do you run the penny tread check, and what result means replacing the tire?
sec03-card-f21.teaching_text: Seeing all of Lincoln's head upside down proves tread depth is too shallow for safe wet grip.

sec03-card-f22.question_text: What should you do if steering feels stiff or lags when the wheel first turns?
sec03-card-f22.teaching_text: Dead play or heavy resistance at the wheel signals worn linkage or power-steering trouble before total loss.

sec03-card-f23.question_text: Which system needs a mechanic inspection if the vehicle keeps bouncing after a bump or stop?
sec03-card-f23.teaching_text: Worn shocks or struts let tires hop off pavement, hurting steering grip and lengthening stops.

sec03-card-f24.question_text: What three jobs does a vehicle exhaust system perform?
sec03-card-f24.teaching_text: Intact pipes and mufflers carry toxic combustion gases out back while taming engine roar and heat.

sec03-card-f25.question_text: What two dangers make leaking exhaust fumes an urgent cabin threat?
sec03-card-f25.teaching_text: Odorless carbon monoxide seeps into cabins silently, making drivers sleepy right before turning lethal.

sec03-card-f26.question_text: What rule applies to running a vehicle engine inside a garage?
sec03-card-f26.teaching_text: Deadly exhaust builds up inside enclosed stalls within minutes, even when warming up briefly.

sec03-card-f27.question_text: What window precaution applies when sitting inside a parked car with the engine running?
sec03-card-f27.teaching_text: Sitting sealed inside an idling car lets invisible exhaust gases accumulate without fresh outside airflow.

sec03-card-f28.question_text: When should detected vehicle exhaust leaks be repaired?
sec03-card-f28.teaching_text: Putting off a noisy or rusted exhaust repair invites poisonous fumes straight through floorboard seams.

sec03-card-f29.question_text: What three operational problems can an out-of-tune engine cause?
sec03-card-f29.teaching_text: Losing power mid-pass or stalling across an intersection turns skipped engine care into a collision hazard.

sec03-card-f30.question_text: Why must items on the rear shelf or back seat be secured?
sec03-card-f30.teaching_text: Hard braking launches unsecured backpacks, tools, or electronics forward at highway speed toward cabin occupants.

sec03-card-f31.question_text: Why must loose objects stay off the floor near the driver pedals?
sec03-card-f31.teaching_text: A dropped water bottle wedging beneath your brake pedal can block stopping altogether in an emergency.

sec03-card-f32.question_text: For what sole purpose should a vehicle horn be sounded?
sec03-card-f32.teaching_text: Honking out of frustration or greeting distracts nearby traffic instead of alerting someone to real danger.

sec03-card-f33.question_text: On post-1956 vehicles, what colors and visibility distance apply to required front and rear lighting?
sec03-card-f33.teaching_text: Distinct front and rear colors visible five hundred feet away tell drivers instantly which way traffic faces.
sec03-card-f33.must_match_memory_hook: White amber front red amber rear

visual_sync.text_span: White amber front red amber rear

sec03-card-f34.question_text: When is colored covering or tinting forbidden on headlights and taillights?
sec03-card-f34.teaching_text: Darkened lens covers slash beam brightness and remain illegal unless built as federally compliant manufacturer equipment.

sec03-card-f35.question_text: At what minimum distance ahead should high-beam headlights reveal people or vehicles?
sec03-card-f35.teaching_text: Three hundred fifty feet of open-road reach gives crucial stopping margin on dark rural Montana highways.

sec03-card-f36.question_text: At what minimum distance ahead should low-beam headlights reveal people or vehicles?
sec03-card-f36.teaching_text: Dropping to low beams cuts forward illumination to roughly one hundred feet, requiring steadier night speeds.

sec03-card-f37.question_text: At what distance from an approaching oncoming vehicle must you dim high-beam headlights?
sec03-card-f37.teaching_text: Waiting closer than one thousand feet blinds oncoming drivers on two-lane highways right as cars converge.

sec03-card-f38.question_text: At what distance behind a vehicle you are overtaking must you dim high beams?
sec03-card-f38.teaching_text: High beams inside five hundred feet bounce straight off rearview mirrors and dazzle the driver ahead.

sec03-card-f39.question_text: Between what sunset and sunrise times must Montana drivers run headlights?
sec03-card-f39.teaching_text: Parking lights alone never count once thirty minutes past sunset begins until thirty minutes before sunrise.

sec03-card-f40.question_text: Below what visibility distance in weather or blowing dust are headlights required?
sec03-card-f40.teaching_text: Snow squalls, fog, or prairie dust below five hundred feet hide grey cars unless headlamps shine.

sec03-card-f41.question_text: Which vehicles may legally use flashing or pulsating lights other than turn signals?
sec03-card-f41.teaching_text: Strobe or pulsing lights on personal cars confuse motorists who reserve flashing signals for emergency response.

sec03-card-f42.question_text: What motions and colors are barred for decorative undercarriage lighting?
sec03-card-f42.teaching_text: Rotating, flashing, oscillating, or police-colored underglow mimics patrol cruisers and draws immediate equipment citations.

sec03-card-f43.question_text: On post-1956 vehicles, what colors and sunlight visibility distance apply to turn signals?
sec03-card-f43.teaching_text: Bright sunlight washes out weak bulbs, so directional lamps must stay clear from three hundred feet.

sec03-card-f44.question_text: Which two steering-post measurements make mechanical or electrical signal lamps mandatory?
sec03-card-f44.teaching_text: Wide cabs or long cargo beds hide a driver's arm, making lamp turn signals essential.
sec03-card-f44.must_match_memory_hook: Over twenty four inches fourteen feet

visual_sync.text_span: Over twenty four inches fourteen feet

sec03-card-f45.question_text: Which two vehicle actions do brake lamps signal?
sec03-card-f45.teaching_text: Even gentle brake taps light up rear lamps to warn trailing traffic you are losing speed.

sec03-card-f46.question_text: On post-1956 vehicles, what colors and normal-sunlight distance apply to brake lights?
sec03-card-f46.teaching_text: High-noon glare hides dim brake bulbs unless red or amber lenses shine three hundred feet back.

sec03-card-f47.question_text: What color and rear visibility distance are required for license-plate lighting on post-1956 vehicles?
sec03-card-f47.teaching_text: Burned-out rear tag bulbs are one of the most common nighttime traffic-stop triggers.

sec03-card-f48.question_text: How does Montana treat aftermarket rear plate lighting compared with original manufacturer equipment?
sec03-card-f48.teaching_text: Swapping stock tag bulbs for colored or aftermarket novelty frames violates Montana equipment law.

sec03-card-f49.question_text: What sound condition must every vehicle muffler prevent?
sec03-card-f49.teaching_text: Cutouts, straight pipes, or blown baffles violate muffler rules against unusual or excessive exhaust roar.

sec03-card-f50.question_text: How far behind must a mirror show on vehicles manufactured after January 1, 1956?
sec03-card-f50.teaching_text: Stacking cargo to the ceiling requires usable side mirrors that still preserve two hundred feet rearward.

sec03-card-f51.question_text: What three things must service and parking brakes do across operating loads and grades?
sec03-card-f51.teaching_text: Mountain passes test both service brakes descending hills and parking brakes holding heavy loads stationary.

sec03-card-f52.question_text: From what minimum distance must a required vehicle horn be audible?
sec03-card-f52.teaching_text: A weak horn cannot alert highway drivers ahead unless clearly heard at least two hundred feet away.

sec03-card-r01.question_text: What parking-light colors and visibility distance apply when stopped or parked on a roadway during headlamp hours?
sec03-card-r01.teaching_text: Unlit cars parked along dark road edges invite rear-end crashes without five-hundred-foot parking lamps.

sec03-card-r02.question_text: What front glass is required on motor vehicles, and which ones require safety glass?
sec03-card-r02.teaching_text: Laminated safety glass resists shattering into jagged shards on vehicles built after January 1, 1956.
sec03-card-r02.must_match_memory_hook: Front windshield post fifty six safety

visual_sync.text_span: Front windshield post fifty six safety

sec03-card-r03.question_text: What condition must a motor vehicle windshield always maintain?
sec03-card-r03.teaching_text: Spiderweb cracks, heavy grime, or haze across your sightline compromise hazard detection and violate equipment rules.

sec03-card-r04.question_text: When is attaching stickers, posters, or other material to any vehicle window prohibited?
sec03-card-r04.teaching_text: Stickers or shades that shrink side or rear visibility hide cyclists and cross traffic.

sec03-card-r05.question_text: What must required windshield wipers be capable of clearing?
sec03-card-r05.teaching_text: Broken wiper motors or missing arms leave you blind the instant rain, sleet, or road spray hits.

sec03-card-r06.question_text: Which seating positions require belts on vehicles built between January 1, 1965 and January 1, 1968?
sec03-card-r06.teaching_text: Mid-sixties classics must maintain restraints at both outer front positions even without rear-seat anchors.

sec03-card-r07.question_text: Which positions require seatbelts on vehicles manufactured after January 1, 1968?
sec03-card-r07.teaching_text: Removing rear buckles in modern cars breaks equipment law covering every designated seating spot.

sec03-card-r08.question_text: In what mechanical state must required vehicle seatbelts be kept?
sec03-card-r08.teaching_text: Frayed webbing or jammed latches fail crash loads and leave occupants legally unrestrained.

sec03-card-r09.question_text: What occupant restraint condition must be met before a driver operates on Montana roads?
sec03-card-r09.teaching_text: Putting a car in drive while any passenger sits unbuckled or slack-belted violates Montana law.

sec03-card-r10.question_text: How many clearance lamps and where go on buses or trucks over 80 inches wide and heavy wide trailers?
sec03-card-r10.teaching_text: Corner clearance lamps mark full vehicle width over eighty inches so oncoming cars avoid sideswipes.

sec03-card-r11.question_text: Where are clearance lamps required on a truck tractor?
sec03-card-r11.teaching_text: Cab-front clearance lamps outline tractor width ahead even when running bobtail or pulling trailers.

sec03-card-r12.question_text: Where must clearance lamps be placed on a pole trailer over three thousand pounds gross weight?
sec03-card-r12.teaching_text: Side-mounted clearance markers keep long utility-pole or log loads visible from either flank.

sec03-card-r13.question_text: Which four vehicle types are exempt from the post-1956 requirement for two rear taillamps?
sec03-card-r13.teaching_text: Narrow cycle frames and bobtail tractors follow separate rear-lamp rules instead of standard dual taillamps.

sec03-card-r14.question_text: What colors and visibility distance apply to required vehicle clearance lamps?
sec03-card-r14.teaching_text: Amber forward-and-side markers paired with red rear lamps orient night drivers from five hundred feet.

sec03-card-r15.question_text: During headlamp hours, what marker belongs on a load extending four feet or more past the rear body?
sec03-card-r15.teaching_text: Unlit lumber or pipe sticking four feet out back disappears in darkness until trailing cars hit it.

sec03-card-r16.question_text: When headlamps are not required, what marker belongs on a rear load extending four feet or more?
sec03-card-r16.teaching_text: Bright red cloth at least twelve inches square alerts daytime drivers before misjudging your cargo overhang.

sec03-card-r17.question_text: What front and rear lights must a farm tractor or implement show on highways during headlamp hours?
sec03-card-r17.teaching_text: Five-hundred-foot white front and red rear lamps keep slow rural machinery visible after dusk.

sec03-card-r18.question_text: Which outer edge must required farm-vehicle lighting mark?
sec03-card-r18.teaching_text: Wide plows or headers jutting toward the centerline clip passing cars unless lit at their left edge.

sec03-card-r19.question_text: How many combined spot or auxiliary fog lamps may a vehicle carry at most?
sec03-card-r19.teaching_text: Stacking rows of extra auxiliary lights exceeds Montana's two-lamp cap on spot and fog units.

sec03-card-r20.question_text: What must you do with spot lamps when approaching another moving vehicle from either direction?
sec03-card-r20.teaching_text: Focused spot beams blind both oncoming traffic and drivers ahead through mirrors.

sec03-card-r21.question_text: Under what beam-strength limit may fog lamps run alongside low-beam headlights?
sec03-card-r21.teaching_text: Overpowered fog lights scatter blinding glare back off mist and dazzle oncoming motorists.

sec03-card-r22.question_text: When do trailers, semitrailers, or pole trailers require separation-activated break-away brakes?
sec03-card-r22.teaching_text: Automatic break-away braking stops a runaway heavy or air-braked trailer if a hitch fails.
sec03-card-r22.must_match_memory_hook: Air vacuum or over three thousand

visual_sync.text_span: Air vacuum or over three thousand

sec03-card-r23.question_text: How must vehicle brakes be maintained and adjusted across the wheels?
sec03-card-r23.teaching_text: Uneven brake grab jerks a car sideways into oncoming lanes or spins during hard stops.

sec03-card-r24.question_text: Which vehicles are allowed an exception to the ban on sirens, whistles, and bells?
sec03-card-r24.teaching_text: Keeping sirens, bells, and whistles exclusive to emergency responders ensures surrounding drivers yield right-of-way without hesitation.

sec03-card-r25.question_text: What front backup connection is required on a trailer weighing three thousand pounds gross or less?
sec03-card-r25.teaching_text: A quarter-inch minimum steel link or cable catches light trailers right at the tongue if a hitch pops loose.

sec03-card-r26.question_text: Which three heavy vehicle types must carry specified roadside warning equipment?
sec03-card-r26.teaching_text: Large trucks, passenger buses, and tractors block lanes badly when disabled and need onboard warning kits.

sec03-card-r27.question_text: What flame-free kit meeting federal standard 125 can replace older roadside warning sets?
sec03-card-r27.teaching_text: Three compliant reflective triangles alert highway traffic cleanly without open sparks, fuel, or batteries.

sec03-card-r28.question_text: Which warning devices may never be carried on explosive, flammable-liquid, or compressed-gas vehicles?
sec03-card-r28.teaching_text: Even storing open-flame flares aboard fuel or gas rigs risks catastrophic ignition after a leak.

sec03-card-r29.question_text: Where must the very first warning device go immediately when a covered commercial vehicle breaks down during lamp hours?
sec03-card-r29.teaching_text: Getting one marker out on the traffic side right away protects you while spacing out distant markers.

sec03-card-r30.question_text: Where do the three warning devices go for a disabled commercial vehicle on an undivided highway during lamp hours?
sec03-card-r30.teaching_text: Two-way undivided roads bring traffic from both directions, requiring warnings hundred feet front and back.

sec03-card-r31.question_text: How are lane warning devices spaced behind a disabled commercial vehicle on a divided highway during lamp hours?
sec03-card-r31.teaching_text: Divided highways send all lane traffic from behind, so markers step back to hundred and two hundred feet.

sec03-card-r32.question_text: How far out must a warning marker move when a disabled commercial rig sits within 500 feet of a blind curve or crest?
sec03-card-r32.teaching_text: Extending the marker past a hillcrest or bend gives fast highway drivers room to brake before seeing you.

sec03-card-r33.question_text: What warnings must a covered disabled vehicle display on a roadway outside required lamp hours?
sec03-card-r33.teaching_text: Daytime breakdowns swap nighttime lamps for red warning markers at the required front and rear spots.

sec03-card-r34.question_text: Which warning devices and distances apply when an explosive, flammable, or compressed-gas rig is disabled?
sec03-card-r34.teaching_text: Spark-free red electric lanterns or reflectors warn both directions safely around volatile cargo or fuel.

sec03-card-r35.question_text: Which roadside signals are strictly forbidden around disabled vehicles carrying explosives, flammables, or compressed gas?
sec03-card-r35.teaching_text: Striking a road flare near leaking vapor or pressurized fuel can trigger an instant highway explosion.

sec03-card-r36.question_text: What speed threshold requires a rear slow-moving emblem, and which protected work equipment is exempt?
sec03-card-r36.teaching_text: Equipment normally traveling twenty-five miles an hour or slower needs the rear triangle unless road crews post flaggers or signs.

sec03-card-r37.question_text: What shape, center color, and dimensions define the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
sec03-card-r37.teaching_text: Fluorescent yellow-orange fourteen-by-fourteen triangle dimensions stand out sharply in bright daylight against rural Montana highway backgrounds.

sec03-card-r38.question_text: What color, material, and width make up the border of a slow-moving emblem?
sec03-card-r38.teaching_text: Reflective red edges one and three-quarter inches wide bounce headlights back after sunset when fluorescence fades.

sec03-card-r39.question_text: Where and how high above the road should a slow-moving vehicle emblem be mounted?
sec03-card-r39.teaching_text: Centering the triangle three to five feet off pavement keeps it square inside trailing headlight beams.

sec03-card-r40.question_text: When must a slow vehicle on a two-lane road pull over to let trailing traffic pass?
sec03-card-r40.teaching_text: Using the first safe turnout prevents impatient lineups and risky blind-zone passing on two-lane highways.

sec03-card-r41.question_text: Why does keeping your windshield clean matter in bright sun or oncoming headlights?
sec03-card-r41.teaching_text: Dust and bug film turn low-angle sun or night headlamps into a glowing wall that hides hazards.

sec03-card-r42.question_text: What washer-fluid habit applies where temperatures can drop below freezing?
sec03-card-r42.teaching_text: Plain water freezes solid inside nozzles or sheets instantly into ice across cold Montana windshields.

sec03-card-r43.question_text: Why should you wipe interior window surfaces, especially if someone smokes inside?
sec03-card-r43.teaching_text: Oily interior smoke residue fogs glass badly and multiplies nighttime headlight haloing.

sec03-card-r44.question_text: Which window surfaces need snow, ice, and frost cleared before driving?
sec03-card-r44.teaching_text: Clearing front, side, and rear glass restores full three-sixty awareness before pulling into winter traffic.

sec12-card-f01.question_text: What sensory screening does Montana require before issuing a driver license?
sec12-card-f01.teaching_text: Every driver relies primarily on sight to spot cross-traffic, read signs, and react before hazards close in.

sec12-card-f02.question_text: What visual acuity standard must you meet in at least one eye, and are corrective lenses allowed?
sec12-card-f02.teaching_text: Glasses or contacts count toward passing the baseline eyesight check, though using them triggers a license restriction.

sec12-card-f03.question_text: If your license requires corrective lenses, must you wear them on a quick neighborhood errand?
sec12-card-f03.teaching_text: Close-to-home errands still cross busy intersections and crosswalks where blurred vision hides pedestrians or cyclists.

sec12-card-f04.question_text: What legal consequence can hit you for driving without corrective lenses required on your license?
sec12-card-f04.teaching_text: Operating without a listed eyewear restriction violates your license terms just like ignoring any other traffic rule.

sec12-card-f05.question_text: Why should drivers who rely on prescription glasses stash an extra pair inside the vehicle?
sec12-card-f05.teaching_text: Snapping a frame or misplacing glasses miles from home leaves a lens-restricted driver stranded without backup eyewear.

sec12-card-f06.question_text: Why should you never wear sunglasses or tinted contact lenses while driving after dark?
sec12-card-f06.teaching_text: Tinted optics cut already scarce nighttime light and make unlit road edges, animals, and pedestrians vanish.

sec12-card-f07.question_text: Once peripheral vision flags motion beside you, what else may you need to see that hazard clearly?
sec12-card-f07.teaching_text: Peripheral eyesight catches movement well at the edges, yet sharp detail requires mirror checks and quick shoulder looks.

sec12-card-f08.question_text: Which two highway maneuvers especially test your practiced ability to judge vehicle speeds and distances?
sec12-card-f08.teaching_text: Misreading how fast oncoming or highway traffic closes turns routine freeway merges and two-lane passes into head-on traps.

sec12-card-f09.question_text: How should you adjust your schedule and driving style if seeing clearly after dark becomes difficult?
sec12-card-f09.teaching_text: Cutting optional evening errands and slowing down when night travel is unavoidable keeps stopping distance inside headlight range.

sec12-card-f10.question_text: Which three traffic sounds serve as vital audible warnings of nearby road danger?
sec12-card-f10.teaching_text: Hearing locked-up tires, emergency sirens, or urgent horns warns you of hidden trouble before it enters view.

sec12-card-f11.question_text: How can a driver with reduced hearing compensate safely behind the wheel?
sec12-card-f11.teaching_text: Sweeping mirrors more frequently and staying extra attentive replaces faint sirens or horns with proactive visual awareness.

sec12-card-f12.question_text: How does driver fatigue degrade eyesight, thinking speed, and cabin safety?
sec12-card-f12.teaching_text: Exhaustion dulls visual tracking and reaction speed right before nodding off sends an unsteered car out of its lane.

sec12-card-f13.question_text: In what sleep condition should you start a long highway drive instead of rolling out already tired?
sec12-card-f13.teaching_text: Heading onto open Montana highways with a sleep deficit guarantees dangerous drowsiness long before your destination arrives.

sec12-card-f14.question_text: Why should you choose light snacks over a heavy meal right before starting a trip?
sec12-card-f14.teaching_text: Digesting a huge meal triggers post-lunch sluggishness that compounds highway monotony and makes eyelids droop faster.

sec12-card-f15.question_text: How often should you plan rest stops on a long drive, and what if tiredness hits sooner?
sec12-card-f15.teaching_text: Stepping out to stretch every couple of hours—or immediately whenever focus slips—breaks up monotonous highway hypnosis.

sec12-card-f16.question_text: How should you budget travel time when planning any trip?
sec12-card-f16.teaching_text: Tight arrival deadlines tempt drivers into aggressive passing, tailgating, and skipping needed rest breaks along the route.

sec12-card-f17.question_text: Why should you avoid scheduling road trips late at night during hours you normally sleep?
sec12-card-f17.teaching_text: Your body's circadian clock pulls alertness down sharply during normal sleep hours no matter how hard you concentrate.

sec12-card-f18.question_text: What two safe options replace pushing forward when drowsiness hits mid-trip?
sec12-card-f18.teaching_text: Cold air or loud music never cures real sleepiness; only actual sleep or handing keys to a fresh driver works.

sec12-card-f19.question_text: Which five core driving abilities does alcohol degrade?
sec12-card-f19.teaching_text: Alcohol dulls clear eyesight, muscular reflexes, and split-second reaction times while tricking your judgment into feeling confident.

sec12-card-f20.question_text: Why does Montana advise never driving after drinking, even if you only had one alcoholic beverage?
sec12-card-f20.teaching_text: Measurable coordination and judgment decline start with the very first drink, well before anyone feels noticeably drunk.

sec12-card-f21.question_text: Beyond how much and how fast someone drinks, which three personal factors change alcohol impairment?
sec12-card-f21.teaching_text: Identical drinks hit two people differently depending on body mass, stomach contents, overall health, and sipping speed.

sec12-card-f22.question_text: Does pacing yourself at one drink per hour guarantee alcohol will not build up in your system?
sec12-card-f22.teaching_text: When liver metabolism trails behind intake, even a single drink each hour stacks rising blood alcohol over an evening.

sec12-card-f23.question_text: Which serving sizes of eighty-proof liquor, commercial beer, and wine represent standard comparable drinks?
sec12-card-f23.teaching_text: Knowing that 1.5 ounces of liquor, 5 ounces of wine, and 12 ounces of regular beer match prevents undercounting.

sec12-card-f24.question_text: Why is counting craft beers or mixed specialty cocktails as single standard drinks risky?
sec12-card-f24.teaching_text: High-gravity IPAs and multi-shot bar pours often pack double the alcohol of standard twelve-ounce commercial beer examples.

sec12-card-f25.question_text: What three sober transportation options should you line up whenever drinking is part of your plans?
sec12-card-f25.teaching_text: Locking in an alcohol-free designated driver, bus, or ride service before the first sip removes tempted late-night choices.

sec12-card-f26.question_text: What blood alcohol percentage triggers arrest, and can you still be arrested below that number?
sec12-card-f26.teaching_text: Officers arrest drivers at 0.08 percent BAC automatically, or below 0.08 whenever observable driving impairment is present.

sec12-card-f27.question_text: What does BAC measure, and which three chemical sample types usually determine it?
sec12-card-f27.teaching_text: Chemical testing of breath, blood, or urine quantifies the exact ratio of alcohol circulating in your bloodstream.
sec12-card-f27.must_match_memory_hook: Blood alcohol via breath, blood, urine

visual_sync.text_span: Blood alcohol via breath, blood, urine

sec12-card-f28.question_text: What happens to your driver license if you refuse a blood alcohol test requested by police?
sec12-card-f28.teaching_text: Saying no to an officer's chemical test request triggers license seizure and suspension separate from any DUI charge.

sec12-card-f29.question_text: Where inside a vehicle on a public highway is keeping an unlawful open alcohol container banned?
sec12-card-f29.teaching_text: Keeping unsealed drinks inside the passenger compartment puts alcohol within arm's reach of the driver on public roads.

sec12-card-f30.question_text: What condition makes a glove box or interior storage compartment legal for stowing an alcohol container?
sec12-card-f30.teaching_text: Securing a bottle inside a genuinely locked glove box prevents anyone in the cabin from sipping while rolling.

sec12-card-f31.question_text: Which four cargo or exterior areas are legal places to transport alcoholic beverage containers?
sec12-card-f31.teaching_text: Stowing bottles in the trunk, pickup bed, luggage bay, or cargo hold isolates them completely from seated occupants.

sec12-card-f32.question_text: Where can an SUV, hatchback, or van without a trunk legally carry an alcohol container?
sec12-card-f32.teaching_text: Placing containers behind the rearmost upright seatback or sealed outside passenger seating satisfies open-container rules in hatchbacks.

sec12-card-f33.question_text: Which two conditions qualify a bottle for the sealed-container exception?
sec12-card-f33.teaching_text: Recapping an already opened bottle still counts as an open container because its factory seal is broken.

sec12-card-f34.question_text: Which section of a camper, travel trailer, or motor home has an open-container storage exception?
sec12-card-f34.teaching_text: Residential living quarters of campers and motor homes remain exempt while the driver's cockpit stays strictly alcohol-free.

sec12-card-f35.question_text: Which three hired-driver vehicles allow passengers an exception to the open-container ban?
sec12-card-f35.teaching_text: Paying riders chauffeured in commercial buses, cabs, or limousines qualify while the professional driver stays completely sober.

sec12-card-f36.question_text: Whom should you contact to report a suspected drunk driver, and what two details help officers intercept them?
sec12-card-f36.teaching_text: Giving local police or Highway Patrol a crisp vehicle description and travel direction lets troopers intercept erratic drivers fast.

sec12-card-f37.question_text: Must you give your own name when calling law enforcement to report a suspected impaired driver?
sec12-card-f37.teaching_text: Allowing anonymous tips encourages witnesses to report dangerous weaving vehicles immediately without worrying about personal involvement.

sec12-card-r01.question_text: Can nonprescription pharmacy medicines impair your driving just like prescription drugs?
sec12-card-r01.teaching_text: Everyday allergy, cold, or sleep aids sold off the shelf cause drowsiness and sluggish reactions just like prescriptions.

sec12-card-r02.question_text: What should you inspect before taking any medication ahead of a planned drive?
sec12-card-r02.teaching_text: Checking drowsiness or dizziness warnings before swallowing a dose prevents getting caught impaired halfway down the highway.

sec12-card-r03.question_text: What does a medication warning against operating heavy machinery mean for everyday drivers?
sec12-card-r03.teaching_text: A two-ton car or pickup at highway speed is heavy machinery, so that label means stay out of the driver's seat.

sec12-card-r04.question_text: Which two health professionals should you ask if you are unsure how a medication affects driving?
sec12-card-r04.teaching_text: Doctors and pharmacists spot hidden sedating side effects or drug interactions long before they surprise you in traffic.

sec12-card-r05.question_text: Why must you never mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medications?
sec12-card-r05.teaching_text: Combining alcohol with medicine creates synergistic reactions that multiply drowsiness and trigger dangerous unexpected side effects.

sec12-card-r06.question_text: What should you do when an illness makes driving unsafe?
sec12-card-r06.teaching_text: Fever, dizziness, or severe symptoms sap reaction time, making handing keys to a healthy driver the smart call.

sec12-card-r07.question_text: When should you evaluate whether you are physically and mentally fit to operate a vehicle?
sec12-card-r07.teaching_text: Taking five honest seconds before turning the key catches exhaustion, illness, or emotional overload while still safely parked.

sec12-card-r08.question_text: What documentation does the Montana handbook call for when an applicant or driver has epilepsy?
sec12-card-r08.teaching_text: Signed medical confirmation verifies that seizures remain well controlled and unlikely to cause sudden loss of consciousness.

sec12-card-r09.question_text: Whom should a driver with a heart condition consult about whether driving remains safe?
sec12-card-r09.teaching_text: Your treating physician understands whether cardiac symptoms, fainting spells, or medications pose sudden highway risks.

sec12-card-r10.question_text: How do heavy stress or intense emotions affect your performance in traffic?
sec12-card-r10.teaching_text: Preoccupation with anger, grief, or worry narrows attention and causes missed red lights or tailgating mistakes.

sec12-card-r11.question_text: What should you do if you feel angry or worked up right before driving?
sec12-card-r11.teaching_text: Cooling down before pulling into traffic prevents aggressive acceleration and road-rage confrontations.

sec12-card-r12.question_text: What trip-planning habit counters impatience before it pushes you into speeding or risky moves?
sec12-card-r12.teaching_text: Leaving ten minutes early removes clock pressure so slow trucks or red lights never provoke reckless lane weaving.

sec12-card-r13.question_text: What should an older driver do if a physician advises avoiding night, high-speed, or heavy-traffic driving?
sec12-card-r13.teaching_text: Honoring tailored medical boundaries lets senior drivers stay mobile on calm daylight streets without overtaxing reflexes.

sec12-card-r14.question_text: Which numbered Montana form can medical professionals file to recommend a driver re-examination?
sec12-card-r14.teaching_text: Clinicians who spot serious cognitive or physical decline use this official referral to trigger a fair skills check.

sec12-card-r15.question_text: Which numbered Montana form is used for a formal Driver Medical Evaluation?
sec12-card-r15.teaching_text: Documenting medical conditions on the official evaluation sheet helps licensing reviewers set appropriate restrictions or clearances.

sec12-card-r16.question_text: Which numbered Montana form records a specialist's Report of Eye Examination?
sec12-card-r16.teaching_text: Optometrists and ophthalmologists record detailed acuity and field measurements on this form when branch screening needs follow-up.

sec12-card-r17.question_text: Under what personal condition should older drivers choose to get behind the wheel?
sec12-card-r17.teaching_text: Postponing errands on off days when stamina or alertness dips prevents minor health flare-ups from causing crashes.

sec12-card-r18.question_text: When may an older driver get behind the wheel after taking medication?
sec12-card-r18.teaching_text: Aging bodies metabolize prescriptions differently, making explicit physician clearance essential before driving on any new dose.

sec12-card-r19.question_text: Whose unexpected, unsafe movements must defensive drivers stay constantly alert for?
sec12-card-r19.teaching_text: Expecting darting kids, jaywalkers, or abrupt lane-changers buys you extra braking margin before a close call turns serious.

sec12-card-r20.question_text: What traffic knowledge should experienced drivers keep refreshing over the years?
sec12-card-r20.teaching_text: Roadway signs, move-over rules, and intersection designs evolve over decades, so lifelong drivers still refresh their rulebook.

sec12-card-r21.question_text: How should older drivers plan routes to match their comfort and safety?
sec12-card-r21.teaching_text: Mapping familiar lower-speed streets ahead of time eliminates frantic last-second lane changes in heavy freeway traffic.

sec12-card-r22.question_text: What three adjustments help if your slower pace backs up vehicles behind you?
sec12-card-r22.teaching_text: Letting queued cars pass safely or choosing quieter roads and off-peak hours prevents frustrated risky passing behind you.

sec12-card-r23.question_text: How should you keep your vehicle mechanically safe as part of personal fitness precautions?
sec12-card-r23.teaching_text: Responsive brakes, crisp wipers, and properly inflated tires reduce physical strain and emergency stopping distances.

sec12-card-r24.question_text: Which three surfaces should you clean regularly to protect visibility, especially after dark?
sec12-card-r24.teaching_text: Road film on headlamps combined with smudges on glass and lenses scatters oncoming beams into blinding halos.

sec12-card-r25.question_text: On which trips does the fitness-precautions section advise buckling your seatbelt?
sec12-card-r25.teaching_text: Fragile bones and sudden neighborhood collisions make consistent seatbelt use critical on every outing regardless of speed.

sec12-card-r26.question_text: How many attempts at parallel parking count as a driving-skill self-check warning?
sec12-card-r26.teaching_text: Repeatedly misjudging curb angles and bumper clearance signals that spatial awareness and low-speed control merit honest review.

sec12-card-r27.question_text: What does struggling to spot objects at night or lingering discomfort from headlight glare indicate?
sec12-card-r27.teaching_text: Slow recovery from bright oncoming beams often reveals cataracts or age-related eye changes an optometrist can evaluate.

sec12-card-r28.question_text: In the older-driver self-check, what do lagging behind traffic pace or slow starts at green lights suggest?
sec12-card-r28.teaching_text: Delayed intersection starts and trouble matching traffic flow point to slowed processing or hesitation worth evaluating.

sec12-card-r29.question_text: What pattern of minor body damage warns a driver to review their driving skills?
sec12-card-r29.teaching_text: Fresh garage grazes or parking-lot dings rarely happen by bad luck alone; they flag shrinking spatial awareness.

sec12-card-r30.question_text: What should missing road signs or feeling disoriented in unfamiliar traffic prompt you to do?
sec12-card-r30.teaching_text: Overlooking regulatory signs or freezing at complex intersections signals cognitive overload that threatens cross-traffic safety.

sec12-card-r31.question_text: What self-check conclusion follows trouble judging distance, spotting near or far objects, or seeing road edges?
sec12-card-r31.teaching_text: Losing track of pavement edges or closing gaps makes lane keeping and safe turns unreliable without intervention.

sec12-card-r32.question_text: Which five personal warning signs can guide a driver's decision to stop driving altogether?
sec12-card-r32.teaching_text: Stacking close calls, medication fog, wheel anxiety, or fear of getting lost shows retiring from driving protects everyone.

sec12-card-r33.question_text: Where can a Montana driver voluntarily surrender their license once safe driving is no longer possible?
sec12-card-r33.teaching_text: Turning in a license voluntarily at a local driver exam station transitions cleanly to non-driver identification.

sec12-card-r34.question_text: Which form lets concerned family or citizens ask the state to re-examine another driver's ability?
sec12-card-r34.teaching_text: Filing a documented Recommendation for Re-Exam prompts an objective skills check when a driver cannot recognize their own decline.

sec14-card-f01.question_text: Why can Montana suspend, revoke, or cancel your driver license if you break traffic laws?
sec14-card-f01.teaching_text: Holding a state credential grants conditional permission to use public roads, never an untouchable right immune from lawbreaking.

sec14-card-f02.question_text: Beyond fines or court dates, what licensing consequence does the handbook tie to impaired driving?
sec14-card-f02.teaching_text: Driving under the influence threatens public safety directly, putting your Montana driving privilege on the chopping block.

sec14-card-f03.question_text: Can distracted driving lead to losing your Montana driver license, or only minor fines?
sec14-card-f03.teaching_text: Taking eyes and attention off traffic ranks alongside major violations capable of costing your driving privilege.

sec14-card-f04.question_text: What happens to your licensing status if you keep driving while already suspended or revoked?
sec14-card-f04.teaching_text: Ignoring an active suspension stacks extended revocation time on top of your original penalty instead of running out the clock.

sec14-card-f05.question_text: Which underage offense can strip a young person's driver license even outside a traffic stop?
sec14-card-f05.teaching_text: Underage alcohol or substance possession hits your driving record directly even if no vehicle was involved.

sec14-card-f06.question_text: Which major section of a Montana driving record holds your identifying background details?
sec14-card-f06.teaching_text: Accurate personal-history entries anchor your official driver file so citations or clearances attach to the right person.

sec14-card-f07.question_text: Which major category of a driving record tracks your credential class, status, and endorsements?
sec14-card-f07.teaching_text: Officers and insurers check the licensing-information section first to verify valid status and active restrictions.

sec14-card-f08.question_text: Which combined major category on a driving record pairs court violations with road collisions?
sec14-card-f08.teaching_text: Grouping traffic convictions alongside crash involvement gives reviewers a unified snapshot of real-world road risk.

sec14-card-f09.question_text: Which major driving-record category logs formal penalties taken against your driving privilege?
sec14-card-f09.teaching_text: Every state restriction or withdrawal sits inside the driver-license sanctions category for courts and agencies to verify.

sec14-card-f10.question_text: Which listed major category of a Montana driving record specifically tracks motor-vehicle collisions?
sec14-card-f10.teaching_text: Reportable collisions stay logged under motor-vehicle accident history where insurers and licensing officials review crash patterns.

sec14-card-f11.question_text: Does your permanent driving record retain details from your original driver-license application?
sec14-card-f11.teaching_text: Statements submitted on your initial license application become permanent record entries from day one.

sec14-card-f12.question_text: What stage of proving your knowledge and road skills is documented in your driving record?
sec14-card-f12.teaching_text: Written, vision, and behind-the-wheel exam outcomes are logged officially before any plastic card is printed.

sec14-card-f13.question_text: Once you pass testing, what milestone of granting driving privileges goes onto your driving record?
sec14-card-f13.teaching_text: Recording exact issuance dates establishes how long you have held valid privileges for graduated rules and renewals.

sec14-card-f14.question_text: If the state declines an applicant's request for a license, is that refusal recorded?
sec14-card-f14.teaching_text: Logging license denials prevents ineligible applicants from simply visiting another exam station without resolving the issue.

sec14-card-f15.question_text: How does a Montana driving record treat a formal license revocation?
sec14-card-f15.teaching_text: Revocations terminate driving privileges outright and remain documented so reinstatement requirements cannot be skipped.

sec14-card-f16.question_text: Is a temporary license suspension stored among the licensing actions on your driving record?
sec14-card-f16.teaching_text: Active and past suspensions appear on your record until every waiting period and reinstatement step finishes.

sec14-card-f17.question_text: Does your driving record's licensing history also include a license cancellation?
sec14-card-f17.teaching_text: Whether triggered by application errors or surrendered consent, cancellations stay visible inside your licensing history.

sec14-card-f18.question_text: Beyond applications and status changes, what performance details and state interventions does your record keep?
sec14-card-f18.teaching_text: Re-examinations, unsafe-driving interventions, and legal compliance actions round out your complete driver performance file.

sec14-card-r01.question_text: Which Montana Motor Vehicle Division resource does the handbook name for deeper suspension and revocation rules?
sec14-card-r01.teaching_text: Checking the Motor Vehicle Division's dedicated suspensions-and-revocations page gives current statutory lengths and reinstatement steps.

sec14-card-r02.question_text: Which Motor Vehicle Division resource explains how to request a copy of a Montana driving record?
sec14-card-r02.teaching_text: Following the Motor Vehicle Division's driving-records instructions lets you verify your own history accurately.

sec13-card-f01.question_text: What routine vehicle care cuts the odds of mechanical failure out on the road?
sec13-card-f01.teaching_text: Catching worn belts, low fluids, and thin brake pads on schedule beats dealing with sudden failures at highway speed.

sec13-card-f02.question_text: If your regular brakes suddenly fail, what should you do first with the brake pedal?
sec13-card-f02.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can rebuild enough hydraulic pressure in a dual-circuit system to slow the car down.

sec13-card-f03.question_text: If pumping fails, how should you apply a handle-operated parking brake—and why stay ready to release it?
sec13-card-f03.teaching_text: Yanking the parking brake locks the rear tires into a spin, whereas gradual pressure slows you down under control.

sec13-card-f04.question_text: If even the parking brake cannot stop your vehicle, what gear and steering action come next?
sec13-card-f04.teaching_text: Dropping into lower gears uses engine compression to bleed off momentum while you guide the car off traffic lanes.

sec13-card-f05.question_text: Once you get a vehicle with failed brakes stopped safely, may you limp it further down the road?
sec13-card-f05.teaching_text: Rolling even a few blocks without working brakes turns the next downhill or red light into an unavoidable crash.

sec13-card-f06.question_text: What is your immediate steering priority the moment a tire blows out?
sec13-card-f06.teaching_text: A blown tire tugs violently toward the flat side, requiring two firm hands to keep the car tracking straight.

sec13-card-f07.question_text: How should you handle the gas and brake pedals to shed speed after a tire blows?
sec13-card-f07.teaching_text: Stomping the brake right after a blowout shifts weight onto the shredded tire and can flip or spin the car.

sec13-card-f08.question_text: Where should you bring the vehicle to a complete stop after slowing from a blowout?
sec13-card-f08.teaching_text: Clearing live travel lanes before changing a flat protects you from distracted highway traffic rushing past.

sec13-card-f09.question_text: Why must you grip the steering wheel firmly if your engine suddenly dies in motion?
sec13-card-f09.teaching_text: Losing engine power kills power-steering assist instantly, making the wheel feel heavy without locking it completely.

sec13-card-f10.question_text: As you steer off the roadway with a stalled engine, how will the brake pedal feel?
sec13-card-f10.teaching_text: Once vacuum brake boost depletes after an engine stall, stopping takes much heavier leg force on the pedal.

sec13-card-f11.question_text: If your headlights suddenly go dark at night, what are your very first three calm steps?
sec13-card-f11.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel blind in the dark drives you into ditches, whereas easing off and braking straight buys reaction time.

sec13-card-f12.question_text: Which two lighting controls should you cycle right away to try reviving dead headlights?
sec13-card-f12.teaching_text: High beams run on separate filaments and relays, often restoring forward illumination when low-beam contacts fail.

sec13-card-f13.question_text: If neither the switch nor high beams restore your headlights, which backup lights help you pull off safely?
sec13-card-f13.teaching_text: Hazard flashers, turn signals, or fog lamps cast enough short-range glow and visibility to guide you onto the shoulder.

sec13-card-f14.question_text: If the accelerator sticks open, what should you do immediately while keeping your eyes on the road?
sec13-card-f14.teaching_text: Snapping the shifter into neutral disconnects the racing engine from the wheels without killing steering or brake boost.

sec13-card-f15.question_text: After shifting a stuck-throttle car to neutral, when do you brake, pull off, and shut off the ignition?
sec13-card-f15.teaching_text: Turning the key off before stopping kills power steering and can lock the steering column while still moving.

sec13-card-f16.question_text: What is your initial response if your right wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-f16.teaching_text: Jerking left immediately catches the pavement lip and slingshots the car sideways across oncoming lanes.

sec13-card-f17.question_text: After slowing beside the pavement edge, how do your hands turn the wheel to reenter the right lane?
sec13-card-f17.teaching_text: Slowing down first and using a controlled two-handed left quarter-turn climbs the shoulder lip without overcorrecting.

sec13-card-f18.question_text: In Montana's right-wheel drop-off recovery, when do you apply the brakes and where do you position the car?
sec13-card-f18.teaching_text: Waiting until all four tires sit squarely on dry asphalt prevents uneven gravel grip from spinning the vehicle.

sec13-card-f19.question_text: Which three vehicle actions can help you avoid an impending collision?
sec13-card-f19.teaching_text: Drivers often freeze onto the brake pedal when steering around an obstacle or accelerating clear would work faster.

sec13-card-f20.question_text: Where should you check the exact anti-lock braking instructions for the specific vehicle you drive?
sec13-card-f20.teaching_text: Knowing how your car's brake system behaves before an emergency stops you from lifting off when ABS pulses.

sec13-card-f21.question_text: How do you execute an emergency quick stop with anti-lock brakes, even if the pedal pulses back?
sec13-card-f21.teaching_text: Pedal chatter means ABS is rapidly cycling brake pressure for you; pumping or lifting off lengthens stopping distance.

sec13-card-f22.question_text: How hard should you press the brake pedal during an emergency stop in a vehicle without ABS?
sec13-card-f22.teaching_text: Squeezing right up to the threshold of lockup maximizes braking force while keeping the front tires rolling and steerable.

sec13-card-f23.question_text: If non-ABS wheels lock up and skid during a hard stop, how should you work the pedal?
sec13-card-f23.teaching_text: Releasing briefly lets sliding tires regain rolling grip before reapplying firm pressure brings you down cleanly.

sec13-card-f24.question_text: How should you hold and aim the steering wheel during a sudden collision-avoidance turn?
sec13-card-f24.teaching_text: Looking and steering toward open pavement with two firm hands prevents one-handed slips during sharp weight transfer.

sec13-card-f25.question_text: Why must you stay poised to straighten and control the vehicle right after an avoidance swerve?
sec13-card-f25.teaching_text: Dodging the first hazard means nothing if body roll or overcorrection sends you into a guardrail or oncoming car.

sec13-card-f26.question_text: Which two safety systems allow a vehicle to handle simultaneous hard braking and emergency turning?
sec13-card-f26.teaching_text: Anti-lock brakes keep tires rolling while stability control selectively brakes individual wheels to resist spinouts mid-turn.

sec13-card-f27.question_text: Without anti-lock brakes, how do you time braking before a quick turn so the car does not plow straight?
sec13-card-f27.teaching_text: Locked or overloaded front tires cannot steer and braking simultaneously, causing the car to slide straight ahead.

sec13-card-f28.question_text: When can stepping on the gas avoid a rear or side crash, and what follows once clear?
sec13-card-f28.teaching_text: Surging forward into open lane space dodges T-bone or rear-end hits, provided you ease back down immediately afterward.

sec13-card-f29.question_text: Which belt combination lowers your vulnerability to injury when a crash cannot be avoided?
sec13-card-f29.teaching_text: Tucking the shoulder strap behind your back leaves your head and chest unrestrained to slam the steering column.

sec13-card-f30.question_text: How should you position your body and foot right before being struck from behind?
sec13-card-f30.teaching_text: Pressing your skull flat against the head restraint limits whiplash while immediate braking stops you from ramming cars ahead.

sec13-card-f31.question_text: Even with side airbags, why do belts stay essential in a side hit—and what must you stay ready for?
sec13-card-f31.teaching_text: Belts hold you in position during lateral spin while active steering and braking stop a secondary crash.

sec13-card-f32.question_text: If an oncoming frontal impact becomes unavoidable, how should you try to alter the hit?
sec13-card-f32.teaching_text: Turning a dead-center head-on smash into a glancing angled blow dramatically lowers peak cabin deceleration.

sec13-card-f33.question_text: Under what two conditions only should you stop at a crash scene?
sec13-card-f33.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily beside an already-attended collision clogs shoulders and triggers chain-reaction rear-end wrecks.

sec13-card-f34.question_text: Why must drivers never drive toward or linger at a crash, fire, or disaster just to watch?
sec13-card-f34.teaching_text: Curious onlookers jam access lanes that ambulances, fire engines, and tow rigs urgently need to reach victims.

sec13-card-f35.question_text: What is every driver's immediate legal duty whenever involved in a crash?
sec13-card-f35.teaching_text: Continuing down the road after any collision turns an accidental fender-bender into a serious hit-and-run offense.

sec13-card-f36.question_text: What must you try to do first right after striking an unattended parked vehicle?
sec13-card-f36.teaching_text: Making an honest effort to find the owner nearby satisfies your initial legal duty before leaving written contact info.

sec13-card-f37.question_text: Whom must you notify whenever a collision injures or kills anyone?
sec13-card-f37.teaching_text: Any bodily harm or fatality requires official law-enforcement investigation and emergency medical dispatch.

sec13-card-f38.question_text: What legal classification applies to leaving an injury or fatal crash before police gather needed details?
sec13-card-f38.teaching_text: Departing an injury or fatal scene before officers collect required statements exposes an involved driver to criminal prosecution.

sec13-card-r01.question_text: After stopping at or near a crash, what should you do if your vehicle still moves safely?
sec13-card-r01.teaching_text: Leaving a drivable fender-bender parked across live highway lanes invites high-speed secondary pileups.

sec13-card-r02.question_text: Where must crash occupants and witnesses avoid standing or walking while waiting at the scene?
sec13-card-r02.teaching_text: Approaching drivers fixate on damaged cars and easily strike people standing in active roadway lanes.

sec13-card-r03.question_text: Which two fire-prevention steps apply around wrecked vehicles at a crash scene?
sec13-card-r03.teaching_text: Ruptured fuel lines leak volatile gasoline vapors that an active ignition spark or lit cigarette can ignite instantly.

sec13-card-r04.question_text: How should everyone at a crash scene treat downed electrical wires?
sec13-card-r04.teaching_text: Fallen power lines can energize wet pavement and metal car bodies with lethal high voltage even without sparking.

sec13-card-r05.question_text: Why should you deploy appropriate warning devices around a crash site?
sec13-card-r05.teaching_text: Reflective triangles, flares, or hazard flashers give fast-moving traffic advance room to slow and steer clear.

sec13-card-r06.question_text: When a crash injures someone, which emergency responders must be called—and what hazard must be reported?
sec13-card-r06.teaching_text: Dispatchers need immediate word of both bodily injuries and vehicle smoke so rescue and fire crews roll together.

sec13-card-r07.question_text: When is the only time you should move an injured crash victim yourself?
sec13-card-r07.teaching_text: Shifting someone with a hidden neck or spinal fracture can cause permanent paralysis unless fire forces evacuation.

sec13-card-r08.question_text: May you offer water or any other drink to someone injured in a collision?
sec13-card-r08.teaching_text: Even plain water can trigger choking or dangerous surgical complications if internal injuries require emergency anesthesia.

sec13-card-r09.question_text: Which three groups of people at a crash should have their names and addresses written down?
sec13-card-r09.teaching_text: Bystander witnesses quickly drive off once lanes clear, taking crucial independent crash accounts with them.

sec13-card-r10.question_text: What three categories of driver, vehicle, and coverage details must involved drivers swap?
sec13-card-r10.teaching_text: Complete license numbers, plate descriptions, and insurer policy numbers prevent claim delays after everyone leaves.

sec13-card-r11.question_text: Which four specific vehicle facts belong in your post-crash information exchange?
sec13-card-r11.teaching_text: Pairing the license plate with exact make, model, and year eliminates mix-ups on police and insurance filings.

sec13-card-r12.question_text: Alongside noting vehicle damage, how must you respond to police or emergency officials at the scene?
sec13-card-r12.teaching_text: Recording fresh damage accurately and cooperating promptly with responding officers builds a clean official crash report.

sec13-card-r13.question_text: If you cannot find a struck parked car's owner, what details belong on the visible note you leave?
sec13-card-r13.teaching_text: Tucking a clear note with your contact details and exact crash timestamp fulfills your legal duty honestly.

sec13-card-r14.question_text: Besides any injury or death, what property-damage threshold requires immediate notice to law enforcement?
sec13-card-r14.teaching_text: Modern bumper repairs cross five hundred dollars effortlessly, meaning almost any real impact requires calling police immediately.

sec13-card-r15.question_text: Within how many days—and to whom—must you file a report for injury, death, or $1,000 property damage?
sec13-card-r15.teaching_text: Separate the two dollar thresholds cleanly since five hundred calls police immediately while one thousand requires ten-day filing.

sec13-card-r16.question_text: Who may submit the required crash report if injuries prevent the driver from filing it personally?
sec13-card-r16.teaching_text: Allowing a passenger, relative, or representative to submit paperwork keeps hospitalized drivers compliant with reporting deadlines.

sec13-card-r17.question_text: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction?
sec13-card-r17.teaching_text: Clearing toward the right edge from both directions opens a predictable center corridor for high-speed responders.

sec13-card-r18.question_text: How should you align your vehicle at the right curb when yielding to emergency lights and sirens?
sec13-card-r18.teaching_text: Stopping angled into the lane leaves your rear bumper jutting out into the ambulance's narrow path.

sec13-card-r19.question_text: On highways posted 50 mph or higher, how much must adjacent-lane traffic slow past a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec13-card-r19.teaching_text: When you cannot change lanes on a 50-plus highway, shedding at least 20 mph protects officers working inches away.

sec13-card-r20.question_text: Whenever traffic allows, which lane should you choose when passing a stationary emergency or police vehicle?
sec13-card-r20.teaching_text: Putting a full empty buffer lane between your mirrors and roadside responders is safer than merely slowing nearby.

sec13-card-r21.question_text: Alongside a siren, which three flashing or rotating light colors identify police emergency signals?
sec13-card-r21.teaching_text: Recognizing blue alongside red and amber strobes identifies law enforcement immediately in mirrors day or night.

sec13-card-r22.question_text: Which warning sound and two lamp colors are listed for authorized emergency vehicles?
sec13-card-r22.teaching_text: Fire rigs, ambulances, and authorized responders command immediate right-of-way using sirens or flashing red and amber lamps.

sec13-card-r23.question_text: How should you immediately acknowledge a patrol officer who turns on emergency lights behind you?
sec13-card-r23.teaching_text: Flashing your right blinker tells the trooper you saw their lights and are actively looking to pull over.

sec13-card-r24.question_text: Where should you guide your car during a routine traffic enforcement stop?
sec13-card-r24.teaching_text: Pulling onto the right shoulder keeps both you and the approaching officer away from fast left-lane passing traffic.

sec13-card-r25.question_text: Which two roadside spots must you never pull into during a police enforcement stop?
sec13-card-r25.teaching_text: Stopping in a center median traps the patrol car beside fast lanes, and crossing left cuts across oncoming traffic.

sec13-card-r26.question_text: How far off the pavement should you pull, and what lighting helps during a night stop?
sec13-card-r26.teaching_text: Giving generous shoulder clearance in a well-lit area protects everyone during nighttime document checks.

sec13-card-r27.question_text: What should you do with active phone calls and car audio as soon as you stop for police?
sec13-card-r27.teaching_text: Silencing calls and stereo noise ensures clear, calm communication from the moment the officer reaches your window.

sec13-card-r28.question_text: Should you step out of your vehicle to meet the officer during a traffic stop?
sec13-card-r28.teaching_text: Popping your door open uninvited looks threatening and exposes you to passing highway traffic.

sec13-card-r29.question_text: Who inside a stopped vehicle should keep their hands in plain view of the approaching officer?
sec13-card-r29.teaching_text: Resting visible hands on the wheel and lap reassures the officer that nobody is reaching for hidden items.

sec13-card-r30.question_text: If your vehicle has tinted windows, when should you roll them down during a traffic stop?
sec13-card-r30.teaching_text: Lowering dark glass once parked on the shoulder—before the officer walks up—eliminates visibility tension safely.

sec11-card-f01.question_text: How does your clear view ahead govern safe speed choice?
sec11-card-f01.teaching_text: Driving faster than your visible stopping zone leaves you helpless if a stalled rig sits beyond sight.

sec11-card-f02.question_text: How do you run the four-second sight-distance check, and what if you pass the object early?
sec11-card-f02.teaching_text: Reaching your farthest visible landmark under four seconds proves your stopping distance exceeds your sightline.

sec11-card-f03.question_text: What common nighttime hazard does the four-second sight-distance check prevent?
sec11-card-f03.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlamp cone means dark road obstacles enter view closer than your brakes can halt.

sec11-card-f04.question_text: Does a dry, empty-looking highway allow exceeding the posted speed limit?
sec11-card-f04.teaching_text: Empty-looking pavement still hides wildlife, side driveways, and abrupt grade changes engineered into the posted maximum.

sec11-card-f05.question_text: What road conditions do posted speed signs assume, and when must you drive slower?
sec11-card-f05.teaching_text: Rain, ice, fog, or heavy traffic slash tire grip and reaction margin well below fair-weather limits.

sec11-card-f06.question_text: Can an officer ticket you while driving below the posted speed limit?
sec11-card-f06.teaching_text: Basic speed law punishes any pace too fast for ice, storms, or congestion regardless of posted signs.

sec11-card-f07.question_text: What crucial advantage does keeping a generous space cushion around your car provide?
sec11-card-f07.teaching_text: Open pavement on all sides gives room to brake smoothly or steer clear when someone errs.

sec11-card-f08.question_text: At what exact moment do you start counting during the three-second following check?
sec11-card-f08.teaching_text: Starting your count as the rear bumper ahead clears a signpost measures true bumper-to-bumper time.

sec11-card-f09.question_text: What should you do if your car passes the fixed marker before reaching three seconds?
sec11-card-f09.teaching_text: Easing back until a fresh count clears three full seconds restores safe dry-road stopping space.

sec11-card-f10.question_text: How many seconds of following space does Montana recommend when conditions demand extra margin?
sec11-card-f10.teaching_text: Adding one extra second builds crucial stopping buffer whenever traction, sightlines, or trailing hazards worsen.

sec11-card-f11.question_text: Why must you widen your following gap on wet, snowy, or icy pavement?
sec11-card-f11.teaching_text: Reduced tire friction on slick surfaces stretches your braking distance far beyond dry-pavement three-second margins.

sec11-card-f12.question_text: How should you adjust speed when a driver behind starts passing you?
sec11-card-f12.teaching_text: Easing off the gas opens a clean return pocket ahead and shortens two-lane exposure.

sec11-card-f13.question_text: Why should you leave extra following distance behind a motorcycle?
sec11-card-f13.teaching_text: Bikes stop rapidly and a spilled rider on pavement needs wide braking clearance from trailing cars.

sec11-card-f14.question_text: On which four surface types are motorcycles especially prone to losing traction and falling?
sec11-card-f14.teaching_text: Two narrow contact patches slip easily across loose gravel, bridge gratings, wet paint, or rail tracks.

sec11-card-f15.question_text: Why must you drop farther back behind a truck, bus, van, or trailer rig?
sec11-card-f15.teaching_text: Tailgating a box trailer hides you inside its rear blind zone while blocking your view ahead.

sec11-card-f16.question_text: How does carrying a heavy cargo load or towing a trailer change needed following space?
sec11-card-f16.teaching_text: Extra momentum pushes loaded trucks and trailers much farther forward under hard braking.

sec11-card-f17.question_text: What following adjustment applies when darkness, fog, or storms obscure the view ahead?
sec11-card-f17.teaching_text: When you cannot see beyond the bumper ahead, extra seconds keep you out of sudden pileups.

sec11-card-f18.question_text: What two options help clear a driver who is following you too closely?
sec11-card-f18.teaching_text: Letting aggressive followers move ahead puts risky behavior in front where you control the gap.

sec11-card-f19.question_text: How should you space your car when following emergency vehicles?
sec11-card-f19.teaching_text: Fire trucks, ambulances, and patrol units may brake, turn, or stop abruptly at incident scenes.

sec11-card-f20.question_text: Which two vehicle classes need extra following space approaching railroad tracks because they must stop?
sec11-card-f20.teaching_text: Expecting school buses and hazmat tankers to halt at crossings prevents surprise rear-end collisions.

sec11-card-f21.question_text: Why must you stop farther back behind another vehicle on an uphill grade?
sec11-card-f21.teaching_text: Manual-shift cars and heavy trucks often drift back a few feet before engaging forward power.
