sec11-card-f22.question_text: Which two driving habits help motorists behind you maintain a safe gap?
sec11-card-f22.teaching_text: Consistent speed and early signal or brake taps keep followers from bunching up unexpectedly.

sec11-card-f23.question_text: Where should you stop whenever picking up or dropping off passengers?
sec11-card-f23.teaching_text: Halting inside an active travel lane exposes stepping passengers and your rear bumper to fast traffic.

sec11-card-f24.question_text: How do you handle trailing traffic before backing into a parallel parking space?
sec11-card-f24.teaching_text: Letting close followers clear first prevents someone nosing right into the pocket you are backing toward.

sec11-card-f25.question_text: What courtesy step applies whenever necessary slow driving holds up cars behind you?
sec11-card-f25.teaching_text: Using a safe shoulder or turnout relieves risky passing frustration on rural Montana roads.

sec11-card-f26.question_text: What is the cleanest response to a tailgater when an open right lane is available?
sec11-card-f26.teaching_text: Changing right opens the passing lane immediately without confrontation or speed games.

sec11-card-f27.question_text: How do you handle a tailgater when no right lane exists?
sec11-card-f27.teaching_text: Waiting until oncoming sightlines open before easing speed helps the tailgater pass safely.

sec11-card-f28.question_text: Why must you never slam the brakes to warn off a tailgater?
sec11-card-f28.teaching_text: Tapping or jabbing brakes aggressively with zero gap behind turns annoyance into an instant collision.

sec11-card-f29.question_text: How do you maintain side escape space on a multilane road?
sec11-card-f29.teaching_text: Pacing side by side traps you with nowhere to steer if a tire blows or obstacle appears.

sec11-card-f30.question_text: Where inside your lane should you normally position your car on a two-lane highway?
sec11-card-f30.teaching_text: Hugging the yellow stripe shrinks margin against wide oncoming mirrors, trailers, and wandering drivers.

sec11-card-f31.question_text: On roads with two or more lanes each way, how can you assist merging traffic?
sec11-card-f31.teaching_text: Shifting into an open left lane clears the right merge pocket cleanly for accelerating ramp cars.

sec11-card-f32.question_text: Why must you keep extra side clearance along a row of parked cars?
sec11-card-f32.teaching_text: Car doors swing open without warning and parked bumpers pull out from curb blind spots.

sec11-card-r01.question_text: Why do pedestrians, especially children, require an extra-wide safety cushion?
sec11-card-r01.teaching_text: Kids chasing balls or friends misjudge vehicle speed and step abruptly off curbs.

sec11-card-r02.question_text: How should you pass a pedestrian or cyclist when the adjacent lane is not yet clear?
sec11-card-r02.teaching_text: Squeezing past inside the same lane risks clipping handlebars or a stumbled walker.

sec11-card-r03.question_text: Where should you steer when hazards sit on both sides at once?
sec11-card-r03.teaching_text: For example, an oncoming car plus a child walker shifts extra cushion toward the unprotected child.

sec11-card-r04.question_text: How do you separate hazards when overtaking a bicycle as an oncoming car approaches?
sec11-card-r04.teaching_text: Slowing briefly behind the cyclist turns a tight three-way squeeze into an easy solo pass.

sec11-card-r05.question_text: How large a time gap should you look for when changing lanes, entering, or merging?
sec11-card-r05.teaching_text: A four-second opening lets you slot smoothly between cars without forcing anyone to slam brakes.

sec11-card-r06.question_text: How much space remains ahead and behind when you center inside a four-second merge gap?
sec11-card-r06.teaching_text: Centering splits the four-second window into immediate two-second cushions until you rebuild three seconds.

sec11-card-r07.question_text: What rule applies whenever a traffic opening is too tight to preserve a safe cushion?
sec11-card-r07.teaching_text: Forcing into a cramped slot cuts off trailing traffic and leaves zero front braking margin.

sec11-card-r08.question_text: How must you move across several lanes of traffic?
sec11-card-r08.teaching_text: Sweeping diagonally across multiple lanes skips fresh mirror and blind-spot checks for each new lane.

sec11-card-r09.question_text: How big a gap do you need before pulling straight across an intersecting roadway?
sec11-card-r09.teaching_text: Stopping partway across leaves your side doors exposed to cross traffic in active lanes.

sec11-card-r10.question_text: What must your gap allow when turning onto a busy street to join traffic?
sec11-card-r10.teaching_text: Turning needs a bigger gap than crossing straight because you must accelerate up to flow pace.

sec11-card-r11.question_text: When is stopping halfway across a divided highway inside the median safe and allowed?
sec11-card-r11.teaching_text: Narrow islands leave your nose or tail jutting out into fast inside highway lanes.

sec11-card-r12.question_text: What must you verify about your destination path before starting a left turn?
sec11-card-r12.teaching_text: Starting a left turn toward a backed-up lane strands you sideways across oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-r13.question_text: May you enter an intersection on a green light when traffic ahead blocks your exit?
sec11-card-r13.teaching_text: Pulling into backed-up intersections traps your car in cross-traffic lanes when signals cycle red.

sec11-card-r14.question_text: What legal penalty can follow from blocking an intersection?
sec11-card-r14.teaching_text: Gridlocking busy cross streets blocks emergency responders and violates Montana intersection right-of-way rules.

sec11-card-r15.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out from a driveway solely because an approaching car has its turn signal blinking?
sec11-card-r15.teaching_text: Drivers forget signals on or aim for the next corner, causing T-bone crashes if you pull out early.

sec11-card-r16.question_text: Why are motorcycle turn signals especially risky to trust before pulling out?
sec11-card-r16.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack self-canceling switches, leaving indicators flashing miles after an earlier turn.

sec11-card-r17.question_text: What two conditions must both be met before overtaking another vehicle?
sec11-card-r17.teaching_text: Broken yellow lines permit passing legally, yet oncoming clearance must still guarantee safe return.

sec11-card-r18.question_text: How many vehicles should you generally overtake per pass?
sec11-card-r18.teaching_text: Leapfrogging strings of cars multiplies time in the opposing lane and blocks emergency return pockets.

sec11-card-r19.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, roughly how many seconds of passing time and oncoming gap are needed?
sec11-card-r19.teaching_text: Accelerating around a moving highway vehicle takes roughly ten full seconds from pull-out to return.

sec11-card-r20.question_text: When two 55 mph cars close toward each other over ten seconds, how much distance does each cover and need combined?
sec11-card-r20.teaching_text: Because both cars cover eight hundred plus feet toward one another, closing distance vanishes twice as fast.

sec11-card-r21.question_text: What is the rule if you feel unsure whether a distant oncoming car leaves enough passing room?
sec11-card-r21.teaching_text: Heat shimmer and flat two-lane perspectives hide how fast oncoming highway traffic is closing.

sec11-card-r22.question_text: How much clear distance or time ahead is needed to pass safely near a hill or curve?
sec11-card-r22.teaching_text: Anything shorter than one-third mile can hide an oncoming car closing at fifty-five miles per hour.

sec11-card-r23.question_text: Within what distance of a view-blocking hill or curve is starting a pass forbidden?
sec11-card-r23.teaching_text: Pulling left inside one-third mile of a blind crest gambles head-on survival against unseen traffic.

sec11-card-r24.question_text: Why is passing dangerous near intersections, railroad crossings, or shopping-center entrances?
sec11-card-r24.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out or turning left rarely expect an overtaking car charging up the opposing lane.

sec11-card-r25.question_text: Why scan ahead for walkers, cyclists, narrow shoulders, ice, or potholes before overtaking?
sec11-card-r25.teaching_text: A pothole or shoulder cyclist ahead can make the driver you are passing swerve straight into you.

sec11-card-r26.question_text: What return-space rule applies before starting any pass?
sec11-card-r26.teaching_text: Banking on tight traffic lines to open space for you leaves you stranded facing oncoming headlights.

sec11-card-r27.question_text: What visual check tells you it is safe to return to your lane after passing?
sec11-card-r27.teaching_text: Pulling right before both headlamps appear in your center mirror cuts across the passed bumper.

sec11-card-r28.question_text: Which three groups of vehicles carry the rear slow-moving emblem in Montana?
sec11-card-r28.teaching_text: Spotting the orange-red triangle warns you immediately that closing speed is forty-plus miles per hour.

sec11-card-r29.question_text: How should you approach and overtake a slow-moving vehicle?
sec11-card-r29.teaching_text: Wide farm implements often turn left into unmarked field gates just as impatient drivers try passing.

sec11-card-r30.question_text: Which animals on or near the roadway receive right-of-way from motorists?
sec11-card-r30.teaching_text: Montana ranching roads grant legal right-of-way to horses and livestock under human control.

sec11-card-r31.question_text: How should you respond near an animal or horse-drawn rig, especially if it approaches or crosses?
sec11-card-r31.teaching_text: Startled horses cannot stop like cars, so motorists must yield speed and halt whenever paths cross.

sec11-card-r32.question_text: What spacing and speed apply when overtaking an animal traveling in your direction?
sec11-card-r32.teaching_text: Buzzing close or fast throws gravel and wind blast that can spook a horse sideways into lanes.

sec11-card-r33.question_text: What sound restriction applies whenever driving near animals?
sec11-card-r33.teaching_text: Horns, revving engines, or shouts trigger panic bolts that endanger rider, animal, and car alike.

sec11-card-r34.question_text: What must you do if an animal appears frightened while you are passing?
sec11-card-r34.teaching_text: Halting quietly gives the rider or handler space to calm a rearing or skittish animal.

sec11-card-r35.question_text: What must a motorist do if an animal's rider or driver signals to stop?
sec11-card-r35.teaching_text: Handlers feel tension in the reins before motorists see panic, making their stop hand mandatory.

sec11-card-r36.question_text: How do traffic rules govern horseback riders, and where along the road must they ride?
sec11-card-r36.teaching_text: Road rules protect riders while requiring single-file travel along the right edge or usable shoulder.

sec11-card-r37.question_text: What three duties apply near a ridden or led horse along the roadway?
sec11-card-r37.teaching_text: Combining cautious pace with generous lateral clearance keeps roadside horses steady as you pass.

sec11-card-r38.question_text: What is the legal status of sounding your horn when approaching or passing a horse?
sec11-card-r38.teaching_text: Montana law explicitly outlaws horn blasts near horses because sudden noise can throw a rider.

sec11-card-r39.question_text: Why leave extra room near drivers at blocked entrances or backing out of spaces?
sec11-card-r39.teaching_text: Drivers backing between tall SUVs often cannot see cross traffic until half their car protrudes.

sec11-card-r40.question_text: Why widen your space around cars with obscured windows or walkers carrying low umbrellas or hats?
sec11-card-r40.teaching_text: Frosted side windows and tilted storm umbrellas blind people to vehicles right beside them.

sec11-card-r41.question_text: How should you adjust when another driver or pedestrian looks distracted?
sec11-card-r41.teaching_text: Someone staring at a phone or digging through bags can drift lanes or step into traffic unannounced.

sec11-card-r42.question_text: How should you treat drivers slowing without obvious reason or scanning street signs?
sec11-card-r42.teaching_text: Lost or unfamiliar drivers often brake abruptly or turn across lanes once spotting their street.

sec11-card-r43.question_text: What should you do if an overtaking driver misjudges and runs short on room to finish passing?
sec11-card-r43.teaching_text: Speeding up to punish a bad pass risks a fatal head-on crash right beside your window.

sec11-card-r44.question_text: How should you respond when another driver must change lanes abruptly in front of you?
sec11-card-r44.teaching_text: Closing the gap out of pride trades two seconds of patience for a multi-car highway sideswipe.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: Which two visual traits help you recognize a traffic sign and know what action it requires?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Spotting outline and color from down the highway gives you extra seconds to adjust speed before lettering sharpens.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: When thick fog hides a sign's words and color, which single visual feature may still identify it?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Recognizing an eight-sided silhouette or inverted triangle in whiteout glare stops you from blowing past hidden intersections.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: What obligation do Montana drivers have toward traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Treating painted lane stripes or overhead lights as optional suggestions invites side-impact crashes and instant citations.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: Into which three functional groups does the Montana manual organize traffic signs?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Sorting signs into laws, hazard alerts, and route directions tells you immediately whether a rule or caution applies.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: Which four traffic-control commands are communicated by red signs?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Red always flags an immediate right-of-way restriction or forbidden entry where hesitation causes head-on wrecks.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: How many sides does a STOP sign have, and what must you do before entering the intersection?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Rolling through an octagon at walking pace still counts as running a stop sign and risks broadside collisions.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt if a stop-controlled intersection includes a crosswalk?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Rolling across painted walk lines to peek around corners blocks pedestrians and puts your bumper in harm's way.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: What speed adjustment and right-of-way duty apply when you approach a YIELD sign?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: Dropping to a controllable pace lets you halt smoothly if a fast mainline vehicle closes the gap.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: Why must you stay out of any roadway posted with a Do Not Enter sign?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Driving past a Do Not Enter plaque can put you nose-to-nose with exit-ramp traffic or inside a closed zone.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: What rule applies whenever a red circle and diagonal slash cross over a black symbol or arrow?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Universal prohibition graphics cut through language barriers in a split second before you commit to an illegal turn.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: What two types of legal commands do regulatory signs post, and are they mandatory?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Ignoring a white regulatory panel carries the exact same ticket risk as disobeying a traffic light.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: What shape and color scheme identify the standard regulatory signs described in the Montana handbook?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: Crisp black-on-white vertical panels stand out cleanly against roadside trees and snowbanks so limits read clearly.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: Which maneuver is forbidden once you enter an area marked Do Not Pass?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: Engineers post Do Not Pass before blind hillcrests, curves, and intersections where oncoming cars hide from view.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: What changes once your vehicle passes a Pass With Care sign?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Leaving the restricted zone restores legal passing, yet you still own checking sight distance before pulling left.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: Which movement is outlawed at an intersection posted with a No U Turn sign?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Swinging a tight U-turn across busy cross-traffic or narrow medians stalls lanes and triggers T-bone wrecks.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: What movement does a No Left Turn sign forbid at that intersection?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Left-turn bans keep rush-hour corridors flowing and stop drivers from turning into one-way oncoming lanes.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: Which side of a roadway obstruction must you take when facing a Keep Right sign?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Steering left of a raised median island puts you straight into opposing lanes with nowhere to swerve.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: How far down the road does a posted speed-limit sign remain in effect?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Speeding up early just because buildings thin out draws tickets before the higher limit plaque actually appears.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: How can limited nighttime visibility affect driving at the posted maximum speed?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: Outrunning your headlight reach means wildlife or stalled rigs appear inside your stopping distance too late.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: What upcoming change does a Speed Zone Ahead sign warn you to prepare for?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Easing off the gas early lets you cross into town at the reduced limit without slamming the brakes.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: What colors and typical shape identify roadway hazard warning signs?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: High-contrast yellow diamonds pop against dark evergreens and gray winter skies far ahead of curves.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: Which advance hazard sign is the only round warning sign described in the Montana handbook?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Even caked in blowing snow, a circular sign silhouette unmistakably warns that train tracks cross ahead.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: What intersection layout and traffic hazard does a Crossroad warning sign announce?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: Hidden rural side roads can launch farm trucks straight across high-speed highways with little visual warning.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: What road alignment lies ahead when you pass a Winding Road warning sign?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Dropping speed before the first bend keeps weight balanced through linked mountain or canyon switchbacks.

sec05-card-f25.question_text: What happens to your straight-ahead path at a T-intersection warning sign?
sec05-card-f25.teaching_text: Missing a T-junction warning at night risks overrunning the crossroad into a ditch or fence line.

sec05-card-f26.question_text: What roadway junction does an angled Side Road warning symbol alert you to?
sec05-card-f26.teaching_text: Vehicles merging from diagonal junctions enter faster and with tougher blind-spot angles than square corners.

sec05-card-f27.question_text: What traffic conflict should you anticipate after seeing a right-side Side Road warning?
sec05-card-f27.teaching_text: Scanning the right treeline early spots pulling-out pickups before they creep into your travel lane.

sec05-card-f28.question_text: What road feature does a Sharp Right Turn warning sign prepare you to handle?
sec05-card-f28.teaching_text: Braking on the straight approach prevents front tires from washing across the centerline mid-corner.

sec05-card-f29.question_text: In what exact direction order does the road bend after a Sharp Left and Right Turn sign?
sec05-card-f29.teaching_text: Overcooking the opening left corner leaves your car off-balance right as the reverse right bend hits.

sec05-card-f30.question_text: Which two bends follow a Right and Left Curves warning sign, and in what order?
sec05-card-f30.teaching_text: Reading the bottom-to-top arrow sequence tells you which way to set up your lane position first.

sec05-card-f31.question_text: What hazard ahead is announced by a Railroad Crossing advance warning sign?
sec05-card-f31.teaching_text: Rural crossings often lack gates or bells, making early visual and audio checks your main protection.

sec05-card-f32.question_text: How should you respond to a School Ahead warning sign, and during what hours does caution apply?
sec05-card-f32.teaching_text: After-hours ballgames, playgrounds, and evening events bring kids near campus streets long past final bell.

sec05-card-f33.question_text: What traction hazard does a Loose Gravel warning sign announce ahead?
sec05-card-f33.teaching_text: Rolling stones act like marbles under tires, lengthening stops and kicking up windshield-cracking rocks if rushed.

sec05-card-f34.question_text: Why must you plan ahead before driving onto a span marked One Lane Bridge?
sec05-card-f34.teaching_text: Two vehicles cannot squeeze across simultaneously, so someone must yield before reaching the bridge deck.

sec05-card-f35.question_text: What animals and highway condition does a Range Cattle warning sign alert you to?
sec05-card-f35.teaching_text: Thousand-pound livestock wander freely across open-range asphalt, especially at dusk when dark hides blend in.

sec05-card-f36.question_text: What changes ahead at a Road Narrows sign, and can vehicles still meet and pass?
sec05-card-f36.teaching_text: Trimmed shoulders leave less margin for drift even though opposing cars can still pass each other carefully.

sec05-card-f37.question_text: What surface danger does an Icy Road warning sign alert drivers to?
sec05-card-f37.teaching_text: Shaded canyon bends and bridge decks stay frozen slick well after sunny highway stretches thaw dry.

sec05-card-f38.question_text: What action should you start taking as soon as you see a School Bus Stop Ahead sign?
sec05-card-f38.teaching_text: Cresting a hill at highway speed without slowing early leaves too little room for a stopped bus and kids.

sec05-card-f39.question_text: What response does a Stop Ahead warning sign require from an approaching driver?
sec05-card-f39.teaching_text: Trees, curves, or hills often hide the red octagon until the last few car lengths.

sec05-card-f40.question_text: What helpful number may be posted on a small plaque beneath a right-curve warning sign?
sec05-card-f40.teaching_text: Matching that advisory speed before turning in keeps lateral forces well inside dry-pavement tire grip.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: What two actions are called for when you pass a School Crossing Ahead warning sign?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: Kids focused on friends or phones can dart toward the painted walk from behind parked cars suddenly.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: What does the School Crossing sign mark, and what must you do when pedestrians wait there?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: Halting promptly when students wait at the curb prevents impatient kids from bolting into small traffic gaps.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: Which three precautions fit approaching a Pedestrian Crossing warning sign?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Mid-block trail and downtown crossings put walkers directly across travel lanes without signal lights.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: What must you do at a Low Clearance sign if your load or vehicle exceeds the posted height?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Wedging a tall camper, rack, or box truck under a low bridge shears roofs into trailing traffic.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: What brake check and transmission choice does a Hill warning sign prompt before descending?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Engine braking in a lower gear keeps steep Montana mountain grades from overheating brake pads into fade.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: What roadway layout starts at a Divided Highway Begins sign, and which side must you take?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Drifting left of the nose of a new divider puts you straight into opposing highway lanes.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: What traffic change does Divided Highway Ends warn of, and where do you position your car?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Forgetting the median ended makes drivers pull left to pass straight into oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: How should you drive past a Deer Crossing sign, especially if a deer comes into view?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: Where one deer bounds across pavement, two or three herd mates frequently trail right behind it.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: What specific farm activity takes place where a Cattle Crossing warning sign stands?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: Ranch hands moving a herd across pavement block both lanes completely around blind rural bends.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: Which three driving adjustments belong at a Slippery When Wet warning sign?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Sharp steering stabs or panic braking on polished wet asphalt break tire grip into an instant spin.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: Which basic background color marks construction and maintenance traffic-control devices?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: Fluorescent orange instantly alerts you that lane shifts, equipment, and crew members replace normal conditions.

sec05-card-r12.question_text: Which two sign outlines are used for work-area warning signs?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Recognizing both orange diamonds and rectangular info boards keeps you from missing lane-shift details.

sec05-card-r13.question_text: What do construction and maintenance signs warn of, and how must you approach the zone?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Drop-offs, milled pavement ridges, and backing dump trucks leave zero room for distracted highway speeds.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: What legal status applies if you drive faster than the posted limit inside a work zone?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Temporary orange speed postings carry full statutory teeth even when crews step briefly off the shoulder.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: What steering clue do the diagonal stripes on work-zone barricades or vertical panels give you?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Following the downward slant keeps your wheels out of open trenches when cones twist lanes at night.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: Which way must you steer when barricade stripes slope downward toward the right?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Picture rainwater rolling down the angled stripes straight onto the open lane you should take.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: Which way must you steer when work-panel stripes slope downward toward the left?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Steering toward the low end of the diagonal stripes guides you cleanly past shoulder excavations.

sec05-card-r18.question_text: How do cones, drums, tubes, panels, and barricades help drivers day and night in work zones?
sec05-card-r18.teaching_text: Steady or flashing top lights trace safe lane edges after dark when painted lines are ground off.

sec05-card-r19.question_text: What two jobs do lighted work-zone arrow panels perform day or night?
sec05-card-r19.teaching_text: Merging early when you spot a bright arrow panel prevents last-second bottleneck cut-ins at cones.

sec05-card-r20.question_text: Which three traffic-control actions may a work-zone flagger direct you to take?
sec05-card-r20.teaching_text: Single-lane alternating work zones rely on flaggers to keep opposing traffic from meeting head-on.

sec05-card-r21.question_text: What high-visibility gear and hand tools identify work-zone flaggers in the Montana handbook?
sec05-card-r21.teaching_text: Scanning ahead for bright orange vests and STOP-SLOW paddles stops rear-end pileups at sudden queues.

sec05-card-r22.question_text: What happens to traffic violation fines inside Montana work zones?
sec05-card-r22.teaching_text: Workers stand mere feet from highway fenders with only plastic cones between them and speeding cars.

sec05-card-r23.question_text: Do all Montana work zones share one standard limit, or who sets each zone's speed?
sec05-card-r23.teaching_text: Every project differs, so state, local, utility, or contractor crews post limits tailored to that site.

sec05-card-r24.question_text: What criminal charge can follow knowingly or negligently endangering people or property in a highway work zone?
sec05-card-r24.teaching_text: Aggressive weaving or speeding past road crews escalates a routine ticket into a serious criminal offense.

sec05-card-r25.question_text: What charge can result from removing, ignoring, or intentionally hitting a construction traffic-control device?
sec05-card-r25.teaching_text: Knocking down barricades or blowing past a flagger strips away the barrier keeping workers alive.

sec05-card-r26.question_text: During what times of day should you check speed and watch for children near schools and parks?
sec05-card-r26.teaching_text: Playgrounds, sports fields, and community events draw kids across neighborhood streets well into dark.

sec05-card-r27.question_text: How low may posted speed limits drop inside a Montana school zone?
sec05-card-r27.teaching_text: At fifteen miles per hour a driver can stop in a fraction of the distance needed at thirty.

sec05-card-r28.question_text: What must drivers do for pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections?
sec05-card-r28.teaching_text: Inching forward before walkers finish clearing puts pressure on children and hides them from adjacent lanes.

sec05-card-r29.question_text: Beyond campus grounds and adjoining streets, what else can a designated school zone cover?
sec05-card-r29.teaching_text: Kids walk several blocks to reach campus, so cities extend reduced-speed boundaries outward along feeder streets.

sec05-card-r30.question_text: Does a pedestrian in a school crosswalk hold right-of-way when no crossing guard is on duty?
sec05-card-r30.teaching_text: Painted school walk lines protect kids before morning guard shifts start and after afternoon shifts end.

sec05-card-r31.question_text: Why does the handbook tell you to stop well before a school crosswalk?
sec05-card-r31.teaching_text: Stopping right on top of the stripes hides small elementary students behind your hood from adjacent lanes.

sec05-card-r32.question_text: What is the rule when a column of schoolchildren is crossing a roadway?
sec05-card-r32.teaching_text: Squeezing through a gap in a class line invites a trailing child to run straight into your fender.

sec05-card-r33.question_text: What is prohibited while a school crossing guard holds the official STOP sign to direct children across?
sec05-card-r33.teaching_text: Until the guard lowers the stop paddle and clears the lane, late-running kids may still be crossing.

sec05-card-r34.question_text: Which three school-zone features can signal an authorized speed-limit reduction?
sec05-card-r34.teaching_text: Scanning pavement stencils, beacons, and roadside plaques together ensures you never miss active school hours.

sec05-card-r35.question_text: Which three areas do school-zone parking and stopping signs keep clear?
sec05-card-r35.teaching_text: Illegal parent drop-offs along red or signed curbs force kids to weave out blindly between tall SUVs.

sec05-card-r36.question_text: What happens to the fine amount if you are caught speeding in a Montana school zone?
sec05-card-r36.teaching_text: Doubled penalties hammer home that rushing past classrooms trades seconds for a child's life.

sec05-card-r37.question_text: Why can drivers never rely on young children near schools to judge traffic safely on their own?
sec05-card-r37.teaching_text: Young brains struggle to gauge how fast a car closes a block or what signal phases mean.

sec05-card-r38.question_text: What extra hazard do school pickup and drop-off crowds create in lots and nearby streets?
sec05-card-r38.teaching_text: Double-parked minivans, swinging doors, and backing parents demand crawling speeds and constant mirror checks.

sec01-card-f01.question_text: What vehicle class and maximum gross weight does a Montana basic Class D license cover?
sec01-card-f01.teaching_text: Stepping into commercial rigs or anything hitting twenty-six thousand pounds gross weight requires upgrading beyond basic Class D.

sec01-card-f03.question_text: What credential must drivers keep with them whenever operating a vehicle in Montana?
sec01-card-f03.teaching_text: Leaving your plastic credential at home turns an ordinary roadside stop into an avoidable citation.

sec01-card-f04.question_text: What insurance proof must remain inside the vehicle being driven?
sec01-card-f04.teaching_text: Borrowing a family or friend car still puts responsibility on you to confirm liability proof is inside before rolling.

sec01-card-f05.question_text: Which document and federal agency records must match the name and birth date on your Montana application?
sec01-card-f05.teaching_text: Even a small spelling mismatch or nickname versus federal records can stall your application at the counter.

sec01-card-f06.question_text: What federal identification number is required on a Montana license or ID application?
sec01-card-f06.teaching_text: Arriving without your nine-digit federal number stops both driver license and state identification paperwork cold.

sec01-card-f22.question_text: How does an active suspension or revocation in another state affect Montana driver licensing?
sec01-card-f22.teaching_text: National driver registries share sanction histories across state lines, so moving to Montana never erases an outside suspension.

sec01-card-f23.question_text: Which three categories of proof must an applicant aged eighteen or older provide?
sec01-card-f23.teaching_text: Showing up missing even one of the three document buckets forces a second trip before staff can issue credentials.

sec01-card-f24.question_text: What must adult applicants do with driver licenses issued elsewhere when getting licensed in Montana?
sec01-card-f24.teaching_text: Trying to pocket an old out-of-state plastic credential violates single-license rules when switching to Montana.

sec01-card-f25.question_text: What health-related requirement must adult applicants satisfy for their requested Montana license class?
sec01-card-f25.teaching_text: Physical qualification standards vary by license class so unsafe medical limitations are caught before solo highway driving.

sec01-card-f26.question_text: Which three court findings disqualify an adult applicant from Montana licensing?
sec01-card-f26.teaching_text: Adjudicated mental incompetence or habitual substance dependence legally bars issuance until proper legal restoration occurs.

sec01-card-f27.question_text: Who must consent for a minor applicant, and what responsibility does the signer accept?
sec01-card-f27.teaching_text: Co-signing a teen application is a serious legal commitment rather than a casual permission slip.

sec01-card-f28.question_text: How long after establishing permanent Montana residency may a newcomer drive on a valid former license?
sec01-card-f28.teaching_text: Letting your transfer slide past sixty straight days turns an otherwise valid out-of-state credential into unlicensed driving.

sec01-card-f29.question_text: Which evaluations are waived when exchanging a valid out-of-state basic license for a Montana license?
sec01-card-f29.teaching_text: Transferring while your former basic credential is still unexpired spares you both knowledge and driving evaluations.

sec01-card-f30.question_text: What evaluations can Montana require if an applicant may have impaired functional driving ability?
sec01-card-f30.teaching_text: Examiners can require full knowledge and behind-the-wheel demonstrations whenever physical or cognitive safety is uncertain.

sec01-card-f31.question_text: How many valid driver licenses may one person hold at the same time across all jurisdictions?
sec01-card-f31.teaching_text: Nationwide compacts prevent drivers from keeping backup credentials across states to hide traffic convictions.

sec01-card-f07.question_text: Who must directly supervise a student driving on a Montana traffic education permit?
sec01-card-f07.teaching_text: Course training permits cover school lessons with your instructor, not solo errands or unapproved family drives.

sec01-card-f08.question_text: How long does a Montana traffic education permit stay valid?
sec01-card-f08.teaching_text: Dropping or finishing the class ends training-permit privileges until you qualify for a regular learner permit.

sec01-card-f09.question_text: At what earliest age can someone get a learner permit through state-approved traffic education?
sec01-card-f09.teaching_text: Joint approval by Justice and Public Instruction is what unlocks Montana driving practice at fourteen and a half.

sec01-card-f10.question_text: Who must sit right beside a Class D learner-permit driver while driving?
sec01-card-f10.teaching_text: Putting your supervisor in the back seat breaks permit law because immediate front-seat intervention is required.

sec01-card-f11.question_text: What minimum age applies for a Montana learner permit without traffic education?
sec01-card-f11.teaching_text: Skipping approved driver education pushes your earliest learner-permit entry all the way to your sixteenth birthday.

sec01-card-f12.question_text: What course requirement must a fifteen-year-old meet to get a learner permit?
sec01-card-f12.teaching_text: Simply signing up is not enough at fifteen at a licensing station when full course completion is required.

sec01-card-f13.question_text: Which documents, fees, and station checks are required to obtain a Montana learner permit?
sec01-card-f13.teaching_text: Passing the knowledge check still will not earn a permit unless identity, presence, residence, fees, and vision clear too.

sec01-card-f14.question_text: What must happen before a teenager under eighteen may start licensing evaluations?
sec01-card-f14.teaching_text: Minors showing up solo cannot even sit for the written screening without signed adult consent in hand.

sec01-card-f15.question_text: What legal obligation does a parent, guardian, or responsible adult take on by signing a minor consent form?
sec01-card-f15.teaching_text: Any property or injury loss caused behind the wheel lands financially on the adult who co-signed.

sec01-card-f16.question_text: When is a learner-license permit issued, and how long does it remain valid?
sec01-card-f16.teaching_text: Passing the primary knowledge check starts a twelve-month window to log supervised miles and finish licensing.

sec01-card-f17.question_text: How long must a new driver under eighteen use a non-commercial learner permit?
sec01-card-f17.teaching_text: Turning sixteen mid-hold does not shorten the mandatory six straight months of supervised teen permit driving.

sec01-card-f18.question_text: Which two Montana agencies must approve a qualifying traffic education course?
sec01-card-f18.teaching_text: Courses lacking sign-off from both state agencies will not unlock early teen permit eligibility.

sec01-card-f19.question_text: Do online or third-party traffic education courses count as approved Montana traffic education?
sec01-card-f19.teaching_text: Buying an internet driver class wastes time and money because Montana rejects online and third-party substitutes.

sec01-card-f20.question_text: Can a Montana resident who holds a valid out-of-state driver license get a Montana ID?
sec01-card-f20.teaching_text: Keeping an unexpired out-of-state driving credential disqualifies you from picking up a separate Montana identification credential.

sec01-card-f21.question_text: May a person hold both a state identification credential and a driver license at once?
sec01-card-f21.teaching_text: State credential rules force a one-or-the-other choice so nobody carries duplicate government photo credentials.

sec01-card-f32.question_text: When may active-duty military members and dependents drive in Montana on a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-f32.teaching_text: Military orders preserve home-state driving privileges right up until off-base civilian employment enters the picture.

sec01-card-f33.question_text: What must a service member or dependent do upon becoming gainfully employed in Montana?
sec01-card-f33.teaching_text: Taking a local civilian paycheck ends out-of-state military reciprocity and triggers Montana licensing requirements.

sec01-card-f34.question_text: What must an eligible service member show to receive a military exemption on a Montana license?
sec01-card-f34.teaching_text: Showing active-duty military credentials adds exemption status that protects your license while deployed away from home.

sec01-card-f35.question_text: How does a military exemption change renewal timing during active service?
sec01-card-f35.teaching_text: Deployment schedules rarely line up with standard six-month windows, so exempt service members can renew early.

sec01-card-f36.question_text: How long after honorable separation does a military-exempt Montana license stay usable?
sec01-card-f36.teaching_text: Returning veterans get a three-month transition cushion after honorable discharge before standard renewal rules resume.

sec01-card-f37.question_text: What two legal statuses satisfy Montana proof of authorized presence?
sec01-card-f37.teaching_text: Every license applicant must establish either United States citizenship or lawful federal permission to stay.

sec01-card-f38.question_text: Which federal system does Montana use to verify a foreign national authorized presence?
sec01-card-f38.teaching_text: Electronic checks against the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements database confirm current immigration records.

sec01-card-f39.question_text: What caps the expiration date of a license issued to a temporarily authorized foreign national?
sec01-card-f39.teaching_text: State driving credentials cannot outlast underlying federal immigration authorization dates on USCIS paperwork.

sec01-card-f40.question_text: Which versions of a United States birth certificate prove authorized presence?
sec01-card-f40.teaching_text: Plain hospital souvenirs or uncertified photocopies get turned away when establishing citizenship at licensing counters.

sec01-card-f41.question_text: Which two federal form numbers report a citizen birth abroad for authorized presence?
sec01-card-f41.teaching_text: Americans born overseas prove citizenship through State Department or embassy birth-abroad reports rather than domestic certificates.

sec01-card-f42.question_text: When can a United States passport or passport credential establish authorized presence?
sec01-card-f42.teaching_text: An expired passport loses authorized-presence eligibility even though it once proved citizenship.

sec01-card-f43.question_text: What companion record must accompany a valid, unexpired foreign passport to prove authorized presence?
sec01-card-f43.teaching_text: A foreign passport alone shows nationality, whereas an unexpired I-94 endorsement or I-551 stamp proves lawful entry.

sec01-card-f44.question_text: Which three unexpired form numbers qualify a naturalization certificate as authorized-presence proof?
sec01-card-f44.teaching_text: Examiners verify both active validity and one of the three qualifying federal naturalization form numbers.

sec01-card-f45.question_text: Which three unexpired form numbers allow a citizenship certificate to prove authorized presence?

sec01-card-r01.question_text: What special marking makes an unexpired I-551 qualify for Northern Mariana authorized presence?

sec01-card-r02.question_text: What special marking on an unexpired I-551 establishes American Indian authorized presence?
sec01-card-r02.teaching_text: Treaty border-crossing credentials carry an American Indian designation rather than standard permanent-resident text.

sec01-card-r03.question_text: Which two unexpired federal form numbers qualify a citizen identification credential for authorized presence?
sec01-card-r03.teaching_text: Legacy federal citizen identification credentials remain acceptable presence proof whenever valid and unexpired.

sec01-card-r04.question_text: Which unexpired federal form proves permanent-resident authorized presence?
sec01-card-r04.teaching_text: Lawful permanent residents must bring an unexpired I-551 green credential so electronic status verification clears.

sec01-card-r05.question_text: Which unexpired federal form qualifies a temporary resident credential as authorized-presence proof?
sec01-card-r05.teaching_text: Temporary resident credentials only establish lawful presence while active and unexpired at the time of application.

sec01-card-r06.question_text: Which unexpired federal travel permit form can establish authorized presence?
sec01-card-r06.teaching_text: Federal re-entry permits on form I-327 confirm ongoing lawful status when presented valid and unexpired.

sec01-card-r07.question_text: Which unexpired federal travel document form establishes refugee authorized presence?
sec01-card-r07.teaching_text: Refugees traveling without a national passport rely on an unexpired I-571 travel document to verify presence.

sec01-card-r08.question_text: Which three unexpired employment authorization form numbers prove authorized presence?
sec01-card-r08.teaching_text: Federal work permits on I-688A, I-688B, or I-766 satisfy lawful-presence checks only before their expiration date.

sec01-card-r09.question_text: When can an unexpired refugee I-94 arrival-departure record prove authorized presence without a passport?
sec01-card-r09.teaching_text: Refugees often lack home-country passports, so federal officers attach a photo and refugee stamp directly onto I-94.

sec01-card-r10.question_text: When does a federally recognized tribe digital ID prove authorized presence in Montana?
sec01-card-r10.teaching_text: Tribal digital credentials must come from a Montana-reservation tribe and display image, birth date, and enrollment number.

sec01-card-r11.question_text: What document combinations establish your full legal name and birth date?
sec01-card-r11.teaching_text: Bringing two secondary records alone fails identity verification because at least one primary credential is mandatory.

sec01-card-r12.question_text: How long past expiration can a United States or Canadian color-photo license or ID still count as primary identity?
sec01-card-r12.teaching_text: Once a domestic or Canadian photo credential passes four years expired, it drops out of the primary identity tier.

sec01-card-r14.question_text: Which two birth-abroad form numbers serve as primary identity proof for a United States citizen?

sec01-card-r16.question_text: When does an unexpired Defense Department military ID count as primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r16.teaching_text: Active, reserve, retired, or dependent military credentials must show both a color or digital image and birth date.

sec01-card-r17.question_text: Which State Department travel credentials qualify as primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r17.teaching_text: Either a current passport book or wallet-sized passport credential satisfies primary identity verification on its own.

sec01-card-r18.question_text: What must accompany an unexpired foreign passport for it to serve as primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r18.teaching_text: Primary identity rules mirror presence rules by requiring a matching unexpired I-94 endorsement or I-551 stamp.

sec01-card-r19.teaching_text: Valid naturalization certificates on forms N-550, N-570, or N-578 cover both lawful status and primary identity.

sec01-card-r20.question_text: Which unexpired USCIS citizenship certificates count as primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r20.teaching_text: Unexpired USCIS citizenship forms N-560, N-561, and N-645 verify legal name and birth date in the primary tier.

sec01-card-r21.question_text: What must Northern Mariana or American Indian I-551 credentials display to count as primary identity?

sec01-card-r22.question_text: When do USCIS citizen ID forms I-179 or I-197 or permanent resident form I-551 count as primary identity?
sec01-card-r22.teaching_text: Letting a green credential expire past its printed date disqualifies it from serving as active primary identity.

sec01-card-r23.question_text: When do USCIS temporary resident, re-entry, refugee-travel, or employment authorization credentials qualify as primary identity?
sec01-card-r23.teaching_text: Forms I-688, I-327, I-571, I-688A, I-688B, and I-766 serve as primary identity only before expiring.

sec01-card-r24.question_text: What makes an unexpired USCIS I-94 without a passport count as primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r24.teaching_text: Without both the refugee designation and an attached photograph, a standalone I-94 cannot establish primary identity.

sec01-card-r25.question_text: When does a current US or Canadian learner permit or licensing receipt count as primary identity?
sec01-card-r25.teaching_text: Paper receipts lacking either your photograph or date of birth cannot verify primary identity at licensing counters.

sec01-card-r26.question_text: What three items must appear on a Montana Department of Corrections inmate ID for primary identity?
sec01-card-r26.teaching_text: Re-entering residents can use state corrections IDs for primary identity when photo, birth date, and offender number appear.

sec01-card-r27.question_text: What details must certified emergency photo IDs show, and which transactions reject them?
sec01-card-r27.teaching_text: Certified emergency photo IDs work only in person and never for mailed renewals or mailed duplicate requests.

sec01-card-r28.question_text: What higher-tier credential can fill the secondary identity document slot?
sec01-card-r28.teaching_text: Bringing two primary credentials like a passport and birth certificate satisfies identity without needing any secondary paper.

sec01-card-r29.question_text: Which United States or Canadian social-insurance credentials qualify as secondary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r29.teaching_text: Photocopies or laminated replicas get rejected because secondary identity rules require the original social card.

sec01-card-r30.question_text: Which marriage records qualify as secondary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r30.teaching_text: Ceremonial church keepsakes lack legal standing, whereas government-issued certified marriage records satisfy secondary proof.

sec01-card-r31.question_text: What expiration range allows a US or Canadian license or ID to serve as secondary identity?
sec01-card-r31.teaching_text: Credentials past five years expired lose even secondary identity value and cannot support an application.
sec01-card-r31.must_match_memory_hook: Expired over one through five years

sec01-card-r32.question_text: Which workplace badge counts as secondary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r32.teaching_text: Private company employee badges do not count, whereas current US or Canadian government photo IDs do.

sec01-card-r33.question_text: How does Montana classify a current US or Canadian license or ID without a color photo?
sec01-card-r33.teaching_text: Lacking a color portrait drops an otherwise current domestic or Canadian credential from primary down to secondary.

sec01-card-r34.question_text: What must a certified US or Canadian court order show to count as secondary identity?
sec01-card-r34.teaching_text: Court judgments missing either your full legal name or birth date cannot verify secondary identity.

sec01-card-r35.question_text: How long after expiration can an otherwise primary USCIS document serve as secondary identity?
sec01-card-r35.teaching_text: Recently lapsed USCIS primary credentials get a twelve-month secondary identity window, though presence still needs active proof.

sec01-card-r36.question_text: How is a certified birth certificate from outside the US and Canada classified for identity?
sec01-card-r36.teaching_text: Certified overseas birth records support secondary identity when paired alongside an accepted primary credential.

sec01-card-r37.question_text: Which Defense Department separation record qualifies as secondary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r37.teaching_text: Veterans can pair Defense Department discharge certifications with one primary record to finish identity proof.

sec01-card-r38.question_text: What two details let a Medicare, Medicaid, or health-insurance credential count as secondary identity?
sec01-card-r38.teaching_text: Family plan cards that omit your personal member number or name will not clear secondary identity checks.

sec01-card-r39.question_text: Who must issue an unexpired color-photo weapon or firearm permit used for secondary identity?
sec01-card-r39.teaching_text: Permits must remain unexpired, carry a color photo, and come from an organized police chief or local US sheriff.

sec01-card-r40.question_text: Which aviation credential qualifies as secondary identity evidence in Montana?
sec01-card-r40.teaching_text: An active Federal Aviation Administration pilot certificate pairs cleanly with one primary identity record.

sec01-card-r41.question_text: What must certified school records or transcripts show to qualify as secondary identity?
sec01-card-r41.teaching_text: Teens without work or marriage records often use certified school transcripts showing full name and ideally birth date.

sec01-card-r42.question_text: When does a Montana-approved driver education completion certificate count as secondary identity?
sec01-card-r42.teaching_text: Your green-light completion slip doubles as secondary identity whenever both full name and birth date appear.

sec01-card-r43.question_text: What three elements make a school ID qualify as secondary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r43.teaching_text: Last year's student badge or one missing a student ID number will not pass secondary verification.

sec01-card-r44.question_text: When can a child certified birth certificate or copy support a parent secondary identity?
sec01-card-r44.teaching_text: Even a photocopy or fax of a certified child birth record works if it prints the parent name and birth date.

sec01-card-r45.question_text: What two addresses must original applicants give if mail cannot reach their Montana home?
sec01-card-r45.teaching_text: Post office boxes can receive your plastic credential by mail, yet physical Montana residence still needs proof.

sec01-card-r46.question_text: What two exact items must appear on a Montana residence-evidence document?
sec01-card-r46.teaching_text: Every residence proof item must match the exact physical Montana street or rural address written on your application.

sec01-card-r47.question_text: When can an identity record, prior-year US or Montana tax return, or Montana voter card prove residence?
sec01-card-r47.teaching_text: Voter registrations or prior-year income returns double as residency proof whenever your name and physical address print clearly.

sec01-card-r48.question_text: Which tax receipt or insurance policies can establish Montana residence when showing name and home address?
sec01-card-r48.teaching_text: Last year's Montana property-tax receipt or a current auto or life policy confirms where you live.

sec01-card-r49.question_text: How recent must attendance be for certified school records to prove Montana residence?
sec01-card-r49.teaching_text: Certified school records prove Teen residency only when attendance falls within four months and lists your home address.

sec01-card-r50.question_text: How can a parent, guardian, responsible adult, or adult child confirm shared Montana residence?
sec01-card-r50.teaching_text: Teens without bills in their own name rely on a family member written note backed by qualifying address proof.

sec01-card-r51.question_text: What makes a rental agreement or rent receipt acceptable as Montana residence proof?
sec01-card-r51.teaching_text: Unsigned printouts fail verification because landlords or rental agents must sign the original lease or receipt.

sec01-card-r52.question_text: When do mortgage or home-equity papers prove residence, and when is a rural address allowed?
sec01-card-r52.teaching_text: Rural descriptions work on mortgage papers when ranches or country homes have no standard street numbering.

sec01-card-r53.question_text: What date limit applies to pay stubs, bank statements, utility bills, or canceled mail for residency?
sec01-card-r53.teaching_text: Grabbing a six-month-old utility bill or pay stub gets rejected because residency mail must stay within four months.

sec01-card-r54.question_text: What three items establish address requirements for an applicant experiencing homelessness?
sec01-card-r54.teaching_text: Social-service letterhead verifying location plus a separate mailing address keeps licensing accessible without a street lease.

sec01-card-r55.question_text: What condition applies to required documents across every REAL ID step?
sec01-card-r55.teaching_text: Crossed-out lines or uncertified copies stall federal credential upgrades because every step demands unaltered, verified records.

sec01-card-r56.question_text: Which three items must the REAL ID identity step prove?
sec01-card-r56.teaching_text: Federal credential rules bundle current legal name, birth date, and citizenship or lawful presence into step one.

sec01-card-r57.question_text: What must Social Security proof display for REAL ID, and how is it verified?
sec01-card-r57.teaching_text: Pay stubs masking the first five digits fail because full nine-digit numbers must show for federal verification.

sec01-card-r58.question_text: How many residency documents does REAL ID require, and what expiration limit applies?
sec01-card-r58.teaching_text: Unlike standard licensing, federal credential upgrades require two physical-address records that are unexpired or within one year.

sec01-card-r59.question_text: May the two REAL ID residency documents come from the same document category?
sec01-card-r59.teaching_text: Bringing two utility bills or two bank statements works fine since different categories are not required.

sec01-card-r60.question_text: What must a REAL ID applicant document whenever current legal name differs from earlier records?
sec01-card-r60.teaching_text: Multiple marriages or court orders require an unbroken paper trail linking your birth record to today's name.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: Why should you switch headlights on whenever seeing other road users becomes difficult?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: If dim light or haze hides traffic from you, oncoming drivers struggle equally to spot your unlit car.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: What brief lighting signal can alert another road user to your presence when needed?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: One quick headlamp flick catches peripheral vision silently before a distracted driver pulls across your lane.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: What lighting step accompanies running windshield wipers in rain, snow, or fog?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: Spray and mist swallow unlit bumpers from behind unless headlamps and taillamps come on together.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: When during evening twilight should you switch your headlights on?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Waiting for pitch blackness leaves dark cars blended into grey dusk pavement during evening rush.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: Which lights must you run instead of parking lights whenever driving conditions require illumination?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Dim marker bulbs fool oncoming motorists into thinking your moving car is parked stationary.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: Why run headlights when driving away from a low rising or setting sun?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: With blinding glare behind your back, oncoming drivers stare straight into sunwash that hides dark hoods.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: What core safety goal governs when to sound your horn?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Treating the horn strictly as a crash-prevention alert keeps surrounding drivers responsive when danger strikes.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: How should you sound the horn when warning someone without immediate collision danger?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: A brief tap gets attention cleanly without startling someone into a panic swerve.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: What horn signal alerts a pedestrian or bicyclist about to step or drift into your lane?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: An early gentle tap lets walkers or riders check back calmly before entering your path.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: What horn alert fits when a car begins drifting into your lane as you overtake?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: You are likely tucked in their side blind spot, and a quick tap stops the sideswipe.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: How should you alert an inattentive driver who appears not to see your vehicle?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Catching a distracted driver early with a short tap restores awareness before paths cross.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: Where can a light horn tap announce your approach before anyone is even in sight?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Sound carries around tight mountain bends, steep crests, and narrow alleys where sightlines vanish.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: What horn warning applies if a child or older person is about to step or ride into the street?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Immediate danger to a child or senior demands an unmistakable sharp warning right away.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: What horn action fits when another vehicle is moments away from striking yours?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: A firm sharp blast gives an encroaching driver one last instant to steer back.

sec10-card-f15.question_text: What warning must you give if you lose control of your car while sliding toward someone?
sec10-card-f15.teaching_text: Loud urgent warning gives bystanders precious split seconds to jump clear of an uncontrollable slide.

sec10-card-f16.question_text: May you honk just to push another driver to hurry up or move out of the way?
sec10-card-f16.teaching_text: Bullying slower motorists with horn blasts fuels road rage and panicked mistakes.

sec10-card-f17.question_text: Why shouldn't you honk to call out a driver mistake or wave hello to friends?
sec10-card-f17.teaching_text: Surrounding traffic hears a horn as an emergency hazard cue, not social chatter or critique.

sec10-card-f18.question_text: How should you treat your horn around visually impaired pedestrians?
sec10-card-f18.teaching_text: Pedestrians navigating by cane or guide dog rely on natural traffic audio that horn blasts disorient.

sec10-card-f19.question_text: How should you use an onboard phone or two-way radio when your vehicle breaks down?
sec10-card-f19.teaching_text: Alerting dispatchers quickly brings roadside protection and clears hazardous shoulder stops faster.

sec10-card-f20.question_text: Where should you steer whenever mechanical trouble forces a stop?
sec10-card-f20.teaching_text: Coasting onto a wide shoulder or lot while momentum remains keeps your car out of high-speed lanes.

sec10-card-f21.question_text: Which warning lights should you switch on whenever stopping for vehicle trouble?
sec10-card-f21.teaching_text: Simultaneous blinking hazard lamps tell approaching motorists immediately that your car is disabled.

sec10-card-f22.question_text: If a disabled car cannot get off the road, where must you avoid stopping?
sec10-card-f22.teaching_text: Halting just past a hillcrest or tight curve hides your stalled bumper until oncoming cars cannot stop.

sec10-card-f23.question_text: Where do emergency warning triangles or markers belong around a stopped vehicle?
sec10-card-f23.teaching_text: Spacing reflective warnings well behind your bumper alerts highway traffic while stopping room remains.

sec10-card-f24.question_text: How can you warn approaching drivers safely if you have no flares or triangles?
sec10-card-f24.teaching_text: Standing well clear off the pavement while waving white fabric warns drivers without putting you in lanes.

sec10-card-f25.question_text: What rule governs standing in a travel lane or changing a flat tire that puts you in one?
sec10-card-f25.teaching_text: No flat tire or rim is worth kneeling inches from seventy-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec10-card-f26.question_text: Which two non-electric signals tell passing patrols or motorists you have an emergency?
sec10-card-f26.teaching_text: Popping your hood or tying white cloth to a mirror, handle, or antenna signals distress even with a dead battery.

sec10-card-f27.question_text: Which position next to another moving car should you avoid lingering in?
sec10-card-f27.teaching_text: Hovering off someone's rear fender plants your nose squarely inside their worst mirror blind zone.

sec10-card-f28.question_text: What two simple speed moves get you out of another vehicle's blind spot?
sec10-card-f28.teaching_text: Either pulling cleanly into side vision or dropping into mirror view restores visibility right away.

sec10-card-f29.question_text: How should you move through another driver's blind spot while overtaking?
sec10-card-f29.teaching_text: Creeping past at one mile per hour faster leaves you vulnerable to an unannounced lane drift.

sec10-card-f30.question_text: Why must you never cruise alongside a large truck or passenger bus?
sec10-card-f30.teaching_text: Tall commercial rigs carry massive side No-Zones that can swallow an entire sedan from mirror sight.

sec10-card-f31.question_text: Why warn surrounding drivers before slowing down or changing direction?
sec10-card-f31.teaching_text: Signaling or tapping brakes before moving gives everyone nearby seconds to adjust smoothly.

sec10-card-f32.question_text: Which five everyday driving maneuvers require turning on your directional signal beforehand?
sec10-card-f32.teaching_text: Every lateral shift from curb parking to highway passing relies on advance blinker communication.

sec10-card-f33.question_text: Should you still signal a turn or lane change when the street looks completely empty?
sec10-card-f33.teaching_text: The bicyclist, pedestrian, or dark car you failed to see is the exact person who needs your blinker.

sec10-card-f34.question_text: What three steps set up a left turn well ahead of the corner?
sec10-card-f34.teaching_text: Moving near the centerline early keeps right-side room open and tells followers your exact plan.

sec10-card-f35.question_text: How many feet ahead of a turn must you signal in town versus in rural areas?
sec10-card-f35.teaching_text: Higher rural highway speeds cover ground three times faster, tripling required blinker lead distance.

sec10-card-f36.question_text: Which traffic has right-of-way before you turn left across a two-way street?
sec10-card-f36.teaching_text: Misjudging oncoming speed during left turns is a top intersection severe-crash cause.

sec10-card-f37.question_text: How must your front wheels point while paused waiting for a gap to turn left, and why?
sec10-card-f37.teaching_text: Pre-cocked front wheels launch your car straight into oncoming traffic if rear-ended from behind.

sec10-card-f38.question_text: Where on the cross street should your vehicle enter when completing a left turn?
sec10-card-f38.teaching_text: Cutting corners diagonally sweeps your left front bumper straight across opposing stop-line traffic lanes.

sec10-card-f39.question_text: What two follow-up checks belong right after completing a left turn?
sec10-card-f39.teaching_text: Leaving a left blinker flashing down the next block misleads cross-street drivers ahead.

sec10-card-f40.question_text: How should you position your car ahead of a planned right turn?
sec10-card-f40.teaching_text: Staying close to the right curb blocks impatient cyclists or cars from squeezing inside your turn.

sec10-card-f41.question_text: What wide-swing errors must you avoid while completing a right turn?
sec10-card-f41.teaching_text: Swinging left before or after a right turn clips adjacent traffic expecting you inside your lane.

sec10-card-f42.question_text: When should you turn your blinker on if a driveway or alley sits right before your corner?
sec10-card-f42.teaching_text: Signaling too early tricks drivers waiting in the first driveway into pulling out across you.

sec10-card-f43.question_text: What timing applies if another car waits to pull out between you and your upcoming turn?
sec10-card-f43.teaching_text: Holding your blinker until passing their bumper keeps the waiting driver safely stopped.

sec10-card-f44.question_text: What must you do after a gentle lane change or shallow turn leaves your blinker flashing?
sec10-card-f44.teaching_text: Gentle highway steering angles rarely trip automatic blinker return levers on their own.

sec10-card-f45.question_text: How early should you begin easing speed ahead of a stop or turn?
sec10-card-f45.teaching_text: Gradual deceleration preserves tire traction and gives drivers behind plenty of notice.

sec10-card-f46.question_text: How can you use your brake pedal to alert following traffic before a sudden stop?
sec10-card-f46.teaching_text: Flashing red brake lamps three or four quick times catches distracted eyes faster than steady glow.

sec10-card-f47.question_text: Why must you warn trailing drivers early when turning off a highway without a separate exit lane?
sec10-card-f47.teaching_text: Decelerating inside the main high-speed lane surprises followers unless blinkers and brake taps start early.

sec10-card-f48.question_text: Why warn drivers behind early before parking or turning into a spot right before an intersection?
sec10-card-f48.teaching_text: Traffic behind assumes you are rolling up to the intersection light unless warned ahead.

sec10-card-f49.question_text: Why warn following motorists before braking for stalled traffic or debris ahead of your hood?
sec10-card-f49.teaching_text: Drivers behind cannot see road hazards screened by your trunk until your brake lights flash.

sec10-card-f50.question_text: Why must every licensed driver still know arm hand signals?
sec10-card-f50.teaching_text: Fuses blow, bulbs burn out, and bright glare washes lenses when cyclists or drivers signal by arm.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: Which four factors must every safe speed choice weigh together?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Matching the sign alone fails whenever traffic density, weather sightlines, or rough surfaces demand less.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: For which three roadway features or surface conditions must you drop speed beforehand?
sec10-card-r02.teaching_text: Entering bends, ice patches, or puddles too fast overwhelms tire friction before steering can recover.

sec10-card-r03.question_text: Which two broad conditions govern how much tire grip you actually have?
sec10-card-r03.teaching_text: Brand-new tread still slides on glare ice, and dry asphalt cannot save bald rubber.

sec10-card-r04.question_text: Where should you look up the proper inflation pressure for your vehicle's tires?
sec10-card-r04.teaching_text: Sidewall numbers print maximum casing ratings rather than the vehicle maker's recommended everyday pressure.

sec10-card-r05.question_text: Why must you drive slower on unpaved dirt or gravel roads?
sec10-card-r05.teaching_text: Rolling stones act like ball bearings underfoot, lengthening stops and kicking tails sideways on turns.

sec10-card-r06.question_text: How do washboard ripples and potholes on gravel affect a moving vehicle?
sec10-card-r06.teaching_text: Rapid chatter bounces tires off loose stone and skates your car toward roadside ditches.

sec10-card-r07.question_text: Which headlight setting helps other motorists spot you through gravel-road dust?
sec10-card-r07.teaching_text: Low beams pierce hanging dust clouds cleanly without reflecting bright glare back into your eyes.

sec10-card-r08.question_text: What signs and oncoming action must you stay ready for on narrow dirt or gravel routes?
sec10-card-r08.teaching_text: One-lane timber or ranch bridges leave room for only one rig at a time.

sec10-card-r09.question_text: When should you slow for a curve, and why avoid braking mid-turn?
sec10-card-r09.teaching_text: Combining cornering side loads with heavy mid-curve braking snaps tires loose into a slide.

sec10-card-r10.question_text: What speed adjustment belongs the moment rain, snow, or sleet begins falling?
sec10-card-r10.teaching_text: Tire traction drops immediately below dry-pavement levels as soon as moisture coats asphalt.

sec10-card-r11.question_text: By roughly how much does Montana advise reducing speed on a wet road?
sec10-card-r11.teaching_text: Shaving about ten miles per hour off dry speeds offsets longer wet braking and hydroplaning.

sec10-card-r12.question_text: How much should you reduce speed when driving on packed snow?
sec10-card-r12.teaching_text: Hard-packed winter snow slashes friction so sharply that halving normal pace is essential.

sec10-card-r13.question_text: What traction equipment helps when roads are covered with snow?
sec10-card-r13.teaching_text: Winter tread compounds or tire chains bite into snowpack where summer rubber spins helplessly.

sec10-card-r14.question_text: What pace and trip choice does Montana advise when roads turn icy?
sec10-card-r14.teaching_text: Even four-wheel drive cannot shorten braking on sheet ice, making staying parked smartest.

sec10-card-r15.question_text: Why should you stay inside your vehicle if stranded during a Montana snowstorm?
sec10-card-r15.teaching_text: Walking into whiteout winds disorients drivers fast, while plows and rescuers spot stranded cars.

sec10-card-r16.question_text: Which sections of roadway freeze earliest and stay icy longest on cold, damp days?
sec10-card-r16.teaching_text: Tree-lined cuts and north-facing hills block winter sun, hiding surprise black ice on dry-looking drives.

sec10-card-r17.question_text: Why watch bridge decks closely even when approaching highway asphalt feels completely dry?
sec10-card-r17.teaching_text: Freezing wind chills elevated bridge decks from both above and below while ground warms regular roadbeds.

sec10-card-r18.question_text: How does ice right around the freezing point compare with subzero ice?
sec10-card-r18.teaching_text: Melting water film atop thirty-two-degree ice acts like grease, cutting grip to half of bitter cold.

sec10-card-r19.question_text: Why are the first minutes of rain on hot pavement extra slick?
sec10-card-r19.teaching_text: Light drizzle lifts baked oil and rubber dust into a slick film before heavy rain washes it off.

sec10-card-r20.question_text: What happens beneath your tires during hydroplaning?
sec10-card-r20.teaching_text: Once water wedges faster than tread grooves drain, steering and braking vanish completely.

sec10-card-r21.question_text: What is the single best way to prevent hydroplaning on wet highways?
sec10-card-r21.teaching_text: Lower speed gives tire tread channels time to squeeze standing water out beneath each footprint.

sec10-card-r22.question_text: What should your right foot do if your tires start floating on standing water?
sec10-card-r22.teaching_text: Smoothly releasing throttle lets speed drop naturally until tire tread settles back onto pavement.

sec10-card-r23.question_text: How should you hold the steering wheel while hydroplaning?
sec10-card-r23.teaching_text: Cranking the wheel while floating sets front tires sideways, snapping the car violently once grip returns.

sec10-card-r24.question_text: When may you resume normal braking or steering after hydroplaning?
sec10-card-r24.teaching_text: Touching the brake pedal before tire rubber reconnects firmly with asphalt triggers an immediate skid.

sec10-card-r25.question_text: What physical loss triggers the start of a vehicle skid?
sec10-card-r25.teaching_text: Whenever braking, cornering, or throttle forces exceed available friction, rubber breaks traction and slides.

sec10-card-r26.question_text: What two immediate steps begin recovery the instant your car starts sliding?
sec10-card-r26.teaching_text: Your hands naturally steer where your eyes aim, so look down your safe lane instead of the ditch.

sec10-card-r27.question_text: What should you do with the brake pedal while recovering a sliding vehicle?
sec10-card-r27.teaching_text: Pressing brakes mid-slide locks rolling wheels and kills the steering traction needed to straighten out.

sec10-card-r28.question_text: After steering toward your desired lane during a skid, what must happen as the car straightens?
sec10-card-r28.teaching_text: Holding recovery lock too long whips the tail into an opposite fishtail skid.

sec10-card-r29.question_text: How long must you keep making smooth steering corrections during skid recovery?
sec10-card-r29.teaching_text: Stopping after the first counter-steer misses smaller secondary swings before the chassis settles straight.

sec10-card-r30.question_text: At what two times of day are wildlife crossings busiest, and how should you respond on spotting one?
sec10-card-r30.teaching_text: Deer and elk feed actively around sunrise and sunset when low light hides dark coats.

sec10-card-r31.question_text: What steering mistake must you avoid when an animal jumps out too close to stop?
sec10-card-r31.teaching_text: Violent swerves trade a deer strike for fatal rollovers, trees, or head-on oncoming crashes.

sec10-card-r32.question_text: What should you always expect right after one deer or elk crosses the road?
sec10-card-r32.teaching_text: Fixating on the first deer that cleared pavement blinds drivers to two more bolting right behind.

sec10-card-r33.question_text: How should you pace yourself within traffic flow, and when should you pass?
sec10-card-r33.teaching_text: Weaving constantly around cars flowing smoothly multiplies lane-change conflicts while saving almost zero trip time.

sec10-card-r34.question_text: What should you do when cars stack up behind your slower vehicle?
sec10-card-r34.teaching_text: Stepping into a safe turnout clears impatient queues before someone gambles a blind two-lane pass.

sec10-card-r35.question_text: What signal and two visual checks accompany every highway merge?
sec10-card-r35.teaching_text: Ramp angles hide fast right-lane cars from mirrors unless you turn over your shoulder too.

sec10-card-r36.question_text: How should you use a highway acceleration ramp before blending into main lanes?
sec10-card-r36.teaching_text: Entering seventy-mile-per-hour traffic at forty forces trucks behind into dangerous emergency swerves.

sec10-card-r37.question_text: Why must you never drive to the end of an entrance ramp and stop?
sec10-card-r37.teaching_text: Stopping at the ramp tip leaves zero runway left to reach highway speed into gaps.

sec10-card-r38.question_text: How can drivers on a controlled-access highway help ramp traffic enter safely?
sec10-card-r38.teaching_text: Sliding into an empty left lane opens the entire right lane for incoming ramp drivers.

sec10-card-r39.question_text: When leaving via an exit ramp, in what order do you signal, enter the ramp, and slow down?
sec10-card-r39.teaching_text: Braking hard on the main interstate before peeling onto the exit ramp invites high-speed rear-ends.

sec10-card-r40.question_text: How do you exit a fast two-lane road safely when traffic follows behind?
