sec10-card-r40.teaching_text: Dragging speed miles early frustrates followers, whereas brake taps plus prompt safe slowing communicates clearly.

sec10-card-r41.question_text: Why watch trucks and underpowered cars carefully on steep grades or highway entries?
sec10-card-r41.teaching_text: Loaded semis shed thirty-plus miles per hour climbing passes and need far longer to accelerate.

sec10-card-r42.question_text: At what speed do farm tractors, buggies, and road machines usually travel, and what rear marker is required?
sec10-card-r42.teaching_text: Closing on a twenty-five-mile-per-hour tractor from highway speed takes only seconds once spotted.

sec10-card-r43.question_text: How many delayed vehicles require a slow-moving driver to pull off at a safe turnout?
sec10-card-r43.teaching_text: Montana law sets four trailing cars as the trigger to use the next safe turnout.

sec10-card-r44.question_text: Which lane must slow-moving traffic use on a multilane roadway?
sec10-card-r44.teaching_text: Camping in left or center lanes below flow pace forces dangerous right-side passing.

sec10-card-r45.question_text: How should you adjust speed in crowded zones where people and cars leave little maneuvering room?
sec10-card-r45.teaching_text: Without open side escape lanes, slower speed is your only defense when someone steps out.

sec10-card-r46.question_text: Around which busy commercial zones and narrow structures must you stay poised to slow?
sec10-card-r46.teaching_text: Shopping lots, downtown blocks, narrow bridges, tunnels, and toll plazas compress lanes and multiply sudden stops.

sec10-card-r47.question_text: What specific hazard demands extra vigilance near schools, playgrounds, and home streets?
sec10-card-r47.teaching_text: Focused on play rather than traffic, young kids bolt between parked SUVs without glancing either way.

sec10-card-r48.question_text: Roughly how many total feet can reacting and stopping from 50 mph take even on dry pavement with good gear?
sec10-card-r48.teaching_text: Drivers drastically underestimate that stopping from fifty eats more than a full football field.

sec10-card-r49.question_text: Roughly how many feet can stopping from 30 mph take on dry pavement with good tires and brakes?
sec10-card-r49.teaching_text: Even neighborhood thirty-mile-per-hour pace consumes roughly two hundred feet once reaction distance counts.

sec10-card-r50.question_text: What rule connects nighttime speed to the distance lit by your headlights?
sec10-card-r50.teaching_text: If fifty requires four hundred feet yet low beams show one hundred, highway speeds overdrive your eyes.

sec10-card-r51.question_text: Why must you run headlights in rain, fog, or falling snow?
sec10-card-r51.teaching_text: Even midday snow or fog hides unlit cars until oncoming traffic closes dangerously near.

sec10-card-r52.question_text: Above what speed does Montana warn driving becomes unsafe when heavy rain, fog, or snow cuts visibility to 200 feet?
sec10-card-r52.teaching_text: Since dry stopping from thirty already takes two hundred feet, going faster in storms guarantees overrunning hazards.

sec10-card-r53.question_text: What should you do when a heavy downpour cuts vision below what safe driving requires?
sec10-card-r53.teaching_text: Pressing forward blind through sheet rain gambles against stalled cars sitting unseen ahead.

sec10-card-r54.question_text: How fast may you approach a hillcrest or curve that hides the lane ahead?
sec10-card-r54.teaching_text: Assuming empty pavement beyond a blind bend leaves zero margin for fallen rock, livestock, or stopped cars.

sec10-card-r55.question_text: Why give parked vehicles along the street as much lateral room as possible?
sec10-card-r55.teaching_text: Tall pickups and vans screen stepping doors and children crossing between bumpers.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: Why must you keep hanging items off the mirror and view-blocking decals off the windshield?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Swinging mirror charms and windshield stickers create blind spots wide enough to hide pedestrians at crosswalks.

sec04-card-f02.question_text: How much effectiveness can dirty headlamps, backup lights, brake lights, and taillights lose?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Road grime and winter slush can slash lamp brightness by fifty percent even with brand-new bulbs.

sec04-card-f03.question_text: When should you check and adjust your seat and mirror settings?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Reaching for seat levers or mirror knobs after rolling pulls eyes and hands off steering.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: How high should you set the driver seat, and what aid helps if needed?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Peering barely above the dashboard hides pavement hazards right in front of your bumper.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: What problem tells you the driver seat is slid too far forward?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Jamming your chest against the wheel cramps arm motion and puts you dangerously close to airbag deployment.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: What view should the interior rearview mirror frame?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: Centering the full rear glass lets quick eye glances spot fast-closing traffic without turning your head.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: How should outside mirrors be angled when checked with a slight forward lean?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Pushing side mirrors outward until body metal appears only on a slight lean shrinks adjacent blind zones.

sec04-card-f08.question_text: How should you set a day-and-night interior mirror before driving?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Leaving night-dimmed glass flipped during daylight dulls reflections, while daytime angle at night invites glare.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: What injury is a vehicle head restraint designed to reduce, and in what kind of crash?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions whip an unsupported neck backward violently unless a properly raised restraint catches your head.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: Where should a properly adjusted head restraint make contact?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Leaving the pad down behind your neck acts like a pivot instead of catching the back of your skull.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: Who does Montana hold legally responsible for making sure occupants wear belts or use child seats?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Unless a narrow legal exemption applies, the person behind the wheel answers for unrestrained passengers.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: Does driving a short distance at low speed excuse skipping your safety belt?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Many serious crashes happen close to home at everyday neighborhood speeds where unbuckled riders slam interiors.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: What two restraint steps belong right before pulling away?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Taking five seconds before shifting out of park ensures nobody rides unprotected once traffic speeds rise.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: What should you do with vehicle doors before driving away?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Locked latches help keep doors closed during rollovers or side impacts while preventing unwanted entry at stops.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: How must a lap-and-shoulder restraint system be worn for full intended protection?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Tucking the shoulder strap behind your back throws upper-body crash forces onto your spine and pelvis.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: What must you still fasten manually in a car equipped with an automatic shoulder belt?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Riding with an motorized shoulder strap alone lets you submarine forward underneath during a frontal crash.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: What happens to crash protection if you wear only one portion of a lap-and-shoulder belt?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Lap and shoulder webbing are engineered as one team, so skipping either half substantially cuts survival odds.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: How does one unrestrained person endanger buckled occupants inside the same car?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Crash forces hurl an unbuckled passenger across the cabin with lethal force against belted family or friends.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: Vehicles manufactured before what date fall under Montana seatbelt-law exceptions?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Classic cars built prior to January 1, 1968 predated universal federal seating-position belt mandates.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: What documentation must an occupant carry to use a medical seatbelt exemption?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Claiming a medical reason during a traffic stop fails unless you carry a doctor's written statement.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: Who is covered by the special-mobile-equipment seatbelt exemption?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Operators running qualifying special mobile rigs are exempted while operating inside their licensed equipment class.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: How does Montana define special mobile equipment regarding transport use and highway travel?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Machinery like road graders or trenchers works off-road primarily and crosses public highways only incidentally.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: Which agency can grant a seatbelt exemption to workers making frequent job-duty stops?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Delivery or route workers cannot self-exempt without securing formal approval from the Montana Department of Justice.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: Which form number applies to frequent-stop workers seeking a seatbelt exemption?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Route drivers apply on MVD-SE1 so state records verify authorized frequent-stop work duties.
sec04-card-r06.must_match_memory_hook: Apply using form MVD SE one

visual_sync.text_span: Apply using form MVD SE one

sec04-card-r07.question_text: Until what milestone should older children continue riding in a booster seat?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Moving out of a booster early lets adult straps ride dangerously across a child's neck and belly.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: Around what height does an adult lap-and-shoulder belt usually fit a child properly?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: Age alone misleads parents because belt geometry depends on torso and leg length around four feet nine.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: What restraint setup must be used if a child has no choice except riding in front with an airbag?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: Unboosted kids sitting forward in airbag seats face severe deployment trauma without proper restraint positioning.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: How should you position the front passenger seat when a child must ride ahead of an active airbag?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Maximizing distance from the dashboard keeps a child outside the explosive initial deployment zone.

sec04-card-r11.question_text: What is the absolute rule on placing a rear-facing child seat in front of an active airbag?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: An inflating front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant carrier directly over the baby's head.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: Where should restrained children younger than thirteen ride whenever possible?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: Back seats shield growing bodies from frontal dashboard intrusion and high-speed passenger airbag blasts.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: May two passengers share one seatbelt, or what does each rider require?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: Buckling two people inside one strap crushes them together violently under collision deceleration.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: What deadly crash hazard comes from holding a child in your arms while riding?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Collision forces multiply body weight so violently that no human arms can prevent crushing a child.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: Which road users do traffic signals direct at intersections and mid-block crosswalks, and how?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Clear signal phases prevent gridlock and guesswork where heavy pedestrian and vehicle streams cross paths.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: How must drivers treat a traffic signal that is dark or not working?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Blowing through a dead signal at street speed causes devastating broadside wrecks during power outages.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: When pedestrian signals are present, which display governs walkers, and what does WALK allow?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Dedicated walk heads time crossings around protected turn arrows that regular green balls do not reveal.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: How do walkers respond to steady or flashing DON'T WALK, and what do the hand and figure symbols mean?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: A flashing orange hand clears people already in the street while holding curb walkers back safely.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: Where must you stop on a steady red light, and when is a cautious right turn permitted?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Skipping the full halt before turning right on red is a classic citation and crosswalk-strike trigger.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: Under what exact street layout may a driver turn left on red, and what applies to walkers facing red?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Turning left on red across two-way traffic would cross live opposing lanes, so only one-way pairs qualify.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: What does a steady red arrow require, and what narrow exception applies?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Treating a red arrow carefully keeps you from turning across fast oncoming lanes unless red-turn rules fit.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: Which sign does a flashing red light match, and what four-step check follows?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: Cross traffic may hold a flashing yellow without stopping, so rolling a flashing red invites T-bone hits.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: When may a driver enter on a steady yellow light, and what rule applies to pedestrians facing yellow?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Gassing it to beat a yellow puts you into the box right as cross-street traffic launches.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: What does a steady yellow arrow signal about your protected turn phase?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Oncoming through lanes are seconds from getting green, so stragglers must clear or stop for the next phase.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: When may you turn left on a flashing yellow arrow, and who holds the green?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Opposing cars and crosswalk users have a green phase, so you wait for a genuinely safe gap.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: What does a flashing yellow traffic light tell an approaching driver to do?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Side-street cars stopping at flashing reds can misjudge your speed if you barrel through untouched.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: What hazard must drivers still watch for on a steady green light, and when may walkers cross?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Scanning left and right on a fresh green saves you from distracted drivers blowing stale reds.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: How does turning on a steady green arrow differ from turning on a plain green ball?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Confusing a round green ball for a green arrow sends left-turners straight into oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: How do a dark traffic light and flashing red compare with a flashing yellow display?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily under a flashing yellow risks rear-end hits while skipping a dead-light stop risks T-bones.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: May a pedestrian step off the curb on a green vehicle light while facing DON'T WALK?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: A green vehicle phase may pair with a protected turn arrow slicing straight across that crosswalk.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: How does Montana's rule for right turns on red differ from left turns on red?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Left on red only avoids crossing opposing traffic when both intersecting streets run one-way.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: How does a steady red arrow's rule compare with a flashing red light's procedure?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Flashing red releases any movement once clear, whereas a steady red arrow holds everything outside allowed red turns.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: What is the exact difference between a steady yellow arrow and a flashing yellow arrow?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Mixing them up makes drivers either linger as red hits or turn blindly into oncoming green traffic.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: How does cautious movement on a flashing yellow compare with proceeding on a steady green?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Neither display guarantees a hazard-free box, so defensive scanning stays active through both.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: Why is treating a plain green ball like a green arrow dangerous when turning?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: On a plain green ball, opposing cars and parallel walkers also hold green right through your turn path.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: What typical speed applies inside a roundabout, and what should you do on approach?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Low entry speeds let you merge smoothly into gaps without panic-braking at the yield line.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way at a roundabout entrance, and which direction does traffic circulate?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Looking left for counterclockwise traffic keeps you from pulling out or turning the wrong way.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Which side of the center island do you enter on, and what passing rule applies inside a single-lane roundabout?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Curved single-lane rings have zero room to overtake without sideswiping cars or mounting islands.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: What signal and pedestrian check are required when exiting a roundabout onto your chosen street?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Your right blinker tells waiting drivers you are leaving while your eyes protect exit crosswalks.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: Why must smaller cars drop back behind large trucks inside a roundabout?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Long trailers sweep across the raised inner apron and adjacent lane space, crushing cars beside them.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: Where must pedestrians cross at a roundabout, and which area is strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Cutting across the circulating lane to the center island puts walkers in drivers' blind spots.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: What two options does the Montana handbook give bicyclists navigating a roundabout?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Hugging the outer curb inside the circle invites right-hook collisions, so riders take the lane or walk.

sec06-card-f22.question_text: How should you respond to an approaching emergency vehicle inside versus before a roundabout?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Halting inside the narrow circular roadway corks the entire intersection and traps fire trucks behind you.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: Why must approaching drivers yield before entering a roundabout?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Keeping the inner ring flowing prevents internal gridlock that would freeze every entry leg.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: Once inside a single-lane roundabout, is passing or overtaking another vehicle ever allowed?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Tight curvature and sudden exits leave zero margin for squeezing past slower cars or cyclists.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: If sirens approach while you are already circulating in a roundabout, what is your exact move?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Clearing the ring gives emergency rigs the full width of the circle and truck apron.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: What four safety rules govern train races, doubt, far-side space, and shifting gears at railroad tracks?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Stalling mid-shift or getting trapped on rails by traffic ahead leaves zero escape from a locomotive.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: At least how far from the nearest rail must you stop when signals, gates, watchmen, or a close hazardous train require it?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: Locomotives overhang steel rails by several feet on each side, clipping bumpers parked too close.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: What four actions do advance railroad warning signs order before you reach the tracks?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Quiet rural crossings have no flashing bells, so rolling down windows and slowing early saves lives.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: What roadway feature do pavement markings with a stop line, a large X, and RR warn of?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: Painted lane stencils catch downward headlight beams even if brush or trucks hide roadside signs.

sec06-card-f27.question_text: Where do white crossbucks stand, and what extra sign appears when multiple tracks cross?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Knowing two or three tracks cross stops you from pulling out into a hidden second train.

sec06-card-f28.question_text: What must you do as soon as crossing lights flash, and what extra check applies on multiple tracks?
sec06-card-f28.teaching_text: A departing caboose on the near track can completely hide a fast freight train on the next.

sec06-card-f29.question_text: When do you stop at a gated crossing, and when is it legal to drive forward again?
sec06-card-f29.teaching_text: Driving around rising arms while red lights still flash risks meeting a second train on parallel rails.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: How do advance railroad warning signs differ in command from flashing crossing lights or lowered gates?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Stopping cold at every empty advance sign invites rear-end crashes, while running active lights is fatal.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: At a gated railroad crossing, why must you wait for both the gate to rise fully and the lights to stop flashing?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Relays keep red lights flashing if a second train enters the circuit just as gates start lifting.

sec06-card-f30.question_text: For what single maneuver may a driver cross a broken yellow centerline?
sec06-card-f30.teaching_text: Cruising left of a broken yellow outside an active pass puts you head-on with opposing traffic.

sec06-card-f31.question_text: What do a solid yellow line on your side and a double yellow bar, and when may a solid centerline be crossed?
sec06-card-f31.teaching_text: Solid yellow bans overtaking across blind zones while still letting residents turn left into driveways.

sec06-card-f32.question_text: How do white lane lines, yellow lane lines, and solid edge lines divide the roadway?
sec06-card-f32.teaching_text: Glancing at stripe color after dark instantly confirms whether the lane beside you flows your way.

sec06-card-f33.question_text: How does a dashed white lane line differ from a solid white lane line?
sec06-card-f33.teaching_text: Solid white lines stabilize turn bays and weave zones where abrupt lane swaps clip mirrors.

sec06-card-f34.question_text: Where must you halt for a required stop, and which crosswalks get pedestrian priority?
sec06-card-f34.teaching_text: Unmarked corner extensions hold the exact same pedestrian protections as bright painted zebra stripes.

sec06-card-f35.question_text: Compare passing rules for a dashed yellow, a solid-plus-dashed yellow pair, and double solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-f35.teaching_text: Sightlines open for one direction on hillcrests long before the opposing lane can see over the crest.

sec06-card-f36.question_text: Into which three destinations may you safely turn across a solid yellow line?
sec06-card-f36.teaching_text: Check mirrors for impatient overtakers and yield to oncoming cars before swinging left across yellow paint.

sec06-card-f37.question_text: How are reversible lanes marked on the pavement, and what must you check before entering one?
sec06-card-f37.teaching_text: Entering a rush-hour reversible lane at the wrong hour puts you head-on against commuter traffic.

sec06-card-f38.question_text: What do a green arrow, red X, flashing yellow X, and steady yellow X mean over a reversible lane?
sec06-card-f38.teaching_text: A steady yellow X warns the lane is about to flip direction, demanding a prompt safe exit.

sec06-card-f39.question_text: How are reserved lanes marked, and who may use transit or bicycle lanes?
sec06-card-f39.teaching_text: Driving a solo passenger car down a diamond bus or bike lane draws tickets and endangers cyclists.

sec06-card-f40.question_text: What controls eligibility for an HOV lane, and how many riders does an HOV 3 sign require?
sec06-card-f40.teaching_text: Posted occupancy counts apply during listed rush hours, and mannequins or pets never count as people.

sec06-card-f41.question_text: Which maneuvers may use a shared center lane, and how are its edges painted?
sec06-card-f41.teaching_text: Cruising down a center turn lane as a passing chute sets up head-on collisions with opposing turners.

sec06-card-f42.question_text: When a road has no lane signs or painted markings, what determines which lane you use?
sec06-card-f42.teaching_text: Snowpack or fresh chip-seal hides paint in Montana, so standard right-side and turn-edge rules take over.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: How does line color alone tell you whether adjacent lanes move with you or toward you?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Spotting white on your left proves you are on a one-way or divided road immediately.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: How does a solid-plus-dashed yellow pair differ from two solid yellow lines?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Crossing when the solid stripe hugs your side puts you blind into a hillcrest or curve.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: What is the functional difference between a painted stop line and a crosswalk?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Stopping behind the thick bar keeps your front bumper completely clear of the pedestrian corridor.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: How does a reserved lane differ in purpose from a reversible lane?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: One filters who may enter by vehicle class, while the other switches flow direction by clock.

sec06-card-r17.question_text: How does a shared center lane's job differ from a reversible lane's job?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Mistaking a two-way turn lane for a commuter through lane guarantees nose-to-nose standoffs.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: Over a reversible lane, how does a flashing yellow X differ from a steady yellow X?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: Flashing yellow X lets you finish a left turn, while steady yellow X warns oncoming flow starts next.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: What three core habits open the Montana handbook's general driving advice before pulling into traffic?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Pulling from a curb only when lanes are truly clear prevents sudden braking cascades behind you.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: What check precedes backing a parked car, and what must you never do in a live travel lane?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Stopping or backing up on an active roadway invites high-speed rear-end crashes before trailing cars react.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: Which four sources of traffic authority form the Montana handbook's first rule of the road?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Live human direction from an officer or flagger overrides routine signs during crashes or roadwork.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: How many feet ahead must you signal a turn in town compared with on a rural Montana road?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Higher rural highway speeds cover one hundred feet in barely a second, demanding triple the warning distance.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: On a road with three or more lanes moving your way, where do you cruise, and when helps the center lane?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Holding the middle lane past busy on-ramps opens the right lane for merging traffic while leaving left open.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: What is the safe recovery sequence if you forget to signal or miss your intended turn?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Whip-turning at the last second without a blinker blindsides cyclists and trailing cars instantly.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: When is driving on the shoulder permitted in Montana?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Shoulders hold broken-down rigs, road debris, and cyclists rather than extra passing or turn lanes.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: How do bad road surfaces or stormy weather affect driving at the posted speed limit?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Posted numbers assume dry summer traction, so snowpack, rain, or gravel require slower speeds.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: What day-and-night interstate speed limits apply to cars and light trucks versus heavy trucks in Montana?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: Loaded semis need far longer braking distances, explaining the ten-to-fifteen-mile speed differential on interstates.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: What speed limit applies day and night across vehicle classes on urban highways near Billings, Great Falls, and Missoula?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Frequent interchanges and commuter merges around Montana's biggest cities require a uniform sixty-five ceiling.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: What day and night limits apply on Montana two-lane highways for cars and light trucks versus heavy trucks?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Unlit rural two-lanes drop five miles per hour after dark because wildlife and curves appear closer.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: By how much may a driver on a two-lane road briefly exceed the limit while overtaking and returning right?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: Minimizing time spent in the oncoming lane cuts exposure on rural two-lane passes before easing back down.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: Which lane or side do you use for normal safe passing on two-lane versus multi-lane roads?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Drivers expect overtakers on their left mirror side, keeping lane discipline predictable at highway pace.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: In which two situations is passing on the right legal, and where is it strictly forbidden?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Dropping tires onto gravel or paved shoulders to squeeze right kicks debris and hits stopped cars.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: When no turn signs or arrows control an intersection, which entry and exit lanes must you use?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Drifting across lanes mid-turn sideswipes opposing turners lawfully entering their own curb lane.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: Which two wide-arc mistakes must you avoid when making a right turn?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Swinging left first baits cars behind you to pass right, and swinging out wide enters oncoming lanes.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: What path error must a left-turning driver avoid while leaving space for oncoming left-turners?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Slicing early across the cross-street centerline clips cars stopped at the crossroad stop bar.

sec07-card-f18.question_text: What sight distance and traffic condition are required before turning around, and where is it banned?
sec07-card-f18.teaching_text: Cresting pickups cover five hundred feet in seconds, turning blind hillcrest U-turns into broadside traps.

sec07-card-f19.question_text: Which two basic conditions must be met before executing any turn?
sec07-card-f19.teaching_text: Cutting across from an improper lane at the last moment causes intersection sideswipes.

sec07-card-f20.question_text: Does Montana law grant anyone absolute right-of-way, or what duty applies to every driver?
sec07-card-f20.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn when someone else blunders still puts both cars in the body shop.

sec07-card-f21.question_text: What special priority do blind pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog hold, and what horn rule applies?
sec07-card-f21.teaching_text: A horn blast masks directional traffic sounds a visually impaired walker uses to stay oriented.

sec07-card-f22.question_text: How does driver crosswalk yielding balance with a pedestrian's duty at the curb?
sec07-card-f22.teaching_text: Even alert drivers need physical stopping footage and cannot halt instantly when someone leaps off a curb.

sec07-card-f23.question_text: What visibility gear helps night walkers, and when is walking on the roadway unlawful?
sec07-card-f23.teaching_text: Dark jackets vanish outside low-beam patterns until a driver is barely two seconds away.

sec07-card-f24.question_text: Where sidewalks are absent, which side of the road do walkers use, and how should they cross?
sec07-card-f24.teaching_text: Facing oncoming headlights lets a pedestrian see drifting cars and step clear onto the verge.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: How does normal two-lane passing compare with the narrow situations allowing a right-side pass?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Keeping right-side overtakes strictly on pavement prevents deadly shoulder drop-offs and intersection traps.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: If another road user fails to yield as required, what crash-avoidance duty remains on you?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Defensive braking beats winning a legal argument after an avoidable intersection wreck.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: Pair Montana's town and rural turn-signal distances with the rule on shoulder driving?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Signaling early inside the legal travel lane keeps trailing traffic informed without misusing breakdown shoulders.

sec07-card-f25.question_text: Who yields when a car crosses a sidewalk at an alley, lot, or driveway, and when may cars use sidewalks?
sec07-card-f25.teaching_text: Joggers and strollers move fast along storefronts where building walls hide emerging hoods.

sec07-card-f26.question_text: To whom must a left-turning driver yield, and to whom must a roundabout entrant yield?
sec07-card-f26.teaching_text: Both maneuvers cross an established traffic stream that already owns the path ahead.

sec07-card-f27.question_text: Who gets priority at an uncontrolled intersection, and how should your foot and eyes prepare?
sec07-card-f27.teaching_text: Hovering your foot over the brake pedal shaves precious reaction footage at blind neighborhood corners.

sec07-card-f28.question_text: Who proceeds first at a four-way stop, and what rule governs pulling onto a main road from a driveway?
sec07-card-f28.teaching_text: Driveway aprons and unpaved roadside pull-outs hold zero priority against fast-moving mainline traffic.

sec07-card-f29.question_text: When must you hold back from entering an intersection, and what does a yield sign order?
sec07-card-f29.teaching_text: Stopping mid-box when traffic backs up traps you broadside when cross-street lights turn green.

sec07-card-f30.question_text: Summarize the lane, stop, and street requirements for right on red and left on red?
sec07-card-f30.teaching_text: Checking for No Turn On Red plaques after halting keeps curb-lane turns ticket-free.

sec07-card-f31.question_text: When a pedestrian is in the crosswalk, when may a stopped driver complete a right turn?
sec07-card-f31.teaching_text: Waiting until walkers reach the far half prevents cutting inches ahead of or behind someone mid-stride.

sec07-card-f32.question_text: What is strictly forbidden when a vehicle ahead of you stops at a crosswalk for a pedestrian?
sec07-card-f32.teaching_text: Whip-changing lanes around a stopped SUV strikes the hidden pedestrian stepping out in front of its hood.

sec07-card-f33.question_text: What duty falls on an overtaking driver if the vehicle being passed slows down or stops?
sec07-card-f33.teaching_text: That slowing car ahead may be halting for a deer, child, or left-turning vehicle hidden from you.

sec07-card-f34.question_text: What three steps are required when an emergency vehicle approaches running lights and siren?
sec07-card-f34.teaching_text: Pulling back out too soon risks colliding with a second trailing ambulance or police cruiser.
sec07-card-f34.must_match_memory_hook: Pull far right, obey PA, hold

visual_sync.text_span: Pull far right, obey PA, hold

sec07-card-f35.question_text: How far must traffic in both directions stop from a red-flashing school bus, and how do you treat yellow flashes?
sec07-card-f35.teaching_text: Thirty feet leaves a wide safety corridor in front of and behind the bus where kids cross.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: How does priority at an uncontrolled crossroad differ from priority at a four-way stop?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Uncontrolled corners have no stop signs to rank arrival order, so yielding right breaks ties immediately.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: Combine the right-turn rule for a stopped lead car with the passing ban on trailing drivers at a crosswalk?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Keeping both lanes patient around crosswalks eliminates the deadly multi-lane screen-out crash.

sec07-card-f36.question_text: What speed habit and visual scan apply near schools during both daytime and nighttime hours?
sec07-card-f36.teaching_text: Evening concerts, gyms, and playgrounds bring families across school streets long after classes dismiss.

sec07-card-f37.question_text: How does the Montana handbook define a legal funeral procession?
sec07-card-f37.teaching_text: Recognizing the lead, escort, and daylight formation alerts you that special procession right-of-way applies.

sec07-card-f38.question_text: Which four actions are prohibited for outside motorists encountering a funeral procession?
sec07-card-f38.teaching_text: Cutting through closely spaced mourners causes chain-reaction fender-benders inside an escorted column.

sec07-card-f39.question_text: How do intersection traffic controls apply differently to a funeral lead car versus following cars?
sec07-card-f39.teaching_text: Allowing escorted followers through keeps the cortege intact while still requiring care at cross streets.

sec07-card-f40.question_text: What spacing, highway speed cap, and lighting rules govern drivers inside a funeral procession?
sec07-card-f40.teaching_text: Headlights on every car plus hazard flashers on lead and tail units mark the column boundaries clearly.

sec07-card-f41.question_text: Must drivers inside a funeral procession still yield to signaled emergency vehicles?
sec07-card-f41.teaching_text: Life-or-death ambulance and fire calls always outrank funeral cortege privileges on public roads.

sec07-card-f42.question_text: How does Montana traffic law classify bicycles, and how should drivers adjust around them?
sec07-card-f42.teaching_text: Closing on a fifteen-mile-per-hour rider at seventy happens four times faster than closing on a car.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: How much clearance does Montana recommend when passing a cyclist, and what if oncoming traffic blocks you?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Mirror windblast from a close high-speed pass can suck a lightweight road bike off balance.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: Where should you expect touring cyclists to ride, and what do single-file groups require when passing?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Rumble strips and glass force riders into the lane, and a string of riders takes longer to clear.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: Why do cyclists often ride eighteen to twenty-four inches inside the lane edge?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: Claiming two feet of pavement margin gives escape room from gravel drop-offs and signals drivers to change lanes.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: What do shared-lane arrow markings guide and warn, and how do they differ from bike-lane symbols?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Sharrows mark lanes too narrow for side-by-side sharing, reminding drivers to pass in another lane.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: What four duties do motorists owe cyclists regarding rights, blocking, passing, and designated bike lanes?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Cutting across a painted bike lane for a right turn without yielding causes classic right-hook crashes.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: When do cyclists ride single file, and in which four settings is riding two abreast allowed?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Knowing riders may pair up on wide shoulders or paths prevents angry honking at legal group rides.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: List the four situations when a slower cyclist may leave the right edge of the lane?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Swinging left past parked cars keeps a rider from getting slammed by a suddenly opened driver door.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: Because most bicycles lack rearview mirrors, what should a driver assume when approaching from behind?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Wind noise masks tire hum, so an unmirrored rider may swerve around a pothole unexpectedly.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: Where are school bus stopping duties at railroad crossings established according to the Montana handbook?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Expect school buses ahead of you to make statutory stops at rail crossings even without flashing gates.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: Contrast how intersection signals bind the funeral lead vehicle versus the following vehicles?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Even with procession right-of-way, followers still watch for cross drivers who miss the cortege lights.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: Contrast how procession cars space themselves with what outside drivers are barred from doing?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Tight procession gaps signal outsiders not to wedge in or tag along to jump red lights.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: Before turning right across a cyclist's lane, what must you confirm first, and why?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: Even though cyclists should overtake on the left, many keep riding straight along the right curb.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: How do daytime lighting rules for bicycles differ from motorcycles, and why does that matter?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Scanning only for bright motorcycle headlights makes narrow unlit bicycle silhouettes disappear in tree shadows.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: Why must motorists use extra caution whenever children ride bicycles nearby?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Young riders frequently wobble or swerve across neighborhood streets without knowing right-of-way rules.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: Which three aggressive behaviors around cyclists must drivers avoid because they can trigger a crash?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: A sudden horn blast or close swerve startles a rider into jerking handlebars straight onto pavement.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: What front headlight color and visibility distance must a bicycle carry at night?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: A five-hundred-foot white beam lets cross-street and oncoming drivers spot an approaching bike before turning.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: At night, is a five-hundred-foot rear red bicycle light mandatory or optional alongside rear reflectors?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: Knowing only reflectors are required explains why dark bikes wait for your headlights to bounce back.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: What side-visibility equipment must both bicycle wheels carry for night riding?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Rim-mounted reflectors spinning across dark intersections catch side-street headlights before a car pulls out.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: How strong must a bicycle's brakes be on dry, flat, clean pavement?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Weak rim pads that cannot lock a tire on clean dry asphalt fail emergency urban stops.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: What tall high-visibility accessory does the Montana handbook encourage cyclists to mount for rear visibility?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: Rising six feet above asphalt lets drivers spot a low recumbent or child's bike over hoods.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: While treating bicycles as vehicles, which five trouble spots demand special driver scanning?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: Kids darting out from between parked SUVs give zero advance notice unless you scan curb gaps.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: What two basic placement and visibility standards must every parked vehicle meet?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: Leaving a fender over the fog line on a blind bend invites a high-speed rear clip.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: Where should you park when markings exist, and how do you secure the brake and transmission?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Combining the parking brake with park or gear prevents runaway rollaways if a pawl slips.

sec08-card-f13.question_text: What three door habits protect you and passing traffic after parking along a street?
sec08-card-f13.teaching_text: Stepping out on the sidewalk side eliminates dooring cyclists and keeps you out of live lanes.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: What two anti-theft steps apply every time you walk away from a parked vehicle?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Even a sixty-second coffee run with keys inside invites opportunistic theft and uninsured crash liability.

sec08-card-f15.question_text: Where relative to moving traffic and the curb or shoulder edge should you position a roadway park?
sec08-card-f15.teaching_text: Tucking tight to the curb or outer shoulder edge maximizes clearance from mirrors and snowplows.

sec08-card-f16.question_text: Within how many inches of the curb or outer shoulder edge must a parked vehicle sit?
sec08-card-f16.teaching_text: Parking two feet out pinches the travel lane and forces passing cars across the centerline.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: Compare Montana's nighttime requirement for a front white bicycle light against a rear red light?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Every night cyclist needs a headlight plus rear reflector, while an active red taillight adds bonus punch.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: Where do bicycle spoke reflectors mount, and which colors belong on the front versus rear wheel?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Color-coded rim arcs tell cross-street drivers which direction a bicycle is rolling in the dark.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: Pair a driver's right-turn duty across a cyclist with which side cyclists should use to pass motorists?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and blind spots catches riders who ignore the left-pass rule and sneak up curbside.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: Why do bicyclists younger than fifteen require extra driver margin on Montana streets?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Without permit study or formal bike training, kids under fifteen miss subtle right-of-way cues.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: Combine Montana's lane-clearance and visibility parking rule with proper roadway edge placement?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Pulling fully off live pavement onto the outer edge keeps stopped cars safe day and night.

sec08-card-f17.question_text: What lights and headlight setting are required when parking on a roadway or shoulder at night?
sec08-card-f17.teaching_text: Bright high beams on a parked shoulder car blind oncoming drivers and disguise which side is open.

sec08-card-f18.question_text: What signal and visual checks are required when leaving a parking space, especially in reverse?
sec08-card-f18.teaching_text: Low-slung bikes and toddlers sit below rear window sills where single quick glances miss them.

sec08-card-f19.question_text: How do you signal and line up beside the forward car to start parallel parking?
sec08-card-f19.teaching_text: Pulling closer than two feet risks clipping the parked car's mirror as your nose swings out.

sec08-card-f20.question_text: Describe the steering sequence once you reverse to the lead car's front door while parallel parking?
sec08-card-f20.teaching_text: Hitting that forty-five-degree angle aims your rear tire neatly toward the curb without hopping over it.

sec08-card-f21.question_text: Which way do you turn front wheels when parking downhill, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec08-card-f21.teaching_text: Only uphill beside a raised curb turns wheels left so the back of the front tire catches.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: During hours of darkness, what visibility distance and beam rule govern cars parked on shoulders?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Marker lamps keep dark rural highway shoulders readable without dazzling approaching drivers overnight.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: Why must backing out of a parking stall add a double-check beyond signaling and scanning traffic?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Pedestrians pushing carts and fast cyclists cross right behind bumpers after your initial glance.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: Compare wheel direction for downhill parking, uphill with a curb, and uphill without a curb?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Without a concrete curb to chock the tire, turning left uphill would roll straight across traffic.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: Put the parallel-parking alignment, right cut, and left swing into one connected sequence?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Nailing the initial two-foot gap makes the forty-five-degree entry repeatable on road-test day.

sec08-card-f22.question_text: What stopping rules apply at white, yellow, and red painted curbs in Montana?
sec08-card-f22.teaching_text: Stopping even briefly with hazards on along a red fire curb risks an immediate ticket.

sec08-card-f23.question_text: Where around an intersection and its crosswalk or sidewalk is parking prohibited?
sec08-card-f23.teaching_text: Parking closer than twenty feet screens pedestrians stepping off corners from turning vehicles.

sec08-card-f24.question_text: How does construction blockage affect parking, and how far must you park from traffic controls?
sec08-card-f24.teaching_text: Thirty feet keeps tall pickups from hiding stop signs, yield triangles, and signal heads.

sec08-card-f25.question_text: How many feet must a parked car stay clear of a fire hydrant versus a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-f25.teaching_text: Fire crews need fifteen feet to couple stiff supply hoses, and trains need wide sightlines.

sec08-card-f26.question_text: Pair the eighteen-inch curb limit with fire-station driveway clearances on both sides of the street?
sec08-card-f26.teaching_text: Long ladder rigs need seventy-five feet across the street to swing their wide turning radius.

sec08-card-f27.question_text: Which four property or sidewalk access features must a parked car never block?
sec08-card-f27.teaching_text: Blocking a sloped sidewalk ramp traps wheelchair users in the street with nowhere to climb.

sec08-card-f28.question_text: On or inside which four elevated or enclosed roadway structures is parking banned?
sec08-card-f28.teaching_text: Bridges and tunnels lack breakdown shoulders, turning any parked car into a bottleneck hazard.

sec08-card-f29.question_text: Which three dangerous roadway positions are outlawed alongside curb parking?
sec08-card-f29.teaching_text: Pulling nose-in against traffic to grab a left-curb spot crosses live oncoming lanes blind.

sec08-card-f30.question_text: What rule governs no-parking signs and marked accessible spaces without a valid permit?
sec08-card-f30.teaching_text: Borrowing an accessible stall even for two minutes strand-locks drivers who need ramp clearance.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: Contrast what white, yellow, and red curbs allow or forbid in one quick summary?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Leaving your driver seat at a yellow loading curb turns an attended load into a ticket.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: Rank the required parking clearances for hydrants, crosswalks, signals or signs, and rail crossings?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Stepping up fifteen-twenty-thirty-fifty locks all four classic Montana test distances in memory.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: How does same-side fire-station driveway clearance compare with opposite-side clearance?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Opposite curbs need nearly four times the gap so heavy engines can swing out wide.

sec08-card-f31.question_text: Which vehicle class is exempt from mandatory liability insurance, and what are Montana's three dollar minimums?
sec08-card-f31.teaching_text: 25-50-10 covers one injured person, total crash injuries, and damaged property of others.

sec08-card-f32.question_text: Where must insurance evidence stay at all times, and when must you show it to officers?
sec08-card-f32.teaching_text: Leaving your insurance card on the kitchen counter still draws a citation at a traffic stop.

sec08-card-f33.question_text: What fine range, jail cap, and point penalty hit a first misdemeanor uninsured-driving offense?
sec08-card-f33.teaching_text: Five driver-record points plus misdemeanor court fines cost far more than monthly liability coverage.

sec08-card-f34.question_text: What minimum fine, jail cap, and plate-registration suspension lengths hit second and third uninsured offenses?
sec08-card-f34.teaching_text: Losing your license plates and registration parks the vehicle completely for three to six months.

sec08-card-f35.question_text: What happens if you are responsible for a crash and fail to pay damages within sixty days?
sec08-card-f35.teaching_text: Driving uninsured into a wreck freezes both your license and registration for up to six years.

sec08-card-f36.question_text: How many Montana-registered vehicles must an owner hold to qualify as a self-insurer?
sec08-card-f36.teaching_text: Only sizable commercial or fleet owners over twenty-five vehicles can prove reserves to self-insure.

sec08-card-f37.question_text: How does Montana's financial-responsibility law treat non-resident drivers who lack adequate coverage?
sec08-card-f37.teaching_text: State lines will not shield an uninsured visitor because Montana reports suspensions home.

sec08-card-f38.question_text: What two records does Montana's insurance verification system match, and who can check it live?
sec08-card-f38.teaching_text: Real-time database matching catches lapsed policies during plate lookups before a stop even begins.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: Pair how minimum liability coverage divides with where proof of insurance must stay?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Having an active policy only spares roadside hassle when proof rides inside the glovebox or phone.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: What extra penalty hits repeat uninsured drivers beyond the fines, jail, and points of a first offense?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: First-timers keep their tags after paying up, while repeat offenders lose plates and registration.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: Contrast who qualifies for Montana self-insurance with how non-residents meet responsibility rules?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: Everyday visitors rely on compliant policies from insurers or lose Montana driving privileges.

sec08-card-r16.question_text: Contrast the purpose of sixty-day crash-nonpayment suspension with the insurance verification system?
sec08-card-r16.teaching_text: One enforces unpaid crash debts afterward while the live system spots coverage gaps anytime.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: What three elements beyond reading a manual build safe driving skill?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: Memorizing rules on paper never replaces real seat time, coaching, and disciplined judgment in live traffic.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: What three losses define driver distraction, and what share of driving decisions relies on vision?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Because nine out of ten driving choices depend on sight, losing visual, manual, or mental focus courts disaster.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: How do quick glances at phones, food, passengers, controls, or drowsiness affect crash risk?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Reaching for fries, playlists, or navigation steals critical split seconds needed when traffic brakes unexpectedly ahead.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: Why does Montana single out texting as the worst driving distraction?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Typing a message pulls fingers off steering, eyes off pavement, and attention off hazards simultaneously.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: How many seconds do eyes leave the road per text, and what 55 mph distance does it match?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Glancing down five seconds at highway pace carries your car three hundred plus feet completely blind.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: What is human multitasking behind the wheel in reality, and who faces the added danger?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Your brain toggles rapidly between tasks rather than handling both, putting nearby drivers and walkers at risk.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: What three phone-free habits apply to you as both a driver and a passenger?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: Passengers who call out distracted texting in the moment protect everyone sharing the cabin and street.

sec09-card-f08.question_text: How do most Montana cities treat phone use behind the wheel, and how should calls or texts be handled?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Local municipal ordinances ticket rolling phone use, so park safely off the street before touching your screen.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: What four baseline safety commitments keep focus and protection intact on every drive?
sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Stacking attentive sight, two-hand control, buckled riders, and zero alcohol eliminates the deadliest crash factors.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: Why is texting singled out above other distractions as the most alarming?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: Few other cabin habits hijack sight, steering grip, and mental processing at the exact same instant.

sec09-card-f10.question_text: How should your brake, gear selector, and clutch be set when starting a manual or automatic car?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Holding the brake with automatics in park or manuals out of gear prevents unexpected lurching on ignition.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: Why should you accelerate gently from a stop, and how should manual transmissions be shifted?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Mashing the gas breaks tire traction into a slide, while rough manual shifts either rev high or stall.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: Where on the steering wheel should your hands grip when driving a car with a wheel airbag?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Balanced side grips keep forearms clear of an inflating center airbag while maximizing emergency steering leverage.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: Why should your eyes aim far down the roadway while steering?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Staring right off your front hood causes jerky corrections instead of smooth, early lane placement.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: What steering technique applies through corners and when straightening out afterward?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: One-hand palming or letting a spinning rim slide loose through your fingers risks overshooting your target lane.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: Which pedal setting is shared when starting both automatic and manual vehicles?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: Whether shifting from park or pressing a clutch in neutral, keeping the brake set anchors the car.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: Why must you check the speedometer often, especially right after leaving a fast highway?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: After miles at seventy, forty-five feels deceptively slow on town streets unless you verify instrument speed.

sec09-card-f16.question_text: How should you adjust speed relative to posted limits when pavement or weather deteriorates?
sec09-card-f16.teaching_text: Posted signs set fair-weather maximums rather than safe targets on slick, snowy, or rutted surfaces.

sec09-card-f17.question_text: Which three hazards come from slamming the brakes late instead of anticipating stops?
sec09-card-f17.teaching_text: Panic braking locks tires into a skid while catching trailing motorists with zero room to stop.

sec09-card-f18.question_text: How can easing off the gas or changing lanes early improve stopping situations?
sec09-card-f18.teaching_text: Lifting off the accelerator ahead of red lights often lets signals turn green before you ever halt.

sec09-card-f19.question_text: Because missed sights top crash causes, where should you scan and when should headlights assist?
sec09-card-f19.teaching_text: Continuous front, side, and mirror checks paired with low-light headlamps expose hazards before space runs out.

sec09-card-f20.question_text: What should you do whenever reading a map or task demands more than a brief glance?
sec09-card-f20.teaching_text: Looking away longer than a couple seconds turns highway travel into guesswork until you park safely.

sec09-card-f21.question_text: Why should you skip even hands-free calls in motion and never wear headphones or earbuds while driving?
sec09-card-f21.teaching_text: Conversations divide mental focus while earbuds muffle approaching ambulance sirens, train horns, and warning honks.

sec09-card-f22.question_text: How should you drive past a roadside crash or patrol stop?
sec09-card-f22.teaching_text: Slowing to stare at flashing lights triggers secondary chain-reaction rear-enders right beside emergency crews.

sec09-card-f23.question_text: What four things does active scanning ahead, beside, and behind help you catch early?
sec09-card-f23.teaching_text: Reading directional and warning signs early keeps you from making last-second swerves across occupied lanes.

sec09-card-f24.question_text: How many seconds ahead should you scan, and what three driving benefits follow?
sec09-card-f24.teaching_text: Looking ten seconds downrange smooths steering, trims wasted braking fuel, and steadies traffic flow.

sec09-card-f25.question_text: How far in distance does a ten-second look-ahead reach in town compared with open highways?
sec09-card-f25.teaching_text: Higher highway speeds stretch ten seconds from a single city block out to roughly four blocks.

sec09-card-f26.question_text: Why must your eyes keep sweeping to both sides, especially near intersections and rail tracks?
sec09-card-f26.teaching_text: Cross traffic, cyclists, and trains enter from peripheral angles that tunnel-vision drivers miss completely.

sec09-card-f27.question_text: What counts as an intersection, and where must you look before entering or pulling out?
sec09-card-f27.teaching_text: Every merge, alley, or cross street demands a left-right-across sweep before your bumper enters conflict space.

sec09-card-f28.question_text: What three checks belong before turning left across oncoming traffic, and when is one-way left on red legal?
sec09-card-f28.teaching_text: A surprise pedestrian blocking the crosswalk can trap your car sideways across oncoming lanes mid-turn.

sec09-card-f29.question_text: What conflicts and walkers must you check before turning right, and when is right on red allowed?
sec09-card-f29.teaching_text: Drivers staring only left for traffic gaps often miss oncoming left-turners or pedestrians stepping off curbs.

sec09-card-f30.question_text: Why is scanning cross traffic vital right after your traffic light turns green?
sec09-card-f30.teaching_text: Impatient cross-street drivers trying to beat yellow lights enter intersections right as opposing signals turn green.

sec09-card-f31.question_text: How should you proceed from a stop when parked cars, hedges, or buildings hide cross-street traffic?
sec09-card-f31.teaching_text: Inching out gradually lets cross-street drivers see your front bumper early enough to warn or slow.

sec09-card-f32.question_text: Why must you scan road edges closely near storefronts, parking lots, work zones, playgrounds, and schools?
sec09-card-f32.teaching_text: Backed-out bumpers, distracted shoppers, and darting kids emerge abruptly wherever activity lines the curb.

sec09-card-f33.question_text: Why must you wait after a train passes on multi-track railroad crossings?
sec09-card-f33.teaching_text: Pulling onto double tracks right behind a clearing freight car blindsides drivers with an opposite-direction locomotive.

sec09-card-f34.question_text: During which five driving situations is checking mirrors behind you especially critical?
sec09-card-f34.teaching_text: Knowing whether a heavy truck or tailgater sits behind shapes how safely you brake, shift lanes, or descend.

sec09-card-f35.question_text: What space must you confirm is clear before changing lanes, merging, or pulling out from a curb?
sec09-card-f35.teaching_text: Checking beside alone misses fast-closing vehicles overtaking quickly from farther back in the target lane.

sec09-card-f36.question_text: In what order do you signal, use mirrors, and check blind spots for a lane change?
sec09-card-f36.teaching_text: Mirrors miss cars tucked alongside your rear quarter panel unless you turn your head over your shoulder.

sec09-card-f37.question_text: How long should blind-spot glances take, and what should you recheck right before steering over?
sec09-card-f37.teaching_text: Staring backward too long lets traffic ahead brake unnoticed right as you drift sideways.

sec09-card-f38.question_text: Why scan the far lane and curb edges for bikes, motorcycles, and walkers during a lane change?
sec09-card-f38.teaching_text: On three-lane streets two outer cars often drift toward the same center gap simultaneously.

sec09-card-f39.question_text: When is checking your rearview mirror during a slowdown most urgent?
sec09-card-f39.teaching_text: Spotting a distracted follower early lets you tap brake lights or leave escape room ahead.

sec09-card-f40.question_text: What three steps belong before pulling out from a curb into traffic?
sec09-card-f40.teaching_text: Side mirrors flatten speed perception, making a direct left-shoulder check vital before entering live lanes.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: How do you measure your look-ahead interval in seconds using a roadside object?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: Counting one-thousand-one up to a signpost ahead reveals instantly whether your scan reaches ten full seconds.

sec09-card-r02.question_text: How do early speed or lane adjustments benefit drivers behind you?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Smooth early inputs prevent accordion shockwaves that cause chain-reaction collisions several cars back.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: What distinct roles do your speedometer and posted speed signs play?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Speedometers reveal true pace while posted numbers set only the ideal-weather ceiling that storms push lower.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: Why does a plain green light never excuse skipping your left-and-right intersection scan?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Right-of-way on paper never stops steel when a distracted cross-street driver blows past red.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: What do mirrors clear versus what only an over-the-shoulder glance clears?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Skipping the physical head turn leaves a car-sized blind zone hidden right beside your rear fender.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: Why does ten seconds equal one city block in town yet four blocks or a quarter mile on highways?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: Doubling or tripling road speed multiplies the ground covered inside the exact same ten-second scan window.

sec09-card-r15.question_text: Aside from allowed one-way-to-one-way lefts, what two conditions govern turning left across oncoming traffic?
sec09-card-r15.teaching_text: Both oncoming lanes and the receiving crosswalk must be open before committing across opposing traffic.

sec09-card-r16.question_text: How do headphones worsen risk beyond the mental distraction already caused by hands-free calling?
sec09-card-r16.teaching_text: Phone talk splits brainpower, whereas covering your ears cuts off emergency sirens and warning horns.

sec09-card-f41.question_text: Because vision drops at night while still guiding ninety percent of decisions, what must you do with speed?
sec09-card-f41.teaching_text: Driving daytime speeds into shortened night sightlines leaves too little pavement to stop for dark hazards.

sec09-card-f42.question_text: During what night hours and what visibility distance must headlights be turned on?
sec09-card-f42.teaching_text: Any fog, snow, or twilight hiding people inside five hundred feet triggers full headlight law.

sec09-card-f43.question_text: What reach distances apply to upper and lower beams, and at what oncoming and following distances must you dim?
sec09-card-f43.teaching_text: Pairing proper high-beam reach with timely dimming protects your sight without blinding highway traffic.

sec09-card-f44.question_text: Where should you look when meeting bright oncoming lights at night, and what if another driver flashes you?
sec09-card-f44.teaching_text: Tracking the white fog line preserves night-adapted pupils while checking your switch stops unintentional high-beam glare.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: How can parking choice cut down reversing, and what should you check before climbing inside?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and low toys sit completely below rear window sightlines once you sit in the seat.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: How should you position your body and eyes while backing up, and what outside help helps?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Relying on mirrors or cameras alone leaves wide rear corner blind zones that turning backward exposes.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: What rules govern driving on parking lights, using spotlights near traffic, and driving at dusk or overcast?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Parking lamps mark stationary cars only, so dusk or grey skies call for full low-beam headlights.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: How much night vision can tinted or photo-gray lenses steal after sunset?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Cutting nearly a third of scarce nighttime light hides dark-clothed walkers and deer along unlit shoulders.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: In what order should you slow, steer, park, and set lights during a nighttime tire failure or breakdown?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: Yanking off pavement before stabilizing speed rolls cars in soft shoulders, and dimmed lights prevent blinding traffic.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: How often should you take breaks on long night drives, and what must you do if drowsy?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: Cold air or loud music cannot stop microsleeps once real drowsiness sets in late at night.
